dervis-irab:35-37.t:
* I'rab:
(يا بَنِي آدَمَ) Its i'rab has been given many times before. (إِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ) The speech is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), introduced to set out the matter of sending messengers. إنْ is conditional, assimilated into the redundant (zāʾida) «ما» which reinforces the conditional meaning; for that reason its verb must take the heavy or the light nūn of emphasis. يأتينكم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; رسل is the fāʿil (agent); منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of رسل. Making the messengers from among them cuts off the argument more decisively and leaves less room for excuse. (يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي) The clause is also an adjective of رسل; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقصون; آياتي is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (فَمَنِ اتَّقى وَأَصْلَحَ فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) This conditional sentence is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the preceding condition; the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); مَن is a conditional noun and mubtadaʾ (subject); the fāʾ in His words فلا خوف is connective; the i'rab of what follows has been given many times before. (وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا عَنْها أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; الذين is a relative noun and mubtadaʾ; the clause كذبوا بآياتنا is the ṣila (relative clause); استكبروا عنها is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and أصحاب النار its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of الذين, the linking element being the demonstrative, as mentioned before; هم is a mubtadaʾ, and فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar «خالدون»; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a second khabar of الذين. (فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِآياتِهِ) The fāʾ is resumptive; مَن is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, i.e. no one is more unjust; أظلم is the khabar of «من»; ممن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أظلم; the clause افترى has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to افترى; كذبا is a mafʿūl bihi, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause كذب بآياته is conjoined to the clause افترى. (أُولئِكَ يَنالُهُمْ نَصِيبُهُمْ مِنَ الْكِتابِ) The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; the clause ينالهم is the khabar; نصيبهم is the fāʿil of ينالهم; من الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (حَتَّى إِذا جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنا يَتَوَفَّوْنَهُمْ) حتى is a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition, or an inceptive particle (ibtidāʾiyya); discussion of this expression has been given before, so refresh your memory of it. إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause جاءتهم رسلنا is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause يتوفونهم is a ḥāl of رسلنا, i.e. taking them in death. (قالُوا أَيْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ) The clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivizing condition; أين is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ما is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ; the interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech); the clause كنتم is the ṣila of the relative; the tāʾ is the noun (ism) of kāna and the clause تدعون its khabar; من دون الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, or attached to تدعون. (قالُوا ضَلُّوا عَنَّا وَشَهِدُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا كافِرِينَ) The clause is the answer to an implied question, as though it had been said: What did your objects of worship do, and those whom you used to call upon? So they answered that they had strayed away. The clause ضلوا is maqūl al-qawl; the clause شهدوا is conjoined to the clause قالوا, or is resumptive; على أنفسهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شهدوا; أنّ and what falls within its scope are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to شهدوا; the clause كانوا كافرين is the khabar of «أنّ».

* Vocabulary:
(ادَّارَكُوا): i.e. تداركوا, meaning they followed one another into the Fire. Its origin is تداركوا: the tāʾ was turned into a dāl, made quiescent and assimilated into the dāl, and then the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was brought in. How this happens will be explained in the Benefits section.
[Translator's note: this Vocabulary section belongs to the following passage (verses 38–41); it appears here as in the source.]
(أخراهم وأولاهم): It is possible that [أخرى] is «فُعلى», the feminine of the «أفعل» that denotes comparison (mufāḍala); on this view the meaning is: the last of them in rank — the followers and the lowly — [said] to the first of them in rank — the leaders, the masters and the chiefs. It is also possible that «أخرى» means "last" (آخِرة), the feminine of «آخِر» as opposed to «أوّل», not the feminine of the «آخَر» of comparison; from this usage is His words, the Exalted: «ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى». Perhaps this is the more apparent [meaning] in the verse.
(الضِّعْفِ): Abū ʿUbayda said: الضعف is the like of a thing once. Al-Azharī said: It is as people use it in the course of their speech. In the speech of the Arabs الضعف is the like and more, and it is not restricted to two likes; rather you say: «هذا ضعفه», meaning twice it and three times it, because الضعف originally means an unlimited increase. Do you not see His words, the Exalted: «فأولئك لهم جزاء الضعف»? He did not mean by it one like nor two likes; the most fitting thing is to make it ten times, as in His words, the Exalted: «من جاء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها». So the minimum of الضعف is limited, namely one like, and its maximum is unlimited. In al-Qāmūs: «ضِعف of a thing, with kasra, is its like, and its two ضعف are its two likes; الضعف is the like and more. One says: لك ضعفه, meaning twice it and three times it, because it is an unlimited increase».
(يَلِجَ): In al-Miṣbāḥ: «ولج الشيء في غيره يلج, of the pattern of وعد, ولوجا [= the thing entered into another]; and أولجته إيلاجا: I made it enter».
(سَمِّ): السم is said with all three vowels on the sīn. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «السم is what kills, mostly with fatḥa; its plural is سموم and سمام, like فلس and فلوس, and also سِمام, like سهم and سهام. The ḍamma is the dialect of the people of al-ʿĀliya, and the kasra the dialect of Banū Tamīm ... And السم is the eye of the needle; it has the three dialectal forms, and its plural is سمام». That is what is meant in the verse, but the Seven [readers] read it with fatḥa, and it has been read anomalously (shādhdhan) with kasra and ḍamma. The eye of the needle is proverbial for the narrowness of a passage; one says: «أضيق من خرت الإبرة» (narrower than the eye of a needle). They called the skilled guide خِرّيت, because he finds his way through narrow places likened to the eyes of needles. And the camel is proverbial for great bulk. Ḥassān ibn Thābit said:
لا بأس في القوم من طول ومن عظم ... جسم البغال وأحلام العصافير
(There is no harm in the people as regards height and bulk: the bodies of mules and the minds of sparrows.) That is: no harm or hurt befalls these people from the side of height and thickness.
In it there is mockery of them: their bodies are like the bodies of mules, and their minds like the minds of sparrows — if sparrows have minds; he means that they have no minds.
(غَواشٍ): the plural of غاشية, which is a covering.

dervis-irab:38-41.t:
* I'rab:
(قالَ ادْخُلُوا فِي أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ فِي النَّارِ) The speech is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), relating what Allah will say to them on the Day of Resurrection. قال is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو"; the clause ادخلوا is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech); في أمم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. being among the number of nations, in their throng, accompanying them; it has also been said that they are attached to ادخلوا, the meaning being "among the number of nations". The clause قد خلت is a naʿt (adjective) of أمم; من قبلكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted second adjective; من الجن والإنس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted third adjective; في النار is a preposition and its genitive noun, a badal (substitute) of His words:
«في أمم». The adverbial expressions (ẓurūf) are figurative, and they will be discussed. Abū Ḥayyān said:
في النار is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «خلت», on the sense that their entry into it came before; or to an omitted adjective of الأمم, i.e. among nations preceding in time, being of the jinn and mankind, being in the Fire. Abū Ḥayyān went on at length in what has no use. (كُلَّما دَخَلَتْ أُمَّةٌ لَعَنَتْ أُخْتَها) كلما is an adverb of time containing the meaning of condition; the clause دخلت أمة is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, or has no grammatical position if we take «ما» as a particle-relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī); the clause لعنت أختها has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivizing condition, and the adverbial sentence is part of the completion of maqūl al-qawl. (حَتَّى إِذَا ادَّارَكُوا فِيها جَمِيعاً) حتى is a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition, or an inceptive particle; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, attached to the apodosis, i.e. to قالت that follows; the clause اداركوا is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اداركوا; جميعا is a ḥāl. (قالَتْ أُخْراهُمْ لِأُولاهُمْ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of إذا. In لأولاهم the lām is a preposition of cause, i.e. for their sake, or of communication (tablīgh); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قالت. (رَبَّنا هؤُلاءِ أَضَلُّونا فَآتِهِمْ عَذاباً ضِعْفاً مِنَ النَّارِ) ربنا is a muḍāf vocative (munādā) from which the vocative particle has been omitted; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause أضلونا its khabar (predicate); the sentence ربنا هؤلاء is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl. فآتهم: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ; آتهم is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); عذابا is a second mafʿūl bihi; ضعفا is an adjective of «عذابا»; من النار is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted second adjective. (قالَ: لِكُلٍّ ضِعْفٌ وَلكِنْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ)
The sentence of saying is resumptive; لكل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ضعف is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the nominal sentence is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying of the Exalted. In ولكن the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or resumptive, and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal); لا is negating; تعلمون is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn. (وَقالَتْ أُولاهُمْ لِأُخْراهُمْ فَما كانَ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنا مِنْ فَضْلٍ) Conjoined to what preceded. The fāʾ is a conjunction: it conjoins the speech after it to the words of Allah the Exalted to the lowly ones, "for each is a double", i.e. it has been established that you have no superiority over us. ما is negating; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of defective كان; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; فضل is genitive in form and the ism of kāna in position; علينا is a preposition and its genitive noun. That is: we and you are equal in going astray and in deserving the punishment. (فَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَكْسِبُونَ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, i.e. if it has become clear to you and you know it, and then you persisted in your contrary position, then taste; العذاب is its object; in بما the bāʾ is a causal preposition and ما is maṣdariyya, i.e. because of your earning; the clause تكسبون is the khabar of كنتم. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا عَنْها لا تُفَتَّحُ لَهُمْ أَبْوابُ السَّماءِ) Resumptive speech introduced to confirm the fate of the disbelievers. إنّ and its noun; the clause كذبوا بآياتنا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, having no grammatical position; the clause استكبروا is conjoined to the clause كفروا [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is كذبوا]; عنها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استكبروا; the clause لا تفتح is the khabar of إنّ; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تفتح; أبواب السماء is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَلا يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى يَلِجَ الْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ الْخِياطِ) This clause is conjoined to the clause لا تفتح لهم; حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; في سم الخياط is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يلج. (وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُجْرِمِينَ) The wāw is resumptive; كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. a recompense like that; المجرمين is a mafʿūl bihi. (لَهُمْ مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ مِهادٌ) The nominal sentence may be circumstantial or resumptive; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; مهاد is a delayed mubtadaʾ; من جهنم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of جهنم [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. an adjective of مهاد fronted before it]. (وَمِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ غَواشٍ وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ) Conjoined; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; غواش is a delayed mubtadaʾ, the ḍamma being implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. More will be said about it in the Benefits section.

* Rhetoric:
In His words, the Exalted: «حتى يلج الجمل سم الخياط» there is a rhetorical figure called al-madhhab al-kalāmī (the dialectical method). Ibn al-Muʿtazz says in his book al-Badīʿ that al-Jāḥiẓ gave it this name. They define it as the speaker's arguing for what he wishes to establish with a proof that blunts the weapon of the stubborn opponent and cuts off his evidence, in the manner of the scholars of kalām.
For the science of kalām consists in establishing the principles of religion by rational proofs and decisive demonstrations that refute obstinacy; and of it there is a logical kind, in which correct conclusions are drawn from true premises. In the verse before us, the way the conclusion is drawn from the two premises is to say: the disbelievers will never enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle; and the camel will never pass through the eye of the needle; therefore they will never enter Paradise — because making a condition depend on something impossible entails the impossibility of what is conditioned. Much of it will occur in the Noble Quran.

The dialectical method in poetry:
This figure has occurred in much Arabic poetry, and they have masterpieces in it. Among them are the words of Abū Tammām:
وإذا أراد الله نشر فضيلة ... طويت أتاح لها لسان حسود
لولا اشتعال النار فيما جاورت ... ما كان يعرف طيب عرف العود
(When Allah wishes to spread a hidden virtue, He provides for it the tongue of an envier; were it not for the fire blazing in what is next to it, the fragrance of aloeswood would not be known.)
The following piece by Bahāʾ al-Dīn Zuhayr is full of varieties of this figure, and we content ourselves with quoting it:
يا من أكابد فيه ما أكابده ... مولاي أصبر حتى يحكم الله
سمّيت غيرك محبوبي مغالطة ... لمعشر فيك قد فاهوا بما فاهوا أقول زيد، وزيد لست أعرفه ... وإنما هو لفظ أنت م
عناه وكم ذكرت مسمّى لا اكتراث به ... حتى يجرّ إلى ذكراك ذ
كراه أتيه فيك على العشاق كلهم ... قد عزّ من أنت يا مولاي
مولاه والناس فينا ببعض القول قد لهجوا ... لو صحّ ما ذكروا ما كنت
آباه كادت عيونهم بالبغض تنطق لي ... حتى كأنّ عيون الناس أفواه
[Translator's note: the line breaks of these verses are disordered in the source and are reproduced as found.]
(O you for whom I endure what I endure, my master, I will be patient until Allah judges. I called someone other than you my beloved, to mislead people who have said what they said about you: I say "Zayd", and Zayd I do not know — it is only a word whose meaning is you. How often I mention someone named for whom I care nothing, until mentioning him leads to mentioning you. I am proud over all lovers because of you: mighty is he whose master you are, my master. People have prattled about us with certain talk; were what they said true, I would not refuse it. Their eyes almost spoke to me with hatred, until it was as if people's eyes were mouths.)
All the reasons mentioned within these verses are genuine, original reasons that the stubborn opponent accepts on hearing them without dispute and without resorting to obstinacy and haughtiness; and that is not hidden from anyone with a grain of taste.

* Benefits:
1- Substitution of the tāʾ:
In ادّكر there are two aspects [Translator's note: so in the source; the word under discussion is ادّاركوا]. The first: the origin is تداركوا, as we mentioned in the Vocabulary section. Whatever has as its first radical a thāʾ, dhāl, dāl, zāy, ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ or ẓāʾ, on the pattern تفاعل, تفعّل or تفعلل, such that the tāʾ and one of these letters come together, the tāʾ is replaced by a letter of the same kind as what follows it and assimilated into it, e.g. اثّاقل، ادّكر، ازّيّن، اصّبر، اضّرع، اطّرب، اظّلم [Translator's note: the source prints «اصتبر»], whose origins are تثاقل، تذكّر، تزيّن، تصبّر، تضرّع، تطرّب، تظلّم. The tāʾ was replaced by a letter of the same kind as what follows it, then made quiescent to be assimilated. Beginning with a quiescent letter being impossible, the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was brought in to escape that.
The second: when the tāʾ of افتعل is changed into a letter homogeneous with what follows it, in stating the pattern one pronounces the original tāʾ of iftiʿāl and not what it has become, ṭāʾ or dāl. So we say the pattern of اصطبر is افتعل, not افطعل, and the pattern of ازدجر is افتعل, not افدعل. Likewise we say here that the pattern of ادّاركوا is اتفاعلوا, not افّاعلوا; there is no difference in this between the tāʾ of iftiʿāl and that of tafāʿul.

2- The defective (manqūṣ) plural on the pattern مفاعل:
The grammarians have two views on a plural on the pattern مفاعل when it is manqūṣ. Some said: it is fully declinable (munṣarif), because the form of the ultimate plural pattern (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ) has left it, so its pattern has become that of جناح; [the cause] has gone, so it is declined. The majority said:
it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), and the tanwīn is a tanwīn of compensation (ʿiwaḍ); this was discussed before.
They differed over what it compensates for. The majority hold that it compensates for the omitted yāʾ; al-Mubarrad held that it compensates for its vowel, and the kasra is not a kasra of i'rab.

dervis-irab:42-43.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الوسع), with all three vowels on the wāw: capacity. One says: «ليس في وسعه أن يفعل كذا», i.e. he is not able to do it. Al-Zajjāj said: الوسع is what one is able to do.
(الغل): rancour.

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ) Resumptive speech introduced to begin mentioning the promise to the believers and what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter, after mentioning the threat to the disbelievers and what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter. The relative noun is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause عملوا الصالحات is conjoined to the ṣila. (لا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْساً إِلَّا وُسْعَها) The clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate). The parenthesis is fitting here because it is of the same kind as the speech: when He, the Exalted, made mention of their righteous deeds, He stated that those deeds are within their capacity and ability and do not go beyond the range of their power. لا is negating; نكلف is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "نحن"; نفسا is the first object of نكلف; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); وسعها is the second object of نكلف. (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ) The nominal sentence is the khabar of الذين; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and أصحاب الجنة its khabar; هم is a mubtadaʾ and خالدون its khabar; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) His word خالدون; the clause هم فيها خالدون is a second khabar of أولئك, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of أصحاب الجنة. (وَنَزَعْنا ما فِي صُدُورِهِمْ مِنْ غِلٍّ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ الْأَنْهارُ) The wāw is a conjunction; نزعنا is a verb and its agent; ما is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في صدورهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted ṣila of the relative; من غلّ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause تجري is a ḥāl of the pronoun. (وَقالُوا: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي هَدانا لِهذا) The wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a verb and its agent; الحمد is a mubtadaʾ; لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; the nominal sentence is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech); الذي is a relative noun, a naʿt (adjective) of لله; the clause هدانا لهذا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (وَما كُنَّا لِنَهْتَدِيَ لَوْلا أَنْ هَدانَا اللَّهُ) The wāw may be resumptive or circumstantial; ما is negating; كان and its noun; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); نهتدي is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām of denial; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar. لولا is a particle of impossibility due to existence (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd); أن is maṣdariyya, and it together with what it governs is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ being omitted, as the rule states:
وبعد لولا غالبا حذف الخبر ... حتم وفي نص يمين ذا استقر
(After لولا, usually, omission of the khabar is obligatory, and in an explicit oath this is established.)
The apodosis of لولا is omitted because what precedes indicates it; the implied sense is: were it not that Allah's guidance of us exists, we would not have been guided, or we would have been wretched. The whole sentence is resumptive or circumstantial. (لَقَدْ جاءَتْ رُسُلُ رَبِّنا بِالْحَقِّ) The lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); جاءت رسل ربنا is a verb and its agent; بالحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاءت. (وَنُودُوا أَنْ تِلْكُمُ الْجَنَّةُ أُورِثْتُمُوها بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; نودوا is a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); أن may be lightened from the heavy [أنّ] or explicative (mufassira). In تلكم الجنة the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, and الجنة is the khabar, or a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative with the khabar being the clause أورثتموها; on the first [view] the clause أورثتموها is circumstantial. The i'rab of the like of بما كنتم تعملون has been given many times before.

dervis-irab:1-3.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المص): A detailed discussion of the openings of the surahs has already been given in Sūrat al-Baqara. We now add to it what al-Suyūṭī mentioned in one of his reports, the gist of which is that these letters are the sound of revelation when it first came down upon the Prophet ﷺ. The well-known words for calling attention, such as ألا and أما, were not used because they are among the words people are accustomed to in their speech, and the Quran is speech unlike any speech, so it was fitting that it should bring words of calling attention that were not familiar, so as to strike the ears more effectively. He also mentioned that when the Arabs heard the Quran they would make noise over it, so Allah revealed this marvellous arrangement so that they would wonder at it, and their wonder at it would be a way of winning them over, and their listening to it a way of listening to what comes after it, so that hearts would soften and souls become tender. In what al-Suyūṭī mentioned there is much sound judgement and fine insight, for the soul is more cheerful towards what is astonishing, and more eager for what is sudden and not familiar or customary.

* I'rab:
(المص كِتابٌ أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ فَلا يَكُنْ فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِنْهُ): المص:
The i'rab of the openings of the surahs has been given in Sūrat al-Baqara, so refresh your acquaintance with it. كتاب is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a Book"; the clause أنزل إليك is an adjective (ṣifa) of كتاب, and إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to أنزل. The ف is a conjunction serving to emphasise the intensity of the prohibition of the الجرح [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for «الحرج» (constraint)], which here is doubt and wavering. Prohibiting the cause is prohibiting the effect by way of demonstration, so what is meant is to forbid him what produces constraint. لا is prohibitive, and يكن is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; في صدرك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of يكن, placed first, and حرج is its noun placed after it. منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of حرج, and the preposition من is causal. (لِتُنْذِرَ بِهِ وَذِكْرى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The لام is causal, and تنذر is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنزل, and به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تنذر. ذكرى: it may be conjoined to «لتنذر»; its being accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) is excluded because its time differs from the time of what it gives the reason for, and because the agent differs: the agent of the sending down is Allah, and the agent of the warning is the Prophet. It may be conjoined to the position of «لتنذر», on the model of conjoining an explicit ḥāl (circumstantial) to an interpreted ḥāl, as in His saying the Exalted: «... دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما». «ذكرى» may also be nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or by conjunction to «كتاب». Abū al-Baqāʾ erred and allowed it to be a ḥāl; this is not permissible because the و enters upon an explicit ḥāl. It may also be genitive by conjunction to the maṣdar interpreted from the implied أن and the verb, the implied form being: "for the sending down and the reminding".
The Kufans said: it is genitive by conjunction to the pronoun in «به». للمؤمنين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of ذكرى. (اتَّبِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) A resumptive statement, set forth to address those legally responsible in general, and the unbelievers in particular, as evidenced by His saying: ولا تتبعوا من دونه أولياء. اتبعوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the ن, and the و is the fāʿil (agent); ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause أنزل is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; إليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزل, and من ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl of the relative noun. (وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءَ قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ) The و is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تتبعوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا. من دونه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تتبعوا, or to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of أولياء and was placed before it. أولياء is a direct object. قليلا is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a little remembrance", or an adjective of a time, i.e. "a little time"; ما is redundant (mazīda), to go deep in emphasising the littleness. تذكرون: originally تتذكرون, an imperfect verb from which one of its two ت's has been dropped; the sign of its nominative is the retention of the ن, and the و is the agent.

dervis-irab:44-47.t:
* Vocabulary:
(العوج) with kasra on the ʿayn: [crookedness] in abstract things and in concrete things that are not upright; with fatḥa: in things that stand upright, such as a spear or a wall. Further discussion of this root will come.
(الْأَعْرافِ): a wall set up between Paradise and the Fire; they are its heights. It is the plural of عُرف, borrowed from the comb of the cock and the mane of the horse. The authors of the long works have described it at length, and some of them brought the views on it to thirteen.
As for the root ع ر ف, it is remarkable, and we mention here some of its properties and meanings, in keeping with what we have aimed at in this book. One says عرف الشيء يعرفه, of the pattern of ضرب, عرفة, عرفانا and معرفة: he knew it. عرف يعرُف with ḍamma, of the pattern of نصر, عرافة على القوم: he managed them and administered their affairs. عرُف يعرُف with ḍamma in the past and the imperfect, عرافة: he became an ʿarīf (overseer); and [عرف also means] he used much perfume. Among the borrowed usages: the أعراف of the wind, the clouds and the fog, for their front parts; اعرورف البحر: its waves rose high; اعرورف فلان للشر: he craned towards it; and a عرفاء hilltop is a high one. Zuhayr said:
ومرقبة عرفاء أوفيت مقصرا ... لأستأنس الأشباح فيه وأنظرا
(Many a high lookout I have climbed at evening, to make out the figures and to watch.)
مقصرا is from القصر, which is the late afternoon (al-ʿashiyy). العرّاف is lower than the soothsayer (kāhin); they said: «إذا سال بك الغراف لم ينفعك العراف» (when the torrent sweeps you away, the diviner will not help you). And ʿUrwa said:
جعلت لعرّاف اليمامة حكمه ... وعرّاف نجد إذ هما شفياني
(I gave the diviner of al-Yamāma his fee, and the diviner of Najd, if the two would cure me.)
(السّيمى), and السّيمة, السّومة, السّيماء and السيمياء: the mark, the appearance, the radiance and the beauty.

* I'rab:
(وَنادى أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ أَصْحابَ النَّارِ) The clause is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), introduced for affirmation and rebuke. أصحاب الجنة is the fāʿil (agent) of نادى, and أصحاب النار its object. (أَنْ قَدْ وَجَدْنا ما وَعَدَنا رَبُّنا حَقًّا) أن is lightened from the heavy [أنّ], so its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and the clause قد وجدنا is its khabar (predicate); or «أن» is explicative (mufassira), so the clause قد وجدنا has no grammatical position because it is explicative. ما is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause وعدنا ربنا is the ṣila (relative clause), having no grammatical position; حقا is the second mafʿūl bihi of وجدنا. (فَهَلْ وَجَدْتُمْ ما وَعَدَ رَبُّكُمْ حَقًّا قالُوا نَعَمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; هل is an interrogative particle; the i'rab of وجدتم and what follows it has been given above. قالوا is a verb and its agent, and the clause is resumptive; نعم is a particle of answer, and the omitted answer-clause is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech). (فَأَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ بَيْنَهُمْ أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; أذن مؤذن is a verb and its agent; أن is lightened from the heavy, and it together with what it governs is in the position of the genitive by removal of the preposition, the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) أذن. It is also possible that «أن» is explicative, in which case the clause أن and what falls within its scope has no grammatical position. لعنة الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject); على الظالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of لعنة; and if أن is lightened from the heavy, «لعنة» is likewise parsed as a mubtadaʾ. (الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَيَبْغُونَها عِوَجاً) الذين is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الظالمين; you may also parse it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. they are those who turn away. The clause يصدون has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative; عن سبيل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يصدون; يبغونها is conjoined to يصدون: an imperfect verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi; عوجا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. crooked. The meaning of crookedness here is deviation from the truth, by disfiguring the religion, confusing people and giving them the illusion that it contains a departure from the right road and a deviation from the truth. (وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ كافِرُونَ) The wāw is circumstantial; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ; بالآخرة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «كافرون»; كافرون is the khabar of «هم»; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (وَبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ وَعَلَى الْأَعْرافِ رِجالٌ يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّا بِسِيماهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; the adverb بينهما is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; حجاب is a delayed mubtadaʾ, i.e. between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire; and likewise His words وعلى الأعراف رجال. The clause يعرفون is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of رجال; كلا is a mafʿūl bihi; بسيماهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يعرفون. (وَنادَوْا أَصْحابَ الْجَنَّةِ أَنْ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ لَمْ يَدْخُلُوها وَهُمْ يَطْمَعُونَ) The clause is resumptive, introduced to speak about the people of al-Aʿrāf. The discussion of them and of their rank is found in the long works, so refer to them if you wish.
نادوا is a verb and its agent, the pronoun referring to the people of al-Aʿrāf; أصحاب الجنة is its object; أن is lightened from the heavy or explicative, as discussed before; سلام is a mubtadaʾ — beginning with it [though indefinite] is allowed because of the sense of supplication in it, which particularizes it; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar. The clause لم يدخلوها is resumptive, introduced to serve as an answer to someone asking about the people of al-Aʿrāf, as though it had been said: What was done with them? And it was said: They have not entered it. The wāw is circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يطمعون is the khabar; and the clause وهم etc. is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (وَإِذا صُرِفَتْ أَبْصارُهُمْ تِلْقاءَ أَصْحابِ النَّارِ) The wāw is a conjunction, completing the account of the people of al-Aʿrāf; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, attached to the apodosis (jawāb), which is قالوا; the clause صرفت is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; أبصارهم is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); تلقاء is an adverb of place attached to صرفت. It also occurs as a maṣdar (verbal noun); no maṣdars have come on the pattern تِفعال with kasra on the tāʾ other than a limited number.
(قالُوا: رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) The clause is the apodosis of a non-jussivizing condition, so it has no grammatical position. ربنا is a muḍāf vocative (munādā); لا is prohibitive, here meaning supplication; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi; مع is an adverb of place attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi; القوم is muḍāf ilayhi; الظالمين is an adjective of القوم.

* Benefits:
The maṣdars of this pattern are all on تفعال with fatḥa on the tāʾ; تِفعال [with kasra] occurs only in nouns, and they are not many. Some authorities on the language mentioned sixteen nouns of it, among them التبيان and التلقاء; «مرّ تهواء من الليل» (a stretch of the night passed); تبراك, تعشار and ترباع, which are places; تمساح, the well-known animal — and التمساح is also the lying man; الزلزال; تجفاف [horse armour]; تمثال [statue]; تمراد — the تمراد is a small compartment in a dovecote for its laying; تلفاق, which is two garments sewn together; تلقام, i.e. quick at swallowing; and one says «أتت الناقة على تضرابها», i.e. at the time when the stallion covered her; تضراب, one who strikes much; تقصار, which is the المخنفة [Translator's note: so in the source; probably المِخنقة, a close-fitting necklace]; and تنبال, which is the short [man].

dervis-irab:48-51.t:
* I'rab:
(وَنادى أَصْحابُ الْأَعْرافِ رِجالًا يَعْرِفُونَهُمْ بِسِيماهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive, introduced to set out what the people of al-Aʿrāf say to the people of the Fire. نادى أصحاب الأعراف is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); رجالا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause يعرفونهم is a naʿt (adjective) of «رجالا»; بسيماهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يعرفونهم, i.e. among those who in the world were marked by grandeur and conceit. (قالُوا: ما أَغْنى عَنْكُمْ جَمْعُكُمْ وَما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ) The sentence of saying has no grammatical position because it is explicative: it explains the calling. ما is an interrogative noun of rebuke, i.e. what thing availed you? It may also be negating. On the first [view] it is a fronted object of أغنى, i.e. [what] benefited you, and [what] your gathering in the world warded off from you; جمعكم is the fāʿil; [the second] ما is maṣdariyya, interpreted with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) conjoined to جمعكم, i.e. and your arrogance, understood from His words «وكنتم تستكبرون»; the clause تستكبرون is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم; and the sentence is maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech). (أَهؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أَقْسَمْتُمْ لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ) The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation and rebuke (taqrīrī tawbīkhī); هؤلاء is a mubtadaʾ (subject); الذين is a relative noun, the khabar; the clause أقسمتم [Translator's note: the source prints «أقستم»] is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; the clause لا ينالهم الله برحمة has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; لا is negating; ينالهم الله is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil; برحمة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينالهم. (ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلا أَنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ) The imperative clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. it has been said to them; the omitted sentence of saying is a second khabar of the demonstrative, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it, i.e. that being said to them. لا is negating and inoperative (muhmala); خوف is a mubtadaʾ — beginning with it [though indefinite] is allowed because negation comes before it; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; the clause ولا أنتم تحزنون is conjoined to the preceding clause. (وَنادى أَصْحابُ النَّارِ أَصْحابَ الْجَنَّةِ) The i'rab of its like has been given before. (أَنْ أَفِيضُوا عَلَيْنا مِنَ الْماءِ أَوْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ) أن is lightened from the heavy [أنّ] or explicative (mufassira); its like has occurred before. أفيضوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; علينا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أفيضوا; من الماء is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to أفيضوا, because the sense of pouring here includes the sense of casting. أو is a conjunction; مما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted [element] conjoined to من الماء; a verb must be implied, i.e. "and feed us", in the manner of their saying: «علفتها تبنا وماء باردا» (I fed her straw and [gave her] cold water); or, by making أفيضوا include the sense of "cast", the attachment of the conjoined element to it is valid. The clause رزقكم الله is the ṣila. It is better that «أو» be in the sense of the wāw for [the meaning] to be sound, and it has parallels in the language. (قالُوا: إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَهُما عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ) The clause is resumptive, to state their answer; the sentence إنّ, its noun and its khabar is in the position of the accusative as the object of their saying; the clause حرمهما is the khabar of إنّ; على الكافرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حرمهما. What is meant by forbidding is its consequence, which is withholding. (الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَهُمْ لَهْواً وَلَعِباً) A relative noun in the position of the genitive as an adjective of الكافرين; the clause اتخذوا is the ṣila; دينهم is the first object of اتخذوا and لهوا its second object; لعبا is conjoined to «لهوا». (وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا) The wāw is a conjunction; غرتهم الحياة is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil; الدنيا is an adjective of الحياة, i.e. it beguiled them with its ornaments and occupied them with greed. (فَالْيَوْمَ نَنْساهُمْ كَما نَسُوا لِقاءَ يَوْمِهِمْ هذا) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa; اليوم is an adverb of time attached to ننساهم; the kāf is a preposition and ما is maṣdariyya, i.e. like their forgetting; the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); لقاء is the mafʿūl bihi of نسوا; يومهم is muḍāf ilayhi; هذا is an adjective of يومهم or a badal (substitute) of it. (وَما كانُوا بِآياتِنا يَجْحَدُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is maṣdariyya, and the resulting maṣdar is conjoined to the first maṣdar; كان and its noun; the clause يجحدون is its khabar; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يجحدون.

dervis-irab:52-53.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ جِئْناهُمْ بِكِتابٍ فَصَّلْناهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ) Resumptive speech introduced to affirm what is set out in the Book in detail of what they did. The lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); جئناهم is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; بكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) جئناهم; the clause فصلناه is a naʿt (adjective) of the Book; على علم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), either of the agent in «فصلناه», i.e. We detailed it knowing its details, or of the object, i.e. We detailed it as containing knowledge. (هُدىً وَرَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ) هدى and رحمة are a ḥāl of the object of فصلناه, i.e.
guiding and showing mercy. They may also be parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. We detailed it for the sake of guidance and mercy. لقوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun); the clause يؤمنون is an adjective of قوم. (هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا تَأْوِيلَهُ) Resumptive speech setting out their stance towards the Book which they deny while at the same time awaiting what it will come to and the outcome of its matter. هل is an interrogative particle in the sense of negation and disapproval, i.e. they await and expect nothing other than that; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). He treated them as those who expect and await, though they are not so, since they deny it. تأويله is a mafʿūl bihi. (يَوْمَ يَأْتِي تَأْوِيلُهُ يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ نَسُوهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ) Resumptive speech introduced to state what they will say on that day. The adverb is attached to يقول; the clause يأتي تأويله is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; تأويله is the fāʿil of يأتي; يقول الذين is a verb and its agent; the clause نسوه is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نسوه [Translator's note: the source prints «بنسوة»], i.e. before the coming of its fulfilment. (قَدْ جاءَتْ رُسُلُ رَبِّنا بِالْحَقِّ) The clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of their saying; جاءت رسل ربنا is a verb and its agent;
بالحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاءت. (فَهَلْ لَنا مِنْ شُفَعاءَ فَيَشْفَعُوا لَنا) The fāʾ is a conjunction; هل is an interrogative particle; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; شفعاء is genitive in form by من and in the position of the nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya), because it occurs in the answer to an interrogative; يشفعوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يشفعوا. (أَوْ نُرَدُّ فَنَعْمَلَ غَيْرَ الَّذِي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ) أو is a conjunction; نرد is a passive imperfect verb; the clause is conjoined to the clause before it, falling with it under the scope of the interrogative, as though it were said: Are there any intercessors for us, or will we be returned? نرد is in the nominative because it occupies the place of a noun, so it is a case of conjoining an interpreted noun to an explicit noun, i.e. Are there intercessors for us, and so intercession from them for us? The fāʾ is also causal; نعمل is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ in answer to the second interrogative; غير is the object of نعمل; الذي is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause كنا نعمل is the ṣila; كان and its noun, and the clause نعمل is the khabar of كان. (قَدْ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ) Resumptive speech introduced to state the answer to the two preceding questions. قد is a particle of realization; خسروا is a verb and its agent; أنفسهم is a mafʿūl bihi; ضل عنهم is conjoined to خسروا; عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ضل; ما is a relative noun, the fāʿil; the clause كانوا يفترون is the ṣila of the relative; and the clause يفترون is the khabar of كانوا.

dervis-irab:54-55.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُغْشِي): covers. [One says:] «انجلت عنه غشية الحمّى», i.e. the fit of the fever cleared from him; «نزلت به غشية الموت» (the swoon of death came upon him); «غشي عليه» (he fainted); «أصابه غشي» (a faint struck him). Dhū al-Rumma said:
وردت وأغباش السّواد كأنها ... سمادير غشي في العيون النواظر
(I came down [to the water] while the dark remnants of night were like the swimming of a faint in looking eyes.)
«على قلبه غشاوة فما يقبل الحق» (there is a covering on his heart, so he does not accept the truth); «استغش ثوبك كي لا تسمع ولا ترى» (cover yourself with your garment so that you neither hear nor see); «كثرت غاشية فلان» (So-and-so's visitors became many). The ghayn followed by the shīn, as the first and second radicals of the verb, has a meaning that is almost the same throughout, namely covering and concealing. غشّ (cheating) is well known, as though [the cheat] hid his scheme; «غشم الوالي الرعية», and he is غشوم, when he tramples them with his oppression; «غشمر السيل»: the torrent came on; and [غشمر] the man: he followed his own head in right and wrong, not caring what he did. This is one of the subtleties of the language, so reflect on it.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ) Resumptive speech introduced to affirm the creation of the heavens and the earth. إنّ and its noun; الله is its khabar (predicate); الذي is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of الله; the clause خلق السموات والأرض is the ṣila (relative clause); في ستة أيام is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلق. (ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ) ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; استوى is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو", i.e. He became established and settled, a settling free of any "how"; على العرش is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استوى. (يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ) The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); الليل is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يغشي and النهار the second, or the reverse, i.e. He makes the night overtake the day or the day the night. (يَطْلُبُهُ حَثِيثاً وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ وَالنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّراتٍ بِأَمْرِهِ) The clause is a ḥāl of الليل, because it is what is being spoken of, i.e. it covers the day seeking it; it may also be a ḥāl of النهار, i.e. being sought. يطلبه is a verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi; حثيثا is a ḥāl of the agent of يطلبه
or of its object, i.e. urging or urged; it may also be parsed as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and so be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. a swift seeking. الشمس والقمر والنجوم: the three words are accusative, conjoined to السموات والأرض; مسخرات is a ḥāl of them, i.e. made subservient to what is willed of them of rising and setting; بأمره is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مسخرات or to an omitted ḥāl, the bāʾ being of accompaniment, i.e. accompanying His command and not departing from it in their subjection. (أَلا لَهُ الْخَلْقُ وَالْأَمْرُ) Resumptive speech introduced to draw attention to the refutation of those who claim that these things have effects in this wondrous world. ألا is a particle of opening and alerting; له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; الخلق is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); الأمر is conjoined to it. (تَبارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعالَمِينَ) Another resumption, introduced to draw attention to the abundance of His good, the Exalted, and to blessing, sanctifying and exalting Him. تبارك is a past verb, i.e. He is holy and exalted; it is a frozen (jāmid) verb that is not inflected, i.e. no imperfect, imperative or active participle comes from it; الله is the fāʿil; رب العالمين is an adjective or a badal (substitute) of الله. (ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعاً وَخُفْيَةً إِنَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ) Resumptive speech introduced to draw attention to the fact that supplication must be directed to Him alone, the Exalted.
ادعوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; ربكم is a mafʿūl bihi; تضرعا is accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. possessed of humility; خفية is conjoined to it. It may also be parsed as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. call on Him with a supplication of humility and a supplication of secrecy. Which of the two is better?
There is a disagreement about it, for which one should refer to the long works. They may also be parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The clause إنه لا يحب المعتدين is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya), falling under the ruling of the resumptive, with no grammatical position. The meaning of transgression here is overstepping the limit. The clause لا يحب المعتدين is the khabar of «إنّ».

dervis-irab:4-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَياتاً), i.e. by night. It is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun). One says: بات يبيت ويبات, بيتا, بيتة, بياتا, بيتوتة, مبيتا and مباتا, of the patterns فتح and جلس, [of being] in a place: he stayed in it for the night.
(قائِلُونَ): sleeping at the time of midday. القيلولة is sleep at midday, or rest at midday even if there is no sleep with it. One says «هذا مقيل طيب» (this is a pleasant midday resting place), and «هو شروب للقيل», which is the drink of القائلة, i.e. midday. The mother of Taʾabbaṭa Sharran said: «ما سقيته غيلا، ولا حرمته قيلا» (I never suckled him on milk while pregnant, nor denied him the midday feed), which is the midday suckling. And «اقتال الرجل», just as you say اصطبح and اغتبق (to take the morning and the evening drink).

* I'rab:
(وَكَمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْناها فَجاءَها بَأْسُنا بَياتاً أَوْ هُمْ قائِلُونَ) The و is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, set forth to speak about past nations and what their fate was because of their turning away from the truth and their aversion to listening to its teachings.
كم is the declarative (khabariyya) كم, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); من قرية is the tamyīz (specification) of the declarative كم, whose rule has already been given; the clause أهلكناها is the khabar (predicate) of «كم». «كم» may also be parsed as being in the position of the accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), with an implied verb explained by what follows it; the clause أهلكناها then has no grammatical position because it is explicative. The ف is a conjunction for sequence and immediate succession; a fine discussion of it will come in the Benefits section. جاءها بأسنا is a verb, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and fāʿil (agent), and the clause is conjoined to أهلكناها. بياتا may be an adverb in view of the meaning, or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), meaning "spending the night"; most parsers hold the latter. The first is sounder in meaning, and the second more regular in i'rab. أو is a conjunction, هم is a mubtadaʾ and قائلون its khabar, and the clause is conjoined to «بياتا», so it is circumstantial. Here an objection arises: how does the clause come as a ḥāl without و, when one does not say «جاءني زيد هو فارس» (Zayd came to me, he being a horseman) without و? The answer will come in the Benefits section. (فَما كانَ دَعْواهُمْ إِذْ جاءَهُمْ بَأْسُنا) The ف is resumptive, ما is negating, كان and its noun; إذ is an adverb of past time attached (mutaʿalliq) to دعواهم, and the clause جاءهم بأسنا is in the position of the genitive by annexation (as muḍāf ilayhi). (إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ) إلا is a particle of restriction, and أن and what follows it are to be interpreted as a maṣdar [that is the khabar of] كان. إنّ and its noun; the clause كنا ظالمين is the khabar of إنّ, and the clause إنا and what falls in its scope is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (فَلَنَسْئَلَنَّ الَّذِينَ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَنَسْئَلَنَّ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) The ف is a conjunction; what is intended by it is to arrange the states of the Hereafter after the states of this world in the mention, according to their order in existence. The لام prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and نسألن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is necessarily joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, as you will learn in the Benefits section [Translator's note: the Benefits section of this entry does not in fact discuss the nūn of emphasis]. The agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being نحن. The clause لنسألنّ is conjoined; الذين is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a direct object; the clause أرسل is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and it is in the passive; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the preposition and its genitive noun, namely إليهم. ولنسألن المرسلين is conjoined to what preceded. The meaning of asking those to whom [messengers] were sent is to put on record against the unbelievers their refusal to listen to what [the messengers] said to them and conveyed to them. (فَلَنَقُصَّنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ بِعِلْمٍ وَما كُنَّا غائِبِينَ) Conjoined to what preceded. عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نقصنّ, i.e. [We will relate] to each of the messengers and those to whom they were sent what happened in their affair. بعلم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl of the agent of نقصنّ, i.e. "knowing the hidden aspects of their states, the folds of their secrets, and what slipped from their lips". The و is circumstantial, ما is negating, كان and its noun, and غائبين is its khabar; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. All these questions and narrations are for rebuke and reproach, as an investigator does with a criminal to convict him, in his presence, of what his own hands have done.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope) in His saying وكم من قرية أهلكناها: He mentioned the town and meant its people. It is a trope whose relation is that of place (al-maḥalliyya). Parallels to it have already been given.

* Benefits:
The wāw of the ḥāl:
It is a و in whose place an adverb could validly occur. It has three states: obligatory mention, prohibited mention and permissible mention. Below are the places of those states:

1- Obligatory mention:
a- When the ḥāl clause is nominal and free of a pronoun linking it to the one whose state it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl), as in His saying the Exalted: «لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة».
b- When the ḥāl clause begins with a pronoun referring to the one whose state it describes, as in:
«لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى».
2- Prohibited mention, in seven cases:
a- When it occurs after a conjunction, as in: «وكم من قرية أهلكناها فجاءها بأسنا بياتا أو هم قائلون».
b- When it emphasises the content of the clause before it, as in: «ذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه», if we parse the clause «لا ريب» as a ḥāl.
c- When it is a past [verbal clause] after إلا, as in: «وما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون».
d- When it is a past [verbal clause] before «أو», as in:
كن للخليل نصيرا جاد أو عدلا ... ولا تشحّ عليه جار أم بخلا
(Be a helper to your friend, whether he was generous or just; and do not be stingy towards him, whether he was unjust or miserly.)
e- When it is an affirmative imperfect [verbal clause] not joined to «قد»; in that case it is linked by the pronoun alone, as in: «ولا تمنن تستكثر». As for the saying of ʿAntara:
علقتها عرضا وأقتل قومها ... قسما لعمر أبيك ليس بمزعم
(I fell in love with her by chance while I was killing her people — an oath, by your father's life, that is no false claim.)
the clause «وأقتل قومها» is a ḥāl of the ت in «علقتها», and it is joined to the و with an affirmative imperfect. There is disagreement over how to account for it. It was said:
it is poetic licence (ḍarūra). It was said: the و is a conjunction and the imperfect is to be interpreted as a past, the implied form being:
«وقتلت قومها» (and I killed her people); he turned from the wording of the past to the wording of the imperfect to narrate a past state, the meaning of which is that what happened in past time is supposed to be occurring in the present, so it is expressed with the wording of the imperfect. It was also said: it is the wāw of the ḥāl, and the imperfect is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «وأنا أقتل قومها» (while I was killing her people).
[f-] When it is an imperfect [verbal clause] negated by «ما», as in his saying [Translator's note: the source omits the letter for this item]:
عهدتك ما تصبو وفيك شبيبة ... فما لك بعد الشّيب صبّا متيّما
(I knew you not to be given to passion while there was youth in you; so what is wrong with you that, after grey hair, you are passionate and lovesick?)
g- When it is an imperfect [verbal clause] negated by «لا», as in: «وما لنا لا نؤمن بالله». If the imperfect clause is negated by «لم», it may be linked by the و, as in the saying of al-Nābigha:
سقط النّصيف ولم ترد إسقاطه ... فتناولته واتّقتنا باليد
(The veil fell, though she did not intend to let it fall; she took it up and shielded herself from us with her hand.)
and it may also not be linked by it, but by the pronoun alone, as in: «فانقلبوا بنعمة من الله وفضل لم يمسسهم سوء», and the saying of Zuhayr:
كأنّ فتات العهن في كلّ موطن ... نزلن به حبّ الفنا لم يحطّم
(As if the bits of dyed wool, in every place they halted, were nightshade berries not yet crushed.)
If it is negated by «لما», the preferred course is to link it with the و, as in: «أم حسبتم أن تدخلوا الجنة ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ويعلم الصابرين», and the saying of the poet:
أشوقا ولما يمض لي غير ليلة ... فكيف إذا جدّ المطيّ بنا عشرا
(Longing already, when only one night has passed for me? How then when the mounts have hastened with us for ten?)

3- Permissibility of mention and omission:
This is in cases other than those mentioned above where it is obligatory or prohibited. There are details we have passed over; whoever wishes may refer to them in the detailed books of grammar.
When you know this, you will realise that al-Zamakhsharī's objection does not apply. Here is the detail.
An enjoyable discussion:

What al-Zamakhsharī says:
Al-Zamakhsharī says: «If you say: one says «جاء زيد هو فارس» without و, so what about His saying the Exalted: «أو هم قائلون»? I say: some grammarians assumed an omitted و. Al-Zajjāj rejected this and said: if you said «جاءني زيد راجلا أو هو فارس» (Zayd came to me on foot or on horseback), or «جاءني زيد هو فارس», there would be no need for a و in it, because the reference has gone back to the first [noun]. The correct view is that when it is conjoined to a ḥāl before it, the و is omitted because the combination of two conjunctions is felt to be heavy, since the wāw of the ḥāl is the wāw of conjunction borrowed for linking. So your saying «جاز زيد راجلا، أو هو فارس» [Translator's note: «جاز» is evidently a misprint for «جاءني»] is eloquent speech, occurring according to its rule. As for «جاءني زيد هو فارس», it is bad.» [Translator's note: in the passage as quoted, the attribution of «The correct view…» is ambiguous between al-Zajjāj and al-Zamakhsharī.]

Abū Ḥayyān's rejoinder to al-Zamakhsharī and al-Zajjāj:
Abū Ḥayyān responded, saying: «As for the "some grammarians" whom al-Zamakhsharī accused, it is al-Farrāʾ. As for al-Zamakhsharī's saying, regarding the two examples, "there would be no need for the و in it, because the reference has gone back to the first", there is vagueness in it, and specifying it: its entry was not permitted in the second example [Translator's note: so in the source; the sentence appears garbled, and in the logic of what follows the impossibility of the و concerns the first example]. So the absence of need is not on the same footing, because in the first it is due to the impossibility of entry, and in the second due to the frequency of entry, not to its impossibility.
As for al-Zamakhsharī's saying "The correct view…" to the end, his reasoning is not correct, because the wāw of the ḥāl is not a conjunction such that mentioning it would entail the combination of two conjunctions. For if it were for conjunction, it would be necessary that what comes before the و be a ḥāl, so that a ḥāl is conjoined to a ḥāl; so its occurrence where [what precedes] cannot be a ḥāl is proof that it is not a wāw of conjunction and that the sense of conjunction is not considered in it. You say «جاءني زيد والشمس طالعة» (Zayd came to me while the sun was rising): «جاء زيد» is not a ḥāl to which a ḥāl clause could be conjoined. Rather, this و differs from the wāw of conjunction in every respect; it is one of the kinds of و, just as it comes for the oath, and is not for conjunction there, when you say «والله لتخرجنّ» (By Allah, you will surely go out). As for his saying "it is bad", it is not bad. He based that on the view that when a nominal clause contains a pronoun of the one whose state it describes, omitting the و from it is anomalous (shādhdh); in that he followed al-Farrāʾ. But it is not anomalous; rather it occurs frequently in the Quran and in the speech of the Arabs, its prose and its poetry, and it is more than the sands of Yabrīn and Palestine.
We have mentioned how often it occurs in Sharḥ al-Tashīl. Al-Zamakhsharī [later] retracted this position in favour of the position of the majority.»

Comment on Abū Ḥayyān's words:
I say: Abū Ḥayyān's rejoinder is not free of inconsistency. It has been objected against him that the و is originally for conjunction and was then borrowed to link the ḥāl to its governing agent, just as the ف is originally for conjunction and was then borrowed to link the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) to the condition.

The conjunctive ف:
The ف is for sequence. This is either real, as in «قام زيد فعمرو» (Zayd stood, then ʿAmr), namely that what follows it actually occurs after what precedes it; or in the mention, which is conjoining a detailed account to a summary one, as in: «فأزلهما الشيطان عنها فأخرجهما مما كانا فيه». This is when what follows it occurs after what precedes it in the wording only; as for reality, it sometimes occurs together with it at the same moment, or before what precedes it. Al-Farrāʾ said: it does not indicate sequence at all.
He adduced as proof His saying the Exalted: «أهلكناها فجاءها بأسنا بياتا أو هم قائلون».
It was answered that the meaning is: "We intended to destroy it", and there is no doubt that the intention to destroy is before the coming of the punishment; so it is a sequence in the mention, since it is an explanation of His saying «أهلكناها», which is a summary. The upshot is that the majority hold that it indicates sequence absolutely, and al-Farrāʾ denies that absolutely. Al-Jarmī said: it does not indicate sequence with places or cities, as evidenced by «بين الدخول فحومل» (between al-Dakhūl and Ḥawmal), and their saying: «مطرنا بنوء بمكان كذا» (we were rained upon under such-and-such a star at such-and-such a place), so "such-and-such a place" — if the fall of rain in both was one [time]. [Translator's note: the last example appears truncated or garbled in the source; the usual form is «مطرنا بمكان كذا فمكان كذا», where the rain fell on both places at once.]

The reference of the pronoun:
They gave the muḍāf ilayhi the i'rab of the muḍāf; therefore the pronoun refers back in both the feminine and the masculine. What is meant is: «وكم من أهل قرية» (how many people of a town); then the muḍāf, which is الأهل, was omitted, and the pronoun refers back to both things. It is feminine in His saying «فجاءها بأسنا», in view of the feminine in the wording, namely القرية; and masculine in His saying «أو هم قائلون», in consideration of the omitted [noun]. When the muḍāf was omitted, the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place, the governing agent acted on it directly, and it became accusative as a direct object, although in reality it is not that; likewise they gave it its rule in matters other than i'rab, namely feminine and masculine gender. An example of that is the saying of Ḥassān ibn Thābit:
يسقون من ورد البريص عليهم ... بردى يصفّق بالرحيق السلسل
(They give those who come to them at al-Barīṣ to drink [the water of] Baradā, mixed with pure, smooth wine.)
The point of evidence in it is the masculine pronoun referring to بردى, which is feminine.
البريض is a place in the land of Damascus. [Translator's note: the verse has «البريص» with ص, while this explanation has «البريض» with ض.]

dervis-irab:56-58.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بُشْراً) with ḍamma on the bāʾ and sukūn on the shīn: plural of بشير, i.e. bearers of glad tidings.
There are four readings of it among the Seven: the second is بُشُرا with two ḍammas; the third is فشرا [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently نُشُرا] with nūn and two ḍammas; and the fourth is نَشْرا with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the shīn. The meaning of نشرا is "scattered".
(أَقَلَّتْ): carried and lifted. الإقلال is derived from القلة (fewness), because one who lifts something and is able to bear it regards what he lifts as little.
(نَكِداً) النكد, with kasra on the kāf: that in which there is no good, or that which is hard and difficult; [one says] قوم أنكاد and مناكيد. Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Mutanabbī] said:
لا تشتر العبد إلا والعصا معه ... إنّ العبيد لأنجاس مناكيد
(Do not buy a slave unless the stick comes with him; slaves are filthy, wretched [creatures].)

* I'rab:
(وَلا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ بَعْدَ إِصْلاحِها) Resumptive speech introduced to warn mankind against corruption in the earth. لا is prohibitive; تفسدوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تفسدوا; بعد is an adverb also attached to تفسدوا; إصلاحها is muḍāf ilayhi. (وَادْعُوهُ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً) Conjoined to what preceded. خوفا and طمعا are accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. fearing and hoping; or as adjectives of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); or as two mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose). (إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) The clause gives the reason for what was mentioned. إنّ and its noun; قريب is its khabar (predicate); من المحسنين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قريب. (وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُرْسِلُ الرِّياحَ بُشْراً بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to what is before it, namely إن ربكم etc. هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as the khabar; the clause يرسل الرياح is the ṣila (relative clause), having no grammatical position; بشرا is a ḥāl, i.e. bearing glad tidings of fertility and growth, so it is [a ḥāl] of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بين is an adverb of place attached to يرسل, and its annexation to يدي is a majāz mursal (metonymic trope). (حَتَّى إِذا أَقَلَّتْ سَحاباً ثِقالًا سُقْناهُ لِبَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ) حتى is a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition, the limit being of the sending; إذا is an adverb of future time; the clause أقلت is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the adverb is attached to سقناه, which is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); سحابا is a mafʿūl bihi; ثقالا is a naʿt (adjective); the clause سقناه has no grammatical position; لبلد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to سقناه; ميت is an adjective of بلد. (فَأَنْزَلْنا بِهِ الْماءَ فَأَخْرَجْنا بِهِ مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; أنزلنا is a verb and its agent; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزلنا; the bāʾ is causal, and the pronoun refers to the dead land or to the clouds. On the first [view] the bāʾ is locative (ẓarfiyya), meaning: We sent down the water in that dead land; on the second the الماء [Translator's note: so in the source; read «the bāʾ»] is causal, i.e. We sent down the water because of the clouds. الماء is a mafʿūl bihi; the fāʾ is a conjunction; أخرجنا is conjoined to أنزلنا; the pronoun in «به» likewise refers to the water, the land or the clouds, as mentioned before; من كل الثمرات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of the omitted mafʿūl bihi, i.e. provision or vegetation. (كَذلِكَ نُخْرِجُ الْمَوْتى لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ) Resumptive speech introduced in a rhetorical style by way of comparison (tashbīh), meaning that He who is able to bring forth fresh fruit from dry wood is able to bring the dead to life. كذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted maṣdar, so it is a fronted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); نخرج الموتى is a verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a mafʿūl bihi; the clause of hope is circumstantial; the clause تذكرون is the khabar of لعل. (وَالْبَلَدُ الطَّيِّبُ يَخْرُجُ نَباتُهُ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِ) Resumptive speech introduced to complete the comparison. البلد is a mubtadaʾ; الطيب an adjective; the clause يخرج نباته the khabar; بإذن ربه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, as though it were said: its vegetation comes forth good and abundant, because it stands in contrast to His word «نكدا» later. So there is an omission in the speech because the meaning is understood, because of what الطيب البلد indicates, and because of its being contrasted with His word نكدا. (وَالَّذِي خَبُثَ لا يَخْرُجُ إِلَّا نَكِداً) The wāw is a conjunction; الذي is a mubtadaʾ, and it is a description of an omitted [noun], i.e. the land that is bad; the clause خبث is the ṣila; the clause لا يخرج is the khabar; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) because negation precedes it; نكدا is a ḥāl, i.e. with difficulty and slowly. It may also be accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar: except a scanty coming forth. (كَذلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَشْكُرُونَ) كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar — the i'rab of its like has been given before; الآيات is the object of نصرف; لقوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نصرف; the clause يشكرون is an adjective of قوم.

* Rhetoric:
1- The majāz mursal (metonymic trope) in His words «بين يدي رحمته», which is the rain; the relation is causality, because the hand is the cause of bestowing favour, and bestowing favour is mercy.
2- The unrestricted simile (tashbīh mursal) in His words «كذلك نخرج الموتى». It was pointed to in the I'rab.

* Benefits:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «He made «قريب» masculine only by interpreting الرحمة as الرحم or الترحم (mercy, compassion); or because it is the adjective of an omitted described noun, i.e. something near; by likening it to فعيل in the sense of مفعول; or because the femininity of الرحمة is not real». Abū ʿUbayda said: «قريب» is masculine on the basis of the masculine «place», i.e. a near place. Al-Akhfash replied to him, saying: This is wrong; if it were as he said, «قريب» would be accusative, as you say إن زيدا قريبا منك (Zayd is near you). Al-Farrāʾ said: When قريب means distance, it is treated as masculine or feminine; if it means kinship, it is made feminine without disagreement among them. So one says: دارك منا قريب (your house is near us), and فلانة منا قريب (So-and-so [f.] is close to us). The Exalted said: «لعل الساعة تكون قريبا».
From it are the words of Imruʾ al-Qays:
لك الويل إن أمسى ولا أمّ هاشم ... قريب ولا البسباسة ابنة يشكرا
(Woe to you if evening comes and neither Umm Hāshim is near, nor al-Basbāsa daughter of Yashkur.)

dervis-irab:8-10.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَعايِشَ): In al-Miṣbāḥ: «عاش عيشا», of the pattern سار: he came to have life, so he is عائش, the feminine عائشة, and also عيّاش as an intensive form. المعيش and المعيشة are a person's earnings by which he lives; the plural is المعايش. This is on the view of the majority that it is from عاش, so the م is extra and the pattern of معايش is مفاعل; so it is not pronounced with hamza, and the Seven [readers] read it so. It was also said that it is from معش, so the م is radical, the pattern of معيش and معيشة is فعيل and فعيلة, and the pattern of معائش is فعائل, so it is pronounced with hamza. Further discussion of not pronouncing معايش with hamza will come in the Benefits section.

* I'rab:
(وَالْوَزْنُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْحَقُّ) The و is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, to establish the weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection with its true, firm balance in which the weighed thing does not go astray, to test creation, to show the judgement of justice and to establish the proof against people. الوزن is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and regarding the khabar (predicate) there are two views. One is that it is the adverb «يومئذ», i.e. "the true weighing exists, or is established, on that day", i.e. the day the messengers and those to whom they were sent are questioned; the clause to which «إذ» is annexed was omitted and the tanwīn was given in compensation for it. The discussion of this question has already been given. On this view there are several views regarding الحق: among them, that it is a naʿt (adjective) of الوزن, i.e. "the true weighing exists on that day"; and among them, that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, as if it were the answer to an implied question from someone saying:
"What is that weighing?" and it was said: "It is the truth, not falsehood." The second of the two views about the khabar of «الوزن» is that the khabar is «الحق», and on this view «يومئذ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «الوزن», i.e. "the weighing takes place on that day". (فَمَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ) The ف is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ; ثقلت is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and موازينه is the fāʿil (agent). The ف is connective for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, هم is a second mubtadaʾ, and المفلحون is the khabar of «هم»; the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative. «هم» may also be a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and المفلحون the khabar of أولئك. The clause «فأولئك هم المفلحون» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من». (وَمَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ) The clause is conjoined to the preceding clause. أولئك is a demonstrative and a mubtadaʾ, and الذين is a relative noun and the khabar; the clause is the apodosis of the jussive condition joined to the ف. The clause خسروا أنفسهم is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and أنفسهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (بِما كانُوا بِآياتِنا يَظْلِمُونَ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خسروا, and بآياتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يظلمون. يظلمون is made transitive with the ب because it includes (taḍmīn) the sense of denying. More on taḍmīn will come in the Benefits section. ما is maṣdariyya; the clause كانوا has no grammatical position because it occurs after a particle relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī), and the clause يظلمون is the khabar of كانوا. (وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَّاكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلْنا لَكُمْ فِيها مَعايِشَ) The و is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, set forth to remind them of the blessings He poured upon them which call for thanks — but they did not meet them with what they called for. The لام is [in] the answer to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). مكناهم [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «مكّنّاكم»] is a past verb and agent, and في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مكناهم. جعلنا is a verb and agent; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted [element that is the] first object of جعلنا, and معايش is the second object of جعلنا; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (قَلِيلًا ما تَشْكُرُونَ) قليلا is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted adverb; its parallels have already been given. ما is redundant (zāʾida), emphasising the littleness, and تشكرون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its agent; the clause is circumstantial or resumptive.

* Benefits:
1- Taḍmīn (implication):
It is imbuing a word with the meaning of another word, so that it is given its rule; this is called taḍmīn.
Its benefit is that one word conveys what two words convey. This is what Ibn Hishām said, and he adduced as evidence for it the saying of al-Zamakhsharī: «Do you not see how the meaning of «ولا تعد عيناك عنهم» comes back to your saying: "and let your eyes not burst forth passing beyond them to others"; and «ولا تأكلوا أموالهم إلى أموالكم», i.e. "and do not join them to your own, consuming them".» It is clear that this is a verbal richness that increases the flexibility of our language and the breadth of its usage; that is why we have favoured it with a mention.

The view of Ibn Jinnī:
Ibn Jinnī said in al-Khaṣāʾiṣ: «The Arabs may take liberties and put one particle in the place of another, to signal that this verb has the meaning of that other one only. On this basis taḍmīn is majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope), because the word is used in other than its meaning owing to a relation between the two and a contextual indicator (qarīna).»

Another view:
It was said, commenting on Ibn Jinnī's saying: in it there is a combination of the literal and the figurative, since what is mentioned indicates its meaning by itself, and the omitted [meaning] by the contextual indicator.

The view of al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salām:
Al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salām said in his book «Majāz al-Qurʾān» on taḍmīn:
It is that a noun is made to include another meaning, so as to convey the meaning of the two nouns, and you give it the other's transitivity in some places, as in His saying: «حقيق على أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق»: «حقيق» is made to include the meaning of حريص (eager), to convey that he is eager for it. And it is made to include the meaning of a verb, and you give it its transitivity in some places, as in the poet's saying «قد قتل الله زيادا عنّي» (Allah has killed Ziyād [and turned him] away from me): «قتل» is made to include the meaning of صرف (to turn away), to convey that He turned him away by the decree of killing rather than by other means; so it conveyed the meaning of killing and of turning away together.
