Remarkable instances of taḍmīn will come in the verses of Allah, so we suffice for now with what we have presented about it.

2- Replacing و and ي with hamza:
1- When one of them is final, being the third radical (lām) or an addition for assimilation (ilḥāq), after an extra alif, as in كساء, سماء and دعاء: the hamza in them is a replacement for و, and the original forms are كساو, سماو and دعاو; and as in بناء, ظباء and فناء: the hamza in them is a replacement for ي, and the original forms are بناي, ظباي and فناي.
2- When one of them is the second radical (ʿayn) of an active participle whose verb has undergone iʿlāl, as in قائل and بائع, where they changed their ʿayn to alif [in the verb].
3- When one of them occurs after the alif of «مفاعل» and was an extra long vowel in the singular, as in عجوز and عجائز, صحيفة and صحائف — unlike, for instance:
قسورة and قساور, معيشة and معايش, because the long vowel is radical in the singular, so it is not replaced. Anomalous are مصيبة and مصائب, منارة and منائر, with the replacement, although the long vowel in the singular is radical.
4- When one of them is the second of two weak letters between which the alif of مفاعل stands, whether the two weak letters are two ي's, as in نيائف, plural of نيف, or two و's, as in أوائل, plural of أول, or different, as in سيائد, plural of سيد, since its original form is سيود: و and ي met in it, the first of them preceded [vowelless], so the و was changed to ي and the ي was assimilated into the ي.
This topic is long, and we have abridged it as much as possible.

Views on reading with hamza:
When you know this, know that al-Aʿraj, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Aʿmash, and Khārija from Nāfiʿ, and Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission, read «معائش» with hamza. It is not according to the rule, as stated above, but these transmitted it and they are trustworthy, so it must be accepted.
Therefore we cite some views of the scholars of language. Al-Zajjāj:
Al-Zajjāj said: all the grammarians of Basra claim that pronouncing it with hamza is an error, and I know of no justification for it except assimilating it to صحيفة and صحائف; one should not rely on this reading.

Al-Māzinī:
Al-Māzinī said: this reading was originally taken from Nāfiʿ, and he did not know what Arabic is; the speech of the Arabs keeps the letter sound (taṣḥīḥ) in such cases.

Al-Farrāʾ:
Al-Farrāʾ said: the Arabs sometimes pronounced this and the like with hamza, imagining that it is فعيلة, so they likened مفعلة to فعيلة.

Abū Ḥayyān:
As for Abū Ḥayyān, he defended it and said: we are not bound in worship by the sayings of the grammarians of Basra. He replied to al-Māzinī and said: as for his saying that Nāfiʿ did not know what Arabic is, it is testimony to a negative — to the end of that useful discussion.

dervis-irab:11-12.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْناكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْناكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنا لِلْمَلائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ) The و is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, set forth to remind of the blessing that flows from Adam to his descendants and that calls for perpetual thankfulness. The لام is [in] the answer to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). خلقناكم is a verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay, and صورناكم is conjoined to خلقناكم. Directing the address to those addressed, although Adam is meant, serves to emphasise the sense of thankfulness for the abundant blessing. ثم قلنا للملائكة is conjoined to what preceded; للملائكة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to قلنا; اسجدوا is an imperative verb and the و is the agent; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl), and لآدم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to His saying اسجدوا. (فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُنْ مِنَ السَّاجِدِينَ) The ف is for sequence with immediate succession, as though they complied with the command the moment it was issued. سجدوا is a verb and agent; إلا is a particle of exception, and إبليس is excepted (mustathnā) from the agent of سجدوا. The clause لم يكن من الساجدين is either resumptive, as if it were the answer to an implied question, or it may be circumstantial (ḥāliyya), i.e. "except Iblīs, in the state of refusing to prostrate". من الساجدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of يكن. (قالَ ما مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ) ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause منعك is in the position of the nominative as its khabar; the meaning is: "What thing prevented you?" أن and what follows it are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. "What prevented you from prostrating?" إذ is a past adverb attached to تسجد, i.e. "What prevented you from prostrating at the time I commanded you to do so?"
لا is redundant (zāʾida), emphasising the sense of negation, and the clause أمرتك is in the position of the genitive by annexation (as muḍāf ilayhi). (قالَ: أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِي مِنْ نارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِنْ طِينٍ) The clause of saying is resumptive, set forth for Iblīs's answer to the question arising from the account of his not prostrating. أنا is a mubtadaʾ and خير the khabar; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خير. The clause خلقتني has no grammatical position because it is set forth to give the reason for his superiority over Adam, which he claimed out of delusion and arrogance. من نار is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلقتني, and the clause خلقتني من طين [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «وخلقته من طين»] is conjoined to the one before it.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ما منعك أن لا تسجد إذ أمرتك» there is the device of tawhīm (creating a false impression), which has been touched upon before. That is, the speaker brings a word such that what follows it in the speech gives the impression that the speaker intended a mis-dotting of it (taṣḥīf), or an alteration of it (taḥrīf), or a different i'rab, or a different meaning. For the apparent meaning is "What prevented you from prostrating?" The interpretation that answers this speech is that the scholars said: «ما منعك» means "What made you refuse to prostrate?" His saying in Āl ʿImrān has already been given regarding a different i'rab: «ثم لا ينصرون», so that the verb remains indicating the present and the future. Among the instances of creating the impression of mis-dotting is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
وإن الفيام التي حوله ... لتحسد أرجلها الأرؤس
(The throngs around him — their heads envy their feet [for standing nearer him].)
The word «الأرجل» (feet) gave the hearer the impression that al-Mutanabbī meant القيام (those standing), with ق, whereas what he meant is الفيام, with ف, which are the throngs; because الفيام applies to the smallest plural, the hyperbole would be lost from it. [Translator's note: so in the source; the final clause seems to mean that reading القيام would lose the hyperbole, and the wording appears garbled.]

dervis-irab:59-64.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمَلَأُ): the nobles and the chiefs; it has also been said: men with no women among them.
In al-Miṣbāḥ: «الملأ, with hamza: the nobles of the people. They were so called because of their sufficiency (ملاءة) in the kindness and sound judgment that is sought from them, or because they fill (يملؤون) the eyes with grandeur and the breasts with awe. The plural is أملاء, like سبب and أسباب». In al-Asās: «قام به الملأ والأملاء» — the nobles who join together (يتمالؤون) in misfortunes.
[The poet] said:
وقال لها الأملاء من كل معشر ... وخير أقاويل الرجال سديدها
(The notables of every clan spoke to her — and the best of men's sayings is the soundest.)
«وما كان هذا الأمر عن ملأ منّا», i.e. [this affair was not] by our joint agreement and consultation. From it [also]: «هو مليء بكذا»: he is equal to it. «وعليها ملاءة الحسن» (she wears the mantle of beauty). Ibn Mayyāda said:
بذّتهم ميالة تميد ... ملاءة الحسن لها جديد
(A swaying, graceful girl outshone them; the mantle of beauty on her is new.)
A young Arab flirted with a town woman, and she was stingy with herself towards him, so he said to her: By Allah, you have neither the mantle of beauty, nor its pillar, nor its hooded cloak, so what is this refusal?

* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ) Resumptive speech introduced to mention stories of the earlier prophets as a consolation for the Prophet ﷺ, so that he may take as a model those before him, and despair may not erode him nor any slackness or weakness trouble him in conveying his message.
The lām is [in] the answer to the omitted oath; the Arabs hardly ever pronounce this lām except with قد. أرسلنا نوحا is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إلى قومه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أرسلنا. (فَقالَ: يا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; يا is a vocative particle; قوم is a vocative (munādā) annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person, as the kasra shows; اعبدوا is an imperative verb, the wāw its fāʿil and الله its object; ما is negating; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; إله is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject) in position; غيره is a naʿt (adjective) of «إله» according to the position, as though it were said: you have no god other than Him. The clause اعبدوا الله is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech), and the clause مالكم من إله غيره is resumptive. (إِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ) The clause gives the reason for the command to worship and has no grammatical position. إنّ and its noun; the clause أخاف is its khabar; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخاف; عذاب is a mafʿūl bihi; يوم is muḍāf ilayhi; عظيم is an adjective. (قالَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ: إِنَّا لَنَراكَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ)
Resumptive speech introduced to set out the reply of his people. قال الملأ is a verb and its agent; من قومه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause إنّ and what falls within its scope is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl. إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); نراك is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the khabar of «إنّ»; في ضلال is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نراك as the second object of seeing — the seeing here is mental (qalbiyya); مبين is an adjective. (قالَ: يا قَوْمِ لَيْسَ بِي ضَلالَةٌ) Resumptive speech introduced to set out Nūḥ's reply to them; it is among the finest and most eloquent of speech. ليس is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; بي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of ليس; ضلالة is its delayed noun. (وَلكِنِّي رَسُولٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; لكنّ and its noun — it has come in the best possible place, because it stands between two contradictories; رسول is the khabar of لكنّ; من رب العالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of رسول. (أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسالاتِ رَبِّي وَأَنْصَحُ لَكُمْ) Resumptive speech introduced to affirm his mission and detail its rulings and task. The clause may also be a second adjective of رسول; but he took account of the preceding first-person pronoun and said أبلغكم; had he taken account of the overt noun after it, he would have said يبلغكم. The kāf is the first object of أبلغكم and رسالات ربي its second object; أنصح لكم is conjoined to أبلغكم. It is known that «نصح» is transitive by itself and with the lām: one says نصحه and نصح له. (وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ اللَّهِ ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ) Conjoined to أبلغكم; من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعلم, and something omitted must be implied, i.e. from His direction; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi; the clause لا تعلمون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, having no grammatical position. (أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ أَنْ جاءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَلى رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ) Conjoined to what preceded, introduced in the style of the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī) with the hamza. The wāw is a conjunction; عجبتم is conjoined to an omitted [verb] that must be implied, i.e. did you give the lie and wonder? أن is a maṣdariyya particle governing the accusative, and it together with what it governs is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. «من أن جاءكم» (at a reminder having come to you); ذكر is the fāʿil; من ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of ذكر or to جاءكم; على رجل is an adjective of ذكر, and something omitted must be implied, i.e. on the tongue of a man; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of رجل, i.e. from among you and of your kind — because they used to wonder at the sending of human beings, and say: «لو شاء الله لأنزل ملائكة ما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين». (لِيُنْذِرَكُمْ وَلِتَتَّقُوا وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ) The lām gives the reason for the coming; ينذركم is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl); لتتقوا is conjoined to لينذركم; the clause of hope is circumstantial; the clause ترحمون is the khabar of لعل. He made the reasons for the coming of the reminder on the tongue of a man from among them three:
the first, لينذركم; the second, لتتقوا; the third, لعلكم ترحمون. This is a fine ordering, reaching the utmost of excellence and beauty. (فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ فِي الْفُلْكِ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, because it occurs as the apodosis of an omitted condition, i.e.
if you wish to know the outcome of their affair, they gave him the lie. كذبوه is a verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi; فأنجيناه is conjoined to فكذبوه; the wāw is of accompaniment (maʿiyya), and الذين is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), though you may conjoin it to the hāʾ; معه is an adverb of place attached to the omitted ṣila of the relative, i.e. who were settled with him in the ark; في الفلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the [notion of] settledness contained in الملك [Translator's note: so in the source; probably «in the adverb»], i.e. to what the adverb is attached to, or to أنجيناه. (وَأَغْرَقْنَا الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا) Conjoined to what preceded; أغرقنا الذين is a verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause كذبوا is the ṣila; بآياتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كذبوا. (إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَوْماً عَمِينَ) The clause gives the reason for their destruction mentioned before, i.e. they perished because of blindness in their insight.
إنّ and its noun; the clause كانوا is its khabar; قوما is the khabar of كانوا; عمين is an adjective of «قوما».

* Rhetoric:
1- The majāz mursal (metonymic trope):
In His words, the Exalted: «إنا لنراك في ضلال مبين» and His words «ليس بي ضلالة», He made error a container, while error is not a container in which a person can dwell,
because it is an abstract notion; one dwells only in its place. So using error for its place is a majāz mursal in which the thing contained (al-ḥāll) is mentioned and the place (al-maḥall) is meant; its relation is containedness (al-ḥāliyya), and its benefit is exaggeration in describing him with error and his being deeply sunk in it, as though he were settled in its darknesses, unable to move out of them. They increased the exaggeration by emphasizing it, opening the sentence with إنّ and adding the lām to its khabar.

2- Negating the more specific and the more general:
He followed that with His words «ليس بي ضلالة» to overturn what they claimed and to refute what they imagined. It is among the finest, most eloquent and most victorious of replies against an opponent, because he denied that a single [act of] error clung to him, let alone that error encompassed him; so he did not say ضلال, as they had said and as the context would require. Al-Zamakhsharī's imagination leapt, and he decided that ضلالة is more specific than ضلال, and so it was more emphatic in denying error of himself, as though he said: there is nothing of error in me, just as if you were asked: Do you have dates (تمر)? and you said: I do not have a single date (ثمرة) [Translator's note: the source prints «ثمرة» with thāʾ]. But al-Zamakhsharī overlooked a very important point in this great discussion: the negation of the more specific is more general than the negation of the more general, so it does not necessarily entail it, since the more general does not entail the more specific, unlike the reverse. Do you not see that if you say "this is not a human being", that does not entail its not being an animal, whereas if you say "this is not an animal", it entails its not being a human being?
So the negation of the more general, as you see, is more emphatic than the negation of the more specific. This being established, the precise answer is to say: ضلالة is lower and less than ضلال, because it is applied only to a single act of it, whereas ضلال applies to a little or much of its kind; and the negation of the lower is more emphatic than the negation of the higher — not in that it is more specific, but in that the lower draws attention to the higher, as we established at the start of this discussion.

* Benefits:
1- A noun preceded by a pronoun:
Every noun preceded by a pronoun of the present person, first or second person, allows two treatments: the first, taking account of the preceding pronoun; the second, taking account of the overt noun. You say: أنا رجل أفعل كذا (I am a man who does such-and-such), taking account of the pronoun «أنا»; and if you wish you say: يفعل كذا, taking account of رجل. Likewise: أنت رجل تفعل العجائب and يفعل العجائب, in the second and the third person. Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said:
أنا الذي سمّتن أمي حيدره ... كليث غابات كريه المنظرة
(I am the one whom my mother named Ḥaydara, like a lion of the thickets, fearsome to behold.) [Translator's note: the source prints «سمّتن»; the usual wording is «سمّتني».]
He said it when he fought the Jew «Marḥab» in single combat on the day of Khaybar. The Jew had said:
قد علمت خيبر أنّي مرحب ... شاكي السلاح بطل مجرب
(Khaybar knows that I am Marḥab, fully armed, a tried hero.)
And ʿAlī answered him with that. His mother Fāṭima bint Asad had named him after her father, because Ḥaydara is one of the names of the lion (asad). When Abū Ṭālib came, he named him ʿAlī.
The lion is called Ḥaydara because of the force with which it rushes down on what it attacks. الليث is a primitive (jāmid) noun for the lion, and they derived from it لايثه, i.e. he treated him as a lion would.
الغاب is its lair in which it hides. The apparent [form] would have been to say "the one whom his mother named", so that the pronoun matches its referent, which is the relative noun, in the third person; but he brought the first-person pronoun, going by the meaning, and the preceding first-person pronoun made it fitting, i.e.:
I am the brave one on whom the signs of courage appeared from my childhood, so my mother named me with the name of the lion, and I do not belie her expectation.
Ibn Jinnī criticised Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī for his line:
أنا الذي نظر الأعمى إلى أدبي ... وأسمعت كلماتي من به صمم
(I am the one whose literary art the blind man has looked at, and whose words have made the deaf hear.)
for departing from the third-person wording; but the noble verse suffices to justify what Abū al-Ṭayyib used.

2- The lām that comes before قد:
The Arabs hardly ever pronounce this lām except with «قد»; rare from them is the like of the words of Imruʾ al-Qays:
حلفت لها بالله حلفة فاجر ... لناموا فما إن من حديث ولا صال
(I swore to her by Allah the oath of a liar: they have fallen asleep, and there is no one talking and no one warming at the fire.)
That is because, since the oath-sentence is only introduced to emphasize the sentence sworn upon, which is its answer, it is a likely place for the sense of expectation, which is the meaning of «قد», when the addressee hears the word of the oath. Ibn al-Rūmī, the Abbasid poet, followed the model of Imruʾ al-Qays in his words:
لرأينا مستيقظين أمورا ... حسبنا أن تكون رؤيا منام
(We have seen, while awake, things we reckoned to be dreams of sleep.)
It has also been said: when an oath is answered by an affirmative, inflected past verb, then if it is near to the present, both the lām and قد are brought, e.g. «تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا»; and if it is remote, the lām alone is brought, as in the words of Imruʾ al-Qays mentioned above and the words of Ibn al-Rūmī.

dervis-irab:13-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الصَّاغِرِينَ): الصّغار, with fatḥa on the ص: humiliation and abasement. «صغر الرجل», of the pattern طرب, so he is صاغر; الصاغر is also one who accepts abasement.
(أَنْظِرْنِي): grant me respite.

* I'rab:
(قالَ فَاهْبِطْ مِنْها فَما يَكُونُ لَكَ أَنْ تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيها) The clause of saying is resumptive. فاهبط: the ف is a conjunction, making the command consequent upon the disobedience that appeared from Iblīs. فما: the ف is also a conjunction, and «ما» is also negating; يكون is a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb, because it includes the sense of ينبغي (it is fitting) or يصح (it is valid). لك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to يكون, because it includes the sense of يصح; أن together with what it governs is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the fāʿil (agent) of يكون, and فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَاخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ الصَّاغِرِينَ) The ف is a conjunction, emphasising the command to descend. إنّ and its noun; من الصاغرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar (predicate); the clause إنّ and what falls in its scope is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "humiliated and abased". (قالَ أَنْظِرْنِي إِلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ) The clause of saying is resumptive, and the clause أنظرني is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). إلى يوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنظرني, and the clause يبعثون is in the position of the genitive by annexation (as muḍāf ilayhi); that is why the adverb was declined, because it is annexed to a declinable clause [i.e. one headed by a declinable verb], as stated before. يبعثون is a passive imperfect verb, and the و is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (قالَ إِنَّكَ مِنَ الْمُنْظَرِينَ) The clause إنك من المنظرين is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying. (قالَ فَبِما أَغْوَيْتَنِي لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِراطَكَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ) The clause is also resumptive. The ف is a conjunction, the ب is a preposition of cause, and ما is maṣdariyya; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted verb of the oath. The preposition and its genitive noun may not be attached to «أقعدن», because the lām of the oath prevents that: we do not say «والله لأمرن بزيد». The meaning is: "Because of Your leading me astray, I swear…" The ب may also be [the particle] of the oath, i.e. "I swear by Your leading me astray, I will surely sit…"; it, with its genitive noun, is attached to its omitted verb. The لام occurs in the answer to the omitted oath, and أقعدن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis. لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أقعدن; صراطك is accusative as an adverb of place, and more on its i'rab will come in the Benefits section; المستقيم is an adjective (ṣifa).

* Benefits:
Sībawayh said in his Book: «صراطك» is accusative as an adverb, i.e.
"on Your straight path". Sībawayh also reported: «ضرب زيد الظهر والبطن» (Zayd was struck [on] the back and the belly).
Abū Ḥayyān preferred its being accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ).

The words of Abū Ḥayyān:
«صراطك is accusative by dropping «على»; al-Zajjāj said this, and likened it to the Arabs' saying «ضرب زيد الظهر والبطن», i.e. on the back and the belly.
Dropping the preposition is not regular (lā yanqās) in the like of this: one does not say «قعدت الخشبة» meaning "on the wood". They said: [it is accusative] as an adverb, as the poet said regarding it: «كما عسل الطريق الثعلب». This too is an interpretation with weakness in it, because «صراطك» is a specific adverb of place, as is الطريق, so the verb does not reach it except through «في»; whatever comes contrary to that is anomalous or poetic licence.» Until he says:
«The better course is that لأقعدنّ be made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of a verb that is transitive by itself, so that «الصراط» is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the implied form being: "I will surely keep to Your straight path by my sitting."» [Translator's note: the source does not close this quotation mark.]

Al-Zamakhsharī agreed with Sībawayh:
As for al-Zamakhsharī, he agreed with Sībawayh. He said: «Its being accusative is as an adverb, as in the saying of Sāʿida ibn Juʾayya describing a spear:
لدن بهز الكفّ يعسل متنه ... فيه كما عسل الطريق الثعلب
(Supple, its shaft quivers with the shaking of the hand, as the fox runs quivering along the road.)
He describes it as supple, its hard shaft quivering because of its being shaken, so there is no stiffness in it, just as the fox «عسل», i.e. ran quivering, on the road. He omitted the preposition from the second [i.e. الطريق] out of poetic necessity.
In «عسل» there is the meaning of entering quickly. [Translator's note: the source does not close the quotation mark of al-Zamakhsharī's passage.]

dervis-irab:17-18.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَذْؤُماً): In al-Mukhtār: الذّأم is a defect; it is pronounced with hamza and without hamza [Translator's note: the source has «ولا يهز», evidently for «ولا يهمز»]. One says «ذأمه», of the pattern قطع, when he found fault with him and despised him, so he is مذءوم.
(مَدْحُوراً): «دحره»: he drove him away and banished him; its pattern is قطع.

* I'rab:
(ثُمَّ لَآتِيَنَّهُمْ مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ وَعَنْ أَيْمانِهِمْ وَعَنْ شَمائِلِهِمْ) ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; the لام prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam). آتينهم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, and the ه is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). من بين أيديهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to آتينهم, i.e. "I will come at them from the four directions from which an enemy comes". But he varied the two prepositions: he made the verb transitive with من in the first two, which is for the starting point, and with عن in the last two, which is for passing beyond, because [the comer] heads straight from the first two and swerves from the last two, passing aside. More detail will come in the Rhetoric section. (وَلا تَجِدُ أَكْثَرَهُمْ شاكِرِينَ) The و is resumptive or a conjunction, so the clause after it is resumptive or conjoined. لا is negating, and تجد is an imperfect verb, either from وجود in the sense of meeting, so it is transitive to one object, «أكثرهم» being a direct object and شاكرين a ḥāl (circumstantial); or from وجود in the sense of knowing, so His saying «شاكرين» is a second direct object. (قالَ: اخْرُجْ مِنْها مَذْؤُماً مَدْحُوراً) The clause is resumptive. أخرج [Translator's note: so in the source, for «اخرج»] is an imperative verb; منها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اخرج; مذءوما and مدحورا are two ḥāls of the agent of اخرج; and the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (لَمَنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنْكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) The لام is the one preparing for the omitted oath; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative; تبعك is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. لأملأن: the لام is [in] the answer to the oath indicated by the preparatory lām; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the answer to the oath indicates it, and the oath clause is resumptive.
The لام may also be the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and من a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause تبعك is the ṣila (relative clause), and لأملأن is the answer to an omitted oath; that oath and its answer are in the position of the nominative [as the khabar] of the mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: "As for whoever follows you among them — by Allah, I will surely fill Hell with you." جهنم is a direct object, منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أملأن, and أجمعين is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is the device of varying the two prepositions. He mentioned the four directions because they are the ones from which an enemy comes at his enemy; that is why he left out above and below. He made the verb transitive to the first two directions with من and to the last two with عن, because one who comes from in front and behind usually heads [at you] with his whole self, and one who comes from the right and left usually comes at a slant; so for the first two transitivity with the particle of starting point was fitting, and for the last two transitivity with the particle of passing beyond. It is a representation (tamthīl) of his whispering and his making [evil] seem fair as one who actually comes [at them].
A splendid passage by al-Zamakhsharī:
Below is a splendid passage by al-Zamakhsharī on this matter, from which we quote the following paragraphs for the vivid embodiment they contain. He said: «If you say: how is it said «من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم» with the particle of starting point, and «وعن أيمانهم وعن شمائلهم» with the particle of passing beyond? I say: the verb is made transitive to the adverbial object (mafʿūl fīhi) in the same way as it is made transitive to the direct object; just as the particles of transitivity differ in that, they differ in this. It was language that is taken [as heard] and not derived by analogy; one only investigates the soundness of its placement. When we heard them say «جلس عن يمينه» and «على يمينه», and «عن شماله» and «على شماله», we said: the meaning of «على يمينه» is that he established himself on the right side as what is above is established over what it is above; and the meaning of «عن يمينه» is that he sat keeping apart from the one on the right, turned aside from him, not adjoining him. Then it became frequent until it was used of one keeping apart and others. Similar to it, of the direct object, is their saying: «رميت عن القوس، وعلى القوس، ومن القوس» (I shot from the bow, upon the bow, and out of the bow), because the arrow goes away from it, is above it when placed on its grip for shooting, and the shooting begins from it. Likewise they said «جلس بين يديه وخلفه» (he sat before him and behind him) in the sense of "in", because they are two adverbs of the action; and «من بين يديه ومن خلفه», because the action occurs in part of the two directions; you say «جئته من الليل» (I came to him by night), meaning part of the night.» [Translator's note: the source has «تربد يعض», evidently misprints for «تريد بعض», and «التغدية» for «التعدية».]

dervis-irab:65-68.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سَفاهَةٍ): ignorance, lack of forbearance and feebleness of mind.

* I'rab:
(وَإِلى عادٍ أَخاهُمْ هُوداً) The wāw is a conjunction; إلى عاد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb conjoined to أرسلنا; أخاهم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أرسلنا; هودا is a full-correspondence badal (substitute) of «أخاهم». (قالَ: يا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ) The conjunction has been omitted from «قال», unlike the first verse in the story of Nūḥ. The secret in that is that the conjunction strings sentences together until it makes them like a single sentence, so it was avoided because each of them was intended to be independent in its meaning. The sentence of the vocative and the command is maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech). (ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ) The clause is resumptive; the i'rab of its exact like has been given before. (أَفَلا تَتَّقُونَ) The hamza is for the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī) and الاستعباد [Translator's note: so in the source; probably الاستبعاد, "finding it far-fetched"] at their not guarding against the punishment after they knew what befell the people of Nūḥ. The fāʾ conjoins to something implied, i.e. Do you not reflect? or Are you heedless, and so do not fear? لا is negating; تتقون is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (قالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ) Resumptive speech introduced to set out what his people answered to his call. قال الملأ is a verb and its agent; الذين is a naʿt (adjective); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); من قومه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). He described the notables here but did not describe the notables in the story of Nūḥ because among Hūd's nobles there were some who believed in him — among them, as is related, Marthad ibn Saʿd, who became Muslim and used to conceal his Islam — so a distinction by description was intended; whereas among the nobles of Nūḥ's people there was no believer. It is also possible that the description was given to record blame, describing them with sheer disbelief and charging them with what rational people disown. (إِنَّا لَنَراكَ فِي سَفاهَةٍ) The clause إنّ and what falls within its scope is in the position of the accusative as the object of the notables' saying. إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause نراك is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; في سفاهة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, or [is] a second mafʿūl bihi if the seeing is mental (qalbiyya) — and perhaps this is the better. (وَإِنَّا لَنَظُنُّكَ مِنَ الْكاذِبِينَ) Conjoined to what preceded; the i'rab of its like has been given before. (قالَ يا قَوْمِ لَيْسَ بِي سَفاهَةٌ) Resumptive speech introduced to set out Hūd's reply, and what follows is the object of his saying. ليس is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; بي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted fronted khabar; سفاهة is its delayed noun. (وَلكِنِّي رَسُولٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The wāw is circumstantial; لكنّ and its noun; رسول is its khabar. It is a rectification (istidrāk) of what preceded, in view of what it entails of his being at the utmost limit of right guidance. من رب العالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of رسول. (أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسالاتِ رَبِّي) Its i'rab was given shortly before. (وَأَنَا لَكُمْ ناصِحٌ أَمِينٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; أنا is a mubtadaʾ (subject); لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ناصح; ناصح is the first khabar of أنا and أمين the second khabar of أنا; it may also be parsed as an adjective of ناصح.

* Rhetoric:
1- The majāz mursal (metonymic trope):
In making foolishness a container, by way of majāz mursal; its relation is containedness (al-ḥāliyya), as was said earlier on the verse of Nūḥ, namely «إنا لنراك في ضلال مبين». What was said there about opening the sentence with إنّ and adding the shifted lām to its khabar is said here, so refresh your memory of it.

2- Turning to the nominal sentence:
In the story of Hūd He brought the nominal sentence, saying «وأنا لكم ناصح أمين», while in the story of Nūḥ He brought the verbal sentence, saying «وأنصح لكم». That is because the verb form indicates renewal hour after hour, and Nūḥ repeated his call night and day without pause, so the verbal expression was fitting; whereas Hūd was not like that, time after time, so it was expressed of him with the nominal [sentence].

3- Kināya (allusion):
That is in His words: «قال: يا قوم ليس بي سفاهة ولكني رسول من رب العالمين»; he alluded to their giving him the lie in their words to Hūd, peace be upon him:
«إنا لنراك في سفاهة». It has been discussed many times before, so refresh your memory of it.

dervis-irab:69-69.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَصْطَةً): with fatḥa on the bāʾ, i.e. strength and stature. In the lexicons:
البسطة, with fatḥa on the bāʾ: amplitude, stature and perfection; بسطة العيش: ease of living.
(آلاءَ): a plural whose singular is إِلْي, with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the lām, like حمل and أحمال; or أُلْي, with ḍamma on the hamza and sukūn on the lām, like قفل and أقفال; or إِلَى, with kasra on the hamza and fatḥa on the lām, like عنب and أعناب; or أَلًى, with fatḥa on the hamza and the lām, like قفا and أفقاء [Translator's note: so in the source; the plural of قفا is أقفاء].

* I'rab:
(أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ أَنْ جاءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَلى رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ لِيُنْذِرَكُمْ) The hamza is for the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī), meant as prohibition, i.e. do not wonder, and reflect on your affair. The wāw is a conjunction; عجبتم is a past verb conjoined to an omitted [verb] indicated by the context of the speech, i.e. did you give the lie or wonder? The omitted [clause] is resumptive, introduced to forbid them from persisting in what they are upon. أن جاءكم is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) عجبتم, i.e.:
or did you wonder at the coming of a reminder from your Lord. ذكر is the fāʿil (agent) of جاءكم; من ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ذكر; على رجل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of ذكر, i.e. spoken on the tongue of a man; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of رجل. In لينذركم the lām is the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl); ينذركم is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām of cause; the maṣdar is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جاءكم. (وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفاءَ مِنْ بَعْدِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the sentence is ranged with what preceded it to set out the order of the matters of sincere counsel, trustworthiness and warning. إذ is accusative as an object, not as an adverb, i.e. remember the time of the said appointing, because the situation is one of embodying and evoking the picture in all its details, as though it were set up before them from which they draw all manner of admonitions and lessons. In any case, the sentence is conjoined to something implied, as though it were said: do not wonder, or reflect on your affair, gain insight and remember. The clause جعلكم is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of جعلكم and خلفاء the second mafʿūl bihi; من بعد قوم نوح is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of خلفاء. (وَزادَكُمْ فِي الْخَلْقِ بَصْطَةً) Conjoined to جعلكم; في الخلق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); بسطة is the second mafʿūl bihi of زادكم, or a tamyīz (specification), the kāf being the first object. (فَاذْكُرُوا آلاءَ اللَّهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, because it occurs as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if you have known this with true knowledge, reflected on it and gained insight into its outcomes and hidden aspects, then remember. آلاء الله is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause of hope is circumstantial; the clause تفلحون is the khabar (predicate) of لعل.

dervis-irab:19-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وسوس): الوسوسة is hidden, repeated speech; likewise الوسواس, which is [also] the sound of jewellery. الوسوسة is also an evil passing thought. وسوس is not transitive to an object but intransitive; one says «هو رجل موسوس» with kasra on the [second] و, and one does not say it with fatḥa. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said this. Someone else said: one says «موسوس له» and «موسوس إليه». Al-Layth said: الوسوسة is the talk of the soul, and the hidden sound of a wind shaking a branch and the like, like a whisper.
Al-Azharī said: وسوس and وزوز have one meaning. In al-Qāmūs: «رجل موزوز», i.e. one who warbles. The secret of the repetition of letters will come in the Rhetoric section.
(وُورِيَ): it was concealed and covered. It is a passive past verb, originally:
وارى, like ضارب; when it was made passive, the alif was changed to و, like ضورب.
(السوآت): the private parts, and everything of which one is ashamed.

* I'rab:
(وَيا آدَمُ اسْكُنْ أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ الْجَنَّةَ) The و is a conjunction or resumptive. يا is a vocative particle, and آدم is the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of the accusative. The statement is conjoined to اخرج, or [it is] with an implied governing agent, i.e. "We said: O Adam". اسكن is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being أنت; أنت is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent agent, and زوجك is conjoined to the latent pronoun. الجنة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); this has already been given. (فَكُلا مِنْ حَيْثُ شِئْتُما) The ف is a conjunction; كلا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the ن, and the alif is the agent. من is a preposition, and حيث is an adverb of place, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of the genitive by من; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to كلا, and the clause شئتما is in the position of the genitive by annexation (as muḍāf ilayhi). (وَلا تَقْرَبا هذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونا مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ) The و is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تقربا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; the alif is the agent. هذه is a demonstrative in the position of the accusative as a direct object; قرب is used intransitively and transitively, as here. الشجرة is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative. فتكونا: the ف is causative (al-sababiyya), and تكونا is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the ف because it occurs as an answer to the prohibition; the alif is the noun of تكونا, and من الظالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of تكونا. (فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا الشَّيْطانُ لِيُبْدِيَ لَهُما ما وُورِيَ عَنْهُما مِنْ سَوْآتِهِما) The ف is a conjunction, وسوس is a past verb, لهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to وسوس, and الشيطان is the agent. ليبدي: the لام is the causal lām, and يبدي is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the لام; it may validly also be the lām of becoming (al-ṣayrūra) or of outcome (al-ʿāqiba). لهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يبدي; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a direct object; the clause ووري is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position; عنهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ووري; and من سوءاتهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَقالَ: ما نَهاكُما رَبُّكُما عَنْ هذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونا مِنَ الْخالِدِينَ) The و is a conjunction, and قال is a past verb conjoined to وسوس. ما is negating; نهاكما is a past verb, the ك is a direct object, and the م and alif are two particles indicating the dual; ربكما is the agent. عن هذه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نهاكما, and الشجرة is a badal of the demonstrative. إلا is a particle of restriction. أن and what falls in its scope are an "emptied" exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the most general of reasons; so it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "except out of dislike [that]". أن تكونا is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by annexation; تكونا is a defective imperfect verb, accusative by أن; the alif is its noun, and ملكين is the khabar of تكونا. أو تكونا من الخالدين is conjoined to the first clause تكونا, and the clause ما نهاكما is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).

* Rhetoric:
The secret of the repetition of letters in a single word:
This is one of the chapters of rhetoric that few notice. Al-Zamakhsharī touched upon it in his Kashshāf, Ibn al-Athīr in his al-Mathal al-Sāʾir, and Ibn Jinnī in his Khaṣāʾiṣ.
But their touching upon it does not go beyond the language of theory that does not quench thirst or cure burning thirst. This chapter can be summed up thus: whenever letters are repeated in a single word, that signals repetition of the action, and the transfer of the verb from one pattern to another, to which the [founder of the language] [Translator's note: the source has «الواضح», evidently for «الواضع» (the founder/coiner)] originally inclined only for this hidden secret. The word here is «وسوس»; it is a living embodiment and an eloquent depiction of Iblīs's persistence in leading astray and his exerting himself to make their foot slip and make them crash into the slippery slopes of evil; so he whispers to them time after time.
Among such cases is their saying خشن and اخشوشن: خشن does not convey what the word اخشوشن conveys, because of the repetition of letters in it. Say the like of this about «أعشب المكان» and «اعشوشب» (the place became grassy / became very grassy): it is as if, when they saw the abundance of grass, they said اعشوشب.
We will encounter remarkable instances of it in the Noble Quran, as in this verse.
A poetic model of repetition:
It is good for us here to cite now a poetic model in which the poet clung to the train of this hidden secret, namely the saying of al-Buḥturī, from an ode praising al-Mutawakkil ʿalā Allāh and mentioning the account of the reconciliation between the paternal and maternal cousins of Banū Taghlib, including his saying:
رفعت بضبعي تغلب بنة وائل ... وقد يئست أن يستقلّ صريعها
فكنت أمين الله مولى حياتها ... ومولاك فتح يوم ذاك شفيعها
تألّفتهم من بعد ما شرّدت بهم ... حفائظ أخلاق بطيء رجوعها
فأبصر غاويها المحجّة فاهتدى ... وأقصر غاليها ودانى شسوعها
(You raised up by the arms Taghlib, daughter of Wāʾil, when she had despaired that her fallen one would ever rise; you, the trustee of Allah, were the patron of her life, and your client Fatḥ was her intercessor that day. You brought them together after rancours of character, slow to return, had scattered them; so her straying one saw the clear road and was guided, her extremist desisted, and her distant one drew near.)
The place of evidence is his saying «تألّفتهم من بعد ما شردت بهم»: the doubling in تألّفتهم and شرّدت بهم is something the situation requires, because it is a situation of reconciliation and of restoring the waters to their courses between the paternal and maternal cousins. What has been given suffices us for now. What supports it and shows the place of its beauty will come elsewhere.

dervis-irab:70-72.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الدابر): the last. Cutting off the دابر means extirpation, because if the last is cut off, what was before it has been cut off, and so extirpation has taken place.

* I'rab:
(قالُوا: أَجِئْتَنا لِنَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ وَحْدَهُ وَنَذَرَ ما كانَ يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا) Resumptive speech introduced [to show them] reproaching him for his coming. They meant coming from his place of devotion, i.e. the place to which he withdrew for worship; or they did not mean actual coming but meant by it simply setting about and undertaking [the matter], as one says «ذهب ليشتمني» (he went to insult me), where actual going is not meant — and perhaps this is the more eloquent and clearer. The hamza is for the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī); جئتنا is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the lām is of cause (taʿlīl); نعبد is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) جئتنا; الله is its object; وحده is an interpreted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. alone; نذر is an imperfect verb conjoined to نعبد; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); the clause يعبد آباؤنا [Translator's note: the source prints «بعبد»] is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كان; and the clause كان and what falls within its scope is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative. (فَأْتِنا بِما تَعِدُنا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa; ائت is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as an object; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ائتنا»; the clause تعدنا is the ṣila of the relative; إن is conditional; كنت is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); كان and its noun; من الصادقين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar; the apodosis of إن is omitted because what precedes indicates it, i.e. then bring us. (قال: قد وقع عليكم رجس من ربكم وغضب) Resumptive speech introduced to set out Hūd's reply to his people. قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); وقع is a past verb; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to وقع; رجس is the fāʿil; من ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of رجس; غضب is conjoined to رجس; the clause قد and what falls within its scope is maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech), i.e. the punishment has become due upon you and binding, or it has descended upon you: he made what is expected equivalent to what has actually occurred. Of this kind is what is related of Ḥassān ibn Thābit: his son was stung by a hornet when he was a child, and he came crying. He said:
"My son, what is the matter with you?" He said: "A little bird stung me, as though it were wrapped in two striped Yemeni cloaks." So he hugged him to his breast and said to him: "My son, you have composed poetry!" (أَتُجادِلُونَنِي فِي أَسْماءٍ سَمَّيْتُمُوها أَنْتُمْ وَآباؤُكُمْ) The hamza is for the disapproving interrogative, and to declare repugnant their objecting to his coming to call them to the worship of Allah and the abandonment of idols.
تجادلونني is an imperfect verb, its agent and its object; في أسماء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجادلونني; the clause سميتموها is an adjective of أسماء, the wāw being for the full lengthening of the ḍamma; أنتم is a tawkīd (emphasis); آباؤكم is conjoined to أنتم. (ما نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ بِها مِنْ سُلْطانٍ فَانْتَظِرُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ) The clause ما نزّل is a second adjective of أسماء; بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نزل, or to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of سلطان, and when it was fronted it was parsed as a ḥāl; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; سلطان is genitive in form and accusative as an object in position. In فانتظروا the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, and انتظروا is an imperative verb and its agent; إنّ and its noun; معكم is an adverb attached to المنتظرين; من المنتظرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of إنّ. (فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنَّا) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, as in His word فانفجرت, i.e. then what happened happened, and We saved him. أنجيناه is a verb, its agent and its object; الذين is conjoined to the hāʾ in أنجيناه, or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); معه is an adverb of place attached to the omitted ṣila; برحمة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنجيناه; منّا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of رحمة. (وَقَطَعْنا دابِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَما كانُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ) Conjoined to أنجيناه; دابر is a mafʿūl bihi; الذين is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause كذبوا is the ṣila, having no grammatical position; ما كانوا is conjoined to كذبوا; مؤمنين is the khabar of كانوا.

* Benefits:
The story of ʿĀd:
History relates that ʿĀd spread out in the land between ʿUmān and Ḥaḍramawt. They had idols that they worshipped, namely Ṣuddāʾ, Ṣumūd and al-Habāʾ. So Allah sent them Hūd as a prophet, from the middlemost of them and the best of them in lineage. They gave him the lie and increased in insolence and tyranny, so Allah withheld the rain from them for three years until they were exhausted. When affliction befell people, they used to ask Allah the Exalted for relief from it at His Sacred House; and the people of Mecca at that time were the Amalekites, the sons of ʿImlīq ibn Lāwadh ibn Sām ibn Nūḥ, and their chief was Muʿāwiya ibn Bakr. ʿĀd dispatched to Mecca seventy men from among their best, among them Qayl ibn ʿItr and Marthad ibn Saʿd, who used to conceal his Islam. When they arrived, they stayed with Muʿāwiya ibn Bakr, who was on the outskirts of Mecca, outside the Sanctuary. He lodged them and honoured them — they were his maternal uncles and in-laws — and they stayed with him a month, drinking wine while the two Jarādas sang to them.
The legend of the two Jarādas:
They were two singing-girls belonging to Muʿāwiya. When he saw how long they stayed and how they were distracted by amusement from what they had come for, it troubled him, and he said: My maternal uncles and in-laws have perished, and these are as they are. He was ashamed to speak to them, fearing they would think their stay a burden on him, so he mentioned it to the two singing-girls, who said: Compose some verses that we will sing to them, without their knowing who composed them. So Muʿāwiya ibn Bakr said:
ألا يا قيل ويحك قم فهينم ... لعلّ الله يسقينا غماما
فيسقي أرض عاد إنّ عادا ... قد أمسوا ما يبينون الكلاما
(O Qayl, woe to you, rise and murmur [a prayer]; perhaps Allah will give us rain-clouds to drink, and water the land of ʿĀd, for ʿĀd have come to the point where they cannot speak clearly.)
When the two sang it, they said: Your people are crying for help from the affliction that has befallen them, and you have been slow on their behalf, so enter the Sanctuary and pray for rain for your people. Marthad ibn Saʿd said to them: By Allah, you will not be given rain through your supplication; but if you obey your prophet and repent to Allah, you will be given rain. And he made his Islam public. They said to Muʿāwiya: Keep Marthad back from us; let him not come with us to Mecca, for he has followed the religion of Hūd and abandoned our religion. Then they entered Mecca, and Qayl ibn ʿItr said: O Allah, give ʿĀd rain as You used to give them. So Allah produced three clouds, white, red and black. Then a caller called him from the sky: O Qayl, choose for yourself and for your people! He said: I choose the black, for it has the most water. It came out upon ʿĀd from a valley of theirs called al-Mughīth, and they rejoiced at it and said: This is a cloud that will give us rain. But there came upon them from it a barren wind that destroyed them; and Hūd and the believers with him were saved. They went to Mecca and worshipped Allah there until they died.

dervis-irab:73-73.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ثَمُودَ): ثمود is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) when understood as "the tribe", and fully declined when understood as "the clan (al-ḥayy)", or in view of its origin, because it is the name of their great forefather, namely Thamūd ibn ʿĀmir ibn Iram ibn Sām ibn Nūḥ. It has also been said that Thamūd was so named because of the scarcity of its water, from الثمد, which is a little water. Al-Nābigha said:
واحكم كحكم فتاة الحي إذ نظرت ... إلى حمام شراع وارد الثّمد
(Judge like the judgement of the girl of the clan when she looked at a flock of doves coming down to the scanty water.)
Their dwellings were al-Ḥijr, between Syria and the Hijaz.

* I'rab:
(وَإِلى ثَمُودَ أَخاهُمْ صالِحاً) The i'rab of its like has been given before; صالحا is a badal (substitute) of «أخاهم». (قالَ يا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ) The i'rab of its like has been given before; the sentence is the object of his saying. (قَدْ جاءَتْكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) The clause falls within the object of his saying; جاءتكم is a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بينة is the fāʿil (agent); من ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) جاءتكم or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of بيّنة. (هذِهِ ناقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً) The clause is resumptive, introduced to explain the clear proof. The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ناقة الله is the khabar (predicate), the annexation being to magnify the matter of the she-camel; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted second khabar or ḥāl (circumstantial); آية is a ḥāl, the governing element (ʿāmil) in it being the verbal sense indicated by the demonstrative. This clause may also be parsed as a badal of بيّنة, because it serves as an explanation of it; a clause may substitute for a single word because it has its force. (فَذَرُوها تَأْكُلْ فِي أَرْضِ اللَّهِ) The fāʾ is of derivation (tafrīʿiyya), because it comes as a consequence of its being one of the signs of Allah, which requires that it not be touched with harm. ذروها is an imperative verb, its agent and its object; تأكل is an imperfect verb, in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request; في أرض الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تأكل or to His word فذروها, as a case of contention (tanāzuʿ) [of two governors]. (وَلا تَمَسُّوها بِسُوءٍ فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تمسوها is an imperfect verb in the jussive, the wāw is the agent and the hāʾ the object; بسوء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تمسوها. فيأخذكم: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya); يأخذكم is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ, because it is the answer to the prohibition; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi; عذاب is the fāʿil; أليم is an adjective.

dervis-irab:21-22.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَقاسَمَهُما): he swore to them. The mufāʿala (reciprocal) form here is not in its proper sense but is for intensification. It may also be kept in the sense of reciprocity, as al-Zamakhsharī established, as if he said: "I swear to you two that I am one of the sincere advisers", and they said to him: "Do you swear by Allah that you are one of the sincere advisers?" So that was made a mutual swearing between them.
(فَدَلَّاهُما): التدلية and الإدلاء: letting a thing down from above to below. Al-Azharī said: its origin is that a thirsty man lets himself down into a well to get water and finds no water in it; so التدلية was put in the place of hoping for what there is no hope for and no benefit from. Al-Farazdaq said:
هما دلّتاني من ثمانين قامة ... كما انقض باز أقتم الريش كاسره
(The two of them let me down from a height of eighty fathoms, as a dark-feathered falcon swoops with folded wings.)
(بِغُرُورٍ): الغرور is showing sincere advice while concealing deceit. «غرّه غرّا وغرّة وغرورا»: he deceived him and made him covet falsehood. Among their proverbs: «أفرّ من ظبي مقمر» (more fleeing than a gazelle on a moonlit night) [Translator's note: so in the source; the explanation that follows fits the well-known form «أغرّ من ظبي مقمر» (more easily deceived than a gazelle on a moonlit night)], because it comes out on the moonlit night thinking it is day, and the beasts of prey eat it. «لم يزل يطلب غرّته حتى صادفها» (he kept seeking his moment of heedlessness until he met it), and «أصاب منه غرّة فبطش به» (he caught him off guard and struck him). «ما غرّك به؟»: how did you dare against him? And «ما غرّك بربك الكريم»?
«أنا غريرك من هذا الأمر»: i.e. if you ask me about it unawares, I will answer you, because of the firmness of my knowledge of its reality. «هو على غرارة»: i.e. in danger. Al-Namir ibn Tawlab said:
تصابى وأمسى علاه الكبر ... وأمسى لجمرة حبل غرر
(He played the youth though old age had come over him, and his bond with Jamra became an unreliable cord.)
i.e. not to be relied upon. A Bedouin was pleased with a woman [Translator's note: so in the source, «ورضى»; perhaps for «ووصف» (described)] and said: «She is the white one, daughter of the dyed one», likening her to butter. One says of the market «درّة غرار», i.e. [alternating] brisk trade and slackness. And «لا غرار في الصلاة» (there is no deficiency in prayer); its origin is «غارّت الناقة غرارا» when the she-camel's milk decreased. «فلان مغار الكف» is said of the miser. From it: «ما أذوق النوم إلا غرارا» (I taste sleep only a little). This root is remarkable in the variety and harmony of its meanings, while all of them go back to one origin.
(طَفِقا): one of the verbs of commencement (afʿāl al-shurūʿ); they will be discussed in the Benefits section.
(يَخْصِفانِ): In al-Mukhtār: «خصف النعل خصفا: he stitched the sandal.
And His saying the Exalted: «وطفقا يخصفان عليهما من ورق الجنة»: i.e. they were sticking some of it onto others to cover their private parts with it.» In al-Miṣbāḥ: «خصف الرجل نعله خصفا, of the pattern ضرب, so he is خصّاف; in [a sandal] it is like patching a garment.»

* I'rab:
(وَقاسَمَهُما إِنِّي لَكُما لَمِنَ النَّاصِحِينَ) The و is resumptive. قاسمهما is a verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent); the ه is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the م and alif are two particles indicating the dual; the clause is resumptive. The clause إنّ and what falls in its scope is explicative (mufassira) of what the mutual swearing contains. إنّ and its noun; لكما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to الناصحين. نصح is a verb that is sometimes transitive by itself and sometimes by a preposition. Al-Farrāʾ said: «The Arabs hardly say نصحتك; they say نصحت لك and أنصح لك, though نصحتك is permissible.» The لام is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and من الناصحين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of إنّ. (فَدَلَّاهُما بِغُرُورٍ) The ف is a conjunction; دلاهما is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object. بغرور is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by deception", so the ف [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently «الباء» (the ب) is meant] is for accompaniment. They may also be attached to دلاهما, so it is for mere causation, i.e.:
"he let them down because of his deceiving them". (فَلَمَّا ذاقَا الشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُما سَوْآتُهُما) The ف is a conjunction; لما is temporal (ḥīniyya) and adverbial, or a particle for mere linking. ذاقا الشجرة is a verb, agent and direct object, and the clause ذاقا is in the position of the genitive by annexation (as muḍāf ilayhi). The clause بدت لهما has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. لهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بدت, and سوءاتهما is the agent of بدت. (وَطَفِقا يَخْصِفانِ عَلَيْهِما مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ) The و is a conjunction; طفقا is one of the verbs of commencement, whose rule will come; the alif is its noun and the clause يخصفان is its khabar. عليهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; من ورق الجنة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يخصفان, and الجنة is a muḍāf ilayhi. (وَناداهُما رَبُّهُما: أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُما عَنْ تِلْكُمَا الشَّجَرَةِ) The و is a conjunction; ناداهما ربهما is a verb, direct object and agent. The clause ألم أنهكما is explicative with no grammatical position. The hamza is for interrogation and conveys reproach and rebuke for the error, in that they did not take precautions and hold fast to caution against what Allah had warned them of. عن تلكما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنهكما, and الشجرة is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative. (وَأَقُلْ لَكُما: إِنَّ الشَّيْطانَ لَكُما عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ) The و is a conjunction, and أقل is an imperfect verb conjoined to the verb made jussive by لم. إنّ and its noun; لكما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عدو, or to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of عدو and was placed before it; مبين is an adjective of عدو. The clause إنّ and what falls in its scope is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).

* Benefits:
The verbs of approximation (afʿāl al-muqāraba): The grammarians apply the name "verbs of approximation" to [a group of] verbs that operate like kāna and its sisters, by applying [the name of] the part to the whole. The reality of the matter is that these verbs are of three kinds:
1- Those coined to indicate the nearness of the khabar; they are named after it [i.e. verbs of approximation proper], and they are three: كاد, كرب and أوشك.
2- Those coined to indicate hope for it; they are three: عسى, حرى and اخلولق.
3- Those coined to indicate commencing it; they are many — some have brought their number to twenty-odd verbs — and the best known are: أنشأ, طفق, طبق (with kasra on the ب), جعل, علق, هلهل, قام and ابتدأ.

The condition of the khabar of these verbs:
The khabar of these verbs must be a clause. Its coming as a single word after كاد and عسى is anomalous (shādhdh), as in the saying of Taʾabbaṭa Sharran:
فأبت إلى فهم وما كدت آئبا ... وكم مثلها فارقتها وهي تصفر
(I returned to Fahm, though I almost did not return; and how many a one like her have I left whistling [in vain].)
and their saying in the proverb: «عسى الغوير أبؤسا» (perhaps the little cave holds disasters), which al-Zabbāʾ said; الغوير is the name of a particular place. Some interpreted it as the khabar of an omitted «يكون»; al-Aṣmaʿī said: the khabar of an omitted «يصير»; and Ibn Hishām chose that it be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, as in «فطفق مسحا», i.e. "he began wiping, a wiping". The condition of the verb [in the khabar] is that it put in the nominative a pronoun of the noun. As for the saying of Abū Ḥayya al-Numayrī:
وقد جعلت إذا ما قمت يثقلني ... ثوبي فأنهض نهض الشّارب الثّمل
(Whenever I stand up, my garment has begun to weigh me down, so I rise like a staggering drunkard.)
and the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
وأسقيه حتّى كاد ممّا أبثّه ... تكلّمني أحجاره وملاعبه
(I water it [with my tears] until, from what I pour out to it, its stones and playgrounds almost speak to me.)
then «ثوبي» in the first verse and «أحجاره» in the second are badals of the nouns of جعل and كاد — a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) — not agents of يثقلني and تكلمني; rather their agent is a latent pronoun, the implied form being: «جعل ثوبي يثقلني» and «كادت أحجارة [Translator's note: so in the source, for «أحجاره»] تكلمني»; so the pronoun refers back to the badal rather than to the noun it substitutes for. [Further conditions are] that it be an imperfect verb; that it be joined to «أن» if [the main verb] indicates hope; and that it be free of it if [the main verb] indicates commencement. The khabar of عسى and أوشك is usually joined to it, as in His saying the Exalted: «عسى ربكم أن يرحمكم», and his saying:
ولو سئل الناس التراب لأوشكوا ... إذا قيل: هاتوا أن يملّوا ويمنعوا
(If people were asked for dust, they would be on the point, when told "Hand it over", of growing weary and refusing.)
Being free of «أن» is rare, as in the saying of Hudba:
عسى الكرب الذي أمسيت فيه ... يكون وراءه فرج قريب
(Perhaps the distress I am in has a near relief behind it.)
and the saying of Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt:
يوشك من فرّ من منيّته ... في بعض غرّاته يوافقها
(He who flees from his death is about to meet it in one of his heedless moments.)
كاد and كرب are the reverse. Of the usual is His saying the Exalted: «وما كادوا يفعلون», and the saying of Kalḥaba al-Yarbūʿī:
كرب القلب من جواه يذوب ... حين قال الوشاة: هند غضوب
(The heart was on the point of melting from its passion when the slanderers said: Hind is angry.)
Of the rare is his saying:
كادت النفس أن تفيض عليه ... مذ غدا حشو ربطة وبرود
(The soul almost poured out over him since he became the stuffing of a shroud and cloaks.)

Caution:
These verbs keep to the past form, except four for which an imperfect is used: كاد, as in «يكاد زيتها يضيء»; أوشك, as in:
يوشك من فر من منيته ... في بعض غرّاته يوافقها
and طفق يطفق, and جعل. An active participle is used for three: كاد, on which is the saying of Kuthayyir ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān:
أموت أسى يوم الرجاء وإنني ... يقينا لرهن بالذي أنا كائد
(I die of grief on the day of al-Rajāʾ, and I am surely pledged to what I am about to [do].)
and كرب; ʿAbd Qays ibn Khufāf ibn Nudba said:
أبنيّ إنّ أباك كارب يومه ... فإذا دعيت إلى المكارم فاعجل
(My son, your father is near his last day; so when you are called to noble deeds, hasten.)
and أوشك, as in the saying of Kuthayyir ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān:
فإنّك موشك أن لا تراها ... وتعدو دون غافره العوادي
(For you are about not to see her, as obstacles intervene before Ghāfir.)

dervis-irab:74-75.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَنْحِتُونَ): In al-Qāmūs: «نحته ينحته, like يضربه, ينصره and يعلمه [i.e. with kasra, ḍamma or fatḥa in the imperfect]: he hewed it».

* I'rab:
(وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفاءَ مِنْ بَعْدِ عادٍ) Conjoined to what preceded. إذ is accusative as an object, not as an adverb, i.e. remember the time of the appointing; the clause جعلكم is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and خلفاء the second mafʿūl bihi; من بعد عاد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of خلفاء. (وَبَوَّأَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْ سُهُولِها قُصُوراً) Conjoined to جعلكم; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بوأكم; the clause تتخذون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object; من سهولها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تتخذون or to an omitted ḥāl of «قصورا», since it would originally be its adjective if it came after it; قصورا is a mafʿūl bihi. The palace (قصر) was called قصر because of the inability (قصور) of the poor to obtain it. (وَتَنْحِتُونَ الْجِبالَ بُيُوتاً) The wāw is a conjunction; تنحتون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). الجبال may be accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. from the mountains, as in His words, the Exalted: «واختار موسى قومه سبعين رجلا», so that «بيوتا» is the mafʿūl bihi. [The verb] may also be made to include the sense of a verb taking two objects, i.e. you take the mountains as houses by hewing, or you make them into houses by hewing. Or الجبال may be the mafʿūl bihi and «بيوتا» an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), as you say: خط هذا الثوب قميصا (sew this cloth as a shirt), وابر هذه القصبة قلما (sharpen this reed as a pen). We said "anticipated" only because the mountain is not a house at the time of hewing, nor the cloth a shirt, nor the reed a pen at the time of sewing and sharpening. And «بيوتا», even though it is not derived, is in the sense of a derived [word], i.e. inhabited. (فَاذْكُرُوا آلاءَ اللَّهِ وَلا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa; اذكروا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; آلاء الله is a mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تعثوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تعثوا; مفسدين is a ḥāl. (قالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ) Resumptive speech introduced as an answer to a question. قال الملأ is a verb and its agent; الذين is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as an adjective; the clause استكبروا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; من قومه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (لِلَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قال; the clause استضعفوا is the ṣila; لمن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted [element], a badal (substitute) of الذين استضعفوا, with repetition of the governing element (ʿāmil). There are two views on it. One: it is a whole-for-whole badal if the pronoun in «منهم» refers to «قومه», so that the oppressed are all the believers only, as though it were said: the arrogant said to the believers among the people of Ṣāliḥ. Or [the other]: it is a part-for-whole badal if the pronoun refers to the oppressed, so that the oppressed are of two kinds, believers and disbelievers, as though it were said: the arrogant said to [the believers] among the weak, not the disbelievers among the weak [Translator's note: the source reads «قال المستكبرون من الضعفاء», apparently missing «للمؤمنين»]. منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (أَتَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ صالِحاً مُرْسَلٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ) The hamza is for the mocking interrogative, i.e. they said that by way of ridicule and derision; the interrogative sentence is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech); أنّ, its noun and its khabar (predicate) take the place of the two objects of تعلمون; من ربه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مرسل. (قالُوا: إِنَّا بِما أُرْسِلَ بِهِ مُؤْمِنُونَ) The clause is resumptive, introduced as their answer. They ran ahead of events, since the context would require them to say: Yes, or: We know that he is sent. إنّ and its noun; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar «مؤمنون»; the clause أرسل is the ṣila; إنّ and what follows it is a sentence in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أرسل.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is a delightful figure called the figure of taghāyur (contrariety); part of it has passed before, and we now repeat its definition as a reminder. It is the contrariety of two positions, either concerning a single notion, such that a person praises a thing or blames it, or blames what another has praised and vice versa; or prefers a thing or blames it, or blames what another has praised and vice versa; or prefers one thing to another and then turns back and makes the inferior superior and the superior inferior. Some of them took contrary positions in the matter of obedience and disobedience, after the contrariety in their speech and belief regarding their intentions; and this is that in which a person takes a position contrary to another.
[Translator's note: the definition is repetitive in the source and is translated as written.]

dervis-irab:76-79.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَعَقَرُوا النَّاقَةَ): العقر originally means laying bare the hamstrings of camels. It is — as al-Azharī said — striking the legs of the camel or she-camel so that it falls; this was their custom in slaughtering. Then every slaughter came to be called عقر, even if it involved no laying bare of hamstrings — naming a thing by what usually accompanies it, applying the cause to its effect. Ibn Qutayba said: العقر is killing in whatever way; one says عقرتها فهي معقورة. It has also been said: العقر is wounding.
(عَتَوْا): they turned away from the command of their Lord and were too proud to comply with it.
(جاثِمِينَ): جثم, i.e. he kept to his place and did not leave it, or he fell on his breast.
Abū ʿUbayda said: الجثوم for people and birds is like البروك (kneeling) for camels.

* I'rab:
(قالَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا) A verb, its fāʿil (agent) and the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative. (إِنَّا بِالَّذِي آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ كافِرُونَ) The i'rab of its like has been given before, and the sentence is the object of their saying. They did not say "we disbelieve in what he has been sent with", as the apparent context [would require], in order to display their opposition and their persistence in their obstinacy, and to avoid what would apparently suggest their affirming his mission, which they deny. (فَعَقَرُوا النَّاقَةَ وَعَتَوْا عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa; عقروا الناقة is a verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); عقروا is conjoined to عتوا [Translator's note: so in the source; in the verse it is عتوا that is conjoined to عقروا]; عن أمر ربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.
being arrogant, or acting on what insolence suggested to them; similar to it is «وما فعلته عن أمري». The hamstringing is ascribed to all of them because it was with their consent, even though only some of them carried it out. (وَقالُوا يا صالِحُ ائْتِنا بِما تَعِدُنا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) Conjoined to what preceded; the clause ائتنا is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ائتنا; the clause تعدنا is the ṣila of the relative; إن is conditional, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. then bring us; من المرسلين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of كنت. (فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دارِهِمْ جاثِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; أخذتهم الرجفة is a verb, its object and its agent; فأصبحوا is conjoined to فأخذتهم; the wāw is the noun of أصبحوا; في دارهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاثمين; جاثمين is the khabar of أصبحوا. (فَتَوَلَّى عَنْهُمْ وَقالَ: يا قَوْمِ لَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ رِسالَةَ رَبِّي) The fāʾ is a conjunction of immediate succession (taʿqīb). It appears that he witnessed with his own eyes what happened to them, and turned away grieved and sorrowful at their persistence in disbelief. عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تولى; قال is conjoined to فتولى; يا is a vocative particle; قوم is a vocative (munādā) annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person. In لقد the lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath and قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); أبلغتكم is a past verb, its agent and its first mafʿūl bihi; رسالة ربي is the second mafʿūl bihi. (وَنَصَحْتُ لَكُمْ وَلكِنْ لا تُحِبُّونَ النَّاصِحِينَ) Conjoined to أبلغتكم; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نصحت; the wāw is circumstantial; لكن is a lightened particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal); لا is negating; the clause لا تحبون الناصحين is circumstantial, because it relates a past state.

dervis-irab:23-27.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رِيشاً): الريش is the clothing of adornment, borrowed from the clothing of the bird because it is its clothing and its adornment. There are two views about it:
1- That it is a noun for this known thing [feathers].
2- That it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); one says «راشه يريشه ريشا» when he put feathers on it.
So الريش should be shared between the maṣdar and the concrete thing. Among figurative usages: «رشت فلانا»: I strengthened his wing by doing him good, so he became feathered (ارتاش وتريّش). He said:
فرشني بخير طال ما قد بريتني ... فخير الموالي من يريش ولا يبري
(So feather me with good — long have you whittled me down; the best of patrons is the one who feathers and does not whittle.)
Al-Nābigha said:
كم قد أحلّ بدار الفقر بعد غنى ... قوما وقد راش قوما بعد إقتار
يريش قوما ويربي آخرين بهم ... لله من رائش عمرو ومن بار
(How many a people has he settled in the abode of poverty after wealth, and how many a people has he feathered after want! He feathers some and whittles others down by them — what a featherer is ʿAmr, by Allah, and what a whittler!)
Jarīr said:
فريشي منكم وهواي معكم ... وإن كانت زيارتكم لماما
(My feathers come from you and my love is with you, even if your visits are only now and then.)
