«ولعن الله الراشي والمرتشي والرائش» (Allah has cursed the briber, the bribed and the رائش), who is the intermediary who "feathers" this one from that one's wealth. «فلان له رياش»: he has clothing, good condition and fine appearance.
Al-Nuʿmān rewarded al-Nābigha with a hundred of his عصافير with their feathers, i.e. with their saddles [Translator's note: so in the source, «برجالها»; perhaps for «برحالها» (with their saddles); the عصافير were royal camels]. It was said:
the kings used to put feathers on their humps so it would be known that they were the gift of a king. Among the subtle figurative usages is their saying «أخفّ من ريشة» (lighter than a feather), meaning lightness and scantiness of flesh from emaciation. How remarkable this root is! (قَبِيلُهُ): القبيل is a group of three or more, from various groups. This is the view of Abū ʿUbayda. And القبيل is the group descended from one father; so القبيلة is not the feminine of القبيل, because of this difference. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «القبيل:
a group of three or more from various peoples; the plural is قبل with two ḍammas. القبيلة is a dialectal variant of it. قبائل الرأس are the pieces [of the skull] joined to one another, and the tribes of the Arabs were named after them; the singular is قبيلة, and they are the sons of one father.»

* I'rab:
(قالا: رَبَّنا ظَلَمْنا أَنْفُسَنا) The clause of saying is resumptive, set forth to report Adam and Eve's confession of the sin against themselves and their feeling of remorse. قالا is a verb and fāʿil (agent); ربنا is the one addressed (munādā), with the vocative particle omitted; ظلمنا is a verb and agent, and أنفسنا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَإِنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنا وَتَرْحَمْنا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ) The و is a conjunction, إن is conditional, لم is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to the past] and the jussive, and تغفر is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to تغفر, and ترحمنا is conjoined to تغفر. لنكونن: the لام is [in] the answer to an implied oath, and نكونن is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being نحن, and من الخاسرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar (predicate). The clause وتكونن [Translator's note: so in the source, for «لنكونن»] is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the answer to the oath indicates it; the implied form is: «ولئن لم تغفر لنا وترحمنا». The reverse is also possible, so there is no need to imply an oath, and the لام would be preparatory for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa). (قالَ: اهْبِطُوا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ) The clause of saying is resumptive, set forth to settle what had been written on the page of destiny. The clause اهبطوا is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying. بعضكم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); لبعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عدوّ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it, because it was an adjective and was placed before it; عدو is the khabar, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl of the و in اهبطوا. (وَلَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتاعٌ إِلى حِينٍ) The و is a conjunction; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar placed first; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مستقر; متاع is conjoined to مستقر; and إلى حين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of متاع, i.e. "extending to a time". (قالَ: فِيها تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيها تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْها تُخْرَجُونَ) The clause of saying is resumptive; the resumption is repeated out of concern for the content of what follows it, namely human life. فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تحيون, and what follows is conjoined to it; the whole clause is the object of the saying of the Exalted. (يا بَنِي آدَمَ قَدْ أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكُمْ لِباساً يُوارِي سَوْآتِكُمْ وَرِيشاً) A resumptive clause, set forth to remind the children of Adam of some of the blessings. يا is a vocative particle and بني آدم is an annexed munādā; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); أنزلنا is a verb and agent; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزلنا; لباسا is a direct object; the clause يواري سوءاتكم is an adjective (ṣifa) of «لباسا», and ريشا is conjoined to His saying لباسا. (وَلِباسُ التَّقْوى ذلِكَ خَيْرٌ) The و is resumptive or circumstantial; لباس is a mubtadaʾ and التقوى a muḍāf ilayhi; ذلك is a demonstrative and a second mubtadaʾ, and خير is the khabar of ذلك. The linking element (rābiṭ) is the demonstrative, because demonstratives are close to pronouns; details of the linking elements will come in the Benefits section. The clause ذلك خير is the khabar of «لباس». (ذلِكَ مِنْ آياتِ اللَّهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ) The clause is resumptive, to emphasise what preceded. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, and من آيات الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar. لعل and its noun; the clause يذكرون is its khabar, and the clause of hope is circumstantial. (يا بَنِي آدَمَ لا يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطانُ) A resumptive statement addressing the children of Adam and warning them. لا is prohibitive, and يفتننكم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of the jussive by لا; the ك is a direct object and الشيطان is the agent. (كَما أَخْرَجَ أَبَوَيْكُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ) كما is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "let him not tempt you with a temptation like the expulsion of your parents from the Garden". أبويكم is an object, and من الجنة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخرج. (يَنْزِعُ عَنْهُما لِباسَهُما لِيُرِيَهُما سَوْآتِهِما) The clause is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «أخرج» referring to Satan, or of the two parents. عنهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينزع, and لباسهما is a direct object. ليريهما: the لام is causal, and يريهما is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the لام; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ينزع, and سوءاتهما is a direct object. (إِنَّهُ يَراكُمْ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُ) The clause gives the reason and has no grammatical position, set forth to give the reason for the prohibition and the warning against Satan's temptation. إنّ and its noun; the clause يراكم is its khabar; «هو» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the nominative pronoun in «يراكم», and قبيله is conjoined to the nominative pronoun; or «هو» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, indicated by the context. (مِنْ حَيْثُ لا تَرَوْنَهُمْ) من حيث is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يراكم, and the clause لا ترونهم is in the position of the genitive by annexation (as muḍāf ilayhi). (إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا الشَّياطِينَ أَوْلِياءَ لِلَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) The clause gives the reason for what preceded. إنّ and its noun; the clause جعلنا is its khabar; الشياطين is a first direct object and أولياء a second direct object; للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of أولياء, and the clause لا يؤمنون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iltifāt (turning):
In His saying the Exalted: «ولباس التقوى ذلك خير». The discussion of
this device has already been given. When He, Glorified is He, reminded humankind of His favour in sending down to them the clothing that covers their private parts, after the account of their father Adam's departure from the Garden, and wished to remind them and urge them to piety, He said before completing the [mention of the] favour: «ولباس التقوى ذلك خير». In this verse it would have been possible, as it was in the verse before it, to delay the clause, so that it would be said: «We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts, and adornment; that is among the signs of Allah; and the clothing of piety — that is best.»
But He inclined to delaying what could have been placed earlier so as to achieve in the arrangement of the speech a kind of beauty called taʿaṭṭuf (bending back): the speech comes opening with mention of clothing as it opened with it at its beginning, and avoids separating verses that suit one another with words not of their kind, so that the speech may be described as harmonious. Qudāma calls this iltifāt, while others, such as Ibn al-Muʿtazz and his like, consider iltifāt to be something else. We have followed the view of Ibn al-Muʿtazz in what we presented elsewhere at the beginning of the book.

Qudāma's definition of iltifāt:
As for Qudāma's definition of iltifāt, as it appears in his book «Naqd al-Shiʿr»: the speaker is engaged in a meaning, and then either doubt about it interrupts him, or he thinks that someone objecting has objected to it, or someone asking has asked about it or its cause; so he turns before finishing his expression of it, and either clears up his doubt, or emphasises and establishes it and mentions its cause. Our view is that this more closely resembles iʿtirāḍ (parenthesis) and more properly belongs in its category.
There is another iltifāt in His saying «لعلهم يذكرون»: He turned from address to the third person, whereas the context required «لعلكم».
2- Istiʿāra (metaphor):
In His saying «لباس التقوى»; it has already been referred to. Its like occurs frequently in the speech of the poets, including:
إذا المرء لم يلبس لباسا من التقى ... تقلّب عريانا وإن كان كاسيا
(If a man does not wear a garment of piety, he moves about naked even if he is clothed.)
and another's saying:
تغطّ بأثواب السّخاء فإنني ... أرى كلّ عيب والسّخاء غطاؤه
(Cover yourself with the garments of generosity, for I see that every fault has generosity as its cover.)
And there is metaphor in الريش: الريش is the clothing of adornment, borrowed from the feathers of the bird because they are its clothing and adornment. That is: We have sent down to you two garments, a garment to cover your private parts and a garment to adorn you, because adornment is a valid aim.

3- Ṭibāq (antithesis):
Between His saying «تحيون» and His saying «تموتون».

4- Tashbīh tamthīlī (representational simile):
In representing Satan's temptation of them by the story of Adam and Eve when Satan expelled them from the Garden by his snares. He used the imperfect in His saying «ينزع عنهما لباسهما» to call up the image that occurred in the remotest of ages and embody it before the hearer.

* Benefits:
The linking elements of the clause that is a khabar:
A clause occurring as a khabar must contain a linking element (rābiṭ) that links it to the mubtadaʾ. The linking elements are four:
a- The overt pronoun, as in «الظلم مرتعه وخيم» (injustice — its pasture is unwholesome), or the latent one, as in:
«الحق يعلو» (the truth rises).
b- Pointing to it [with a demonstrative], as in «ولباس التقوى ذلك خير».
c- Repeating the mubtadaʾ with its wording, as in «الحاقّة ما الحاقّة», and the saying of Kaʿb:
أخي ما أخي لا فاحش عند بيته ... ولا ورع عند اللقاء هيوب
(My brother — what a brother! Not obscene at his home, nor timid and fearful at the encounter.)
d- Generality, as in «زيد نعم الرجل» (Zayd — what an excellent man!): زيد is a mubtadaʾ, the clause نعم is its khabar, and the link between them is generality. From it is the saying of Ibn Mayyāda:
ألا ليت شعري هل إلى أمّ معمر ... سهيل فأمّا الصّبر عنها فلا صبرا
(Would that I knew whether there is a way to Umm Maʿmar; as for patience without her, there is no patience.) [Translator's note: the source prints «سهيل», evidently for «سبيل» (a way).]
الصبر is a mubtadaʾ, عنها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it, لا is the lā of generic negation, and صبرا is its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa [Translator's note: so in the source, although the verse prints it with an alif, «صبرا»]; the khabar is omitted, its implied form being «لي». The clause «لا صبر لي» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the link between them is the generality in the noun of «لا», because an indefinite noun in a context of negation conveys generality.
The clause may not need a linking element:
Note that the clause occurring as a khabar may be the mubtadaʾ itself in meaning;
then it does not need a linking element, because it is not extraneous to it, as in His saying the Exalted: «قل هو الله أحد»: «هو» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and a mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause after it is the khabar; it does not need a linking element because it is identical with it.

dervis-irab:80-81.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلُوطاً إِذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ: أَتَأْتُونَ الْفاحِشَةَ) The wāw conjoins to the stories that preceded, i.e. and mention Lūṭ at that time. لوطا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, i.e. and mention Lūṭ; إذ is an adverb serving as a badal (substitute) of His word:
«ولوطا», i.e. and mention the time when he said to his people. The clause قال is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; لقومه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) قال; the hamza is for the disapproving interrogative of rebuke (istifhām inkārī tawbīkhī); تأتون الفاحشة is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech). (ما سَبَقَكُمْ بِها مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِنَ الْعالَمِينَ) This clause may properly be resumptive, introduced to reinforce the disapproval and intensify the rebuke and reproach — for committing a vile deed is vile, and inventing it is viler. It may also be circumstantial, either of the agent, meaning: do you commit it as the first to do it?, or of the object, meaning: do you commit it as something begun [by you], not preceded by others? سبقكم is a past verb and its object; بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to سبقكم, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. no one preceded you accompanied by it, i.e. involved in it; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; أحد is the fāʿil of سبقكم; من العالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أحد. (إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الرِّجالَ شَهْوَةً مِنْ دُونِ النِّساءِ) The clause is resumptive, introduced to set out the kind of indecency they had invented. إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause تأتون is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; الرجال is a mafʿūl bihi; شهوة is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. you have no motive other than sheer lust — and this is an eloquent censure, because it attaches them to beasts wallowing in filth. It may also be parsed as a ḥāl in the sense of "lusting", i.e. following the promptings and incentives of lust, heedless of its ugliness. من دون النساء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl of the wāw in «تأتون», i.e. passing over women, or of الرجال. (بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُسْرِفُونَ) بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb), turning from disapproval to informing about them with the state that entails the joining together of scandals and vices. أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); قوم is the khabar; مسرفون is an adjective.

* Benefits:
(بَلْ) is for digression (iḍrāb), conjunction, and turning from one thing to another, if it occurs after an affirmative statement, whether a declaration or a command; or for rectification (istidrāk), equivalent to «لكن», if it occurs after a negation or prohibition. It conjoins only on condition that what it conjoins is a single word, not a clause. If it occurs after an affirmation or a command, its meaning is to remove the ruling from what precedes it, as though nothing had been said about it, and to give it to what follows, e.g. قام علي بل خالد (ʿAlī stood — no, Khālid), and ليقم عليّ بل سعيد (let ʿAlī stand — no, Saʿīd). If it occurs after a negation or prohibition, its meaning is to confirm the negation or prohibition for what precedes it and to give its opposite to what follows, e.g. ما قام علي بل خالد (ʿAlī did not stand, but Khālid), and لا يذهب عليّ بل خالد (let ʿAlī not go, but Khālid). If a clause follows it, it is not a conjunction but an inceptive particle conveying iḍrāb of cancellation (ibṭālī) or of transition (intiqālī). The first is as in His words, the Exalted: «وقالوا:
اتخذ الرحمن ولدا سبحانه بل عباد مكرمون», i.e. rather they are servants.
The second is as in the verse just mentioned. «لا» is sometimes added before it, after an affirmation or a negation. The first is as in the words of the poet:
وجهك البدر لا بل الشمس لو لم ... يقض للشمس كسفنة أو أفول
(Your face is the full moon — no, rather the sun, were it not that eclipse or setting is decreed for the sun.) [Translator's note: «كسفنة» is so in the source; the usual wording is «كسفة».]
And the second as in the words of another:
وما هجرتك لا بل زادني شغفا ... هجر وبعد تراخ لا إلى أجل
(I did not forsake you — no, rather forsaking and a distance drawn out without end only increased my passion.)

dervis-irab:82-84.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْغابِرِينَ): those remaining, i.e. those who stayed behind (غبروا) in their homes, i.e. remained in them. The masculine is used to give precedence (taghlīb) [Translator's note: the source prints «لتعليب»] to the males over the females. His wife was a disbeliever, loyal to the people of Sadūm — with an undotted dāl; it has also been said that it is with the dotted [dhāl] — which is a city lying on the shore of Lake Tiberias.

* I'rab:
(وَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا:) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negating; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; جواب is its fronted khabar (predicate); قومه is muḍāf ilayhi; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); the maṣdariyya أن and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the delayed noun of كان, i.e. except their saying. (أَخْرِجُوهُمْ مِنْ قَرْيَتِكُمْ إِنَّهُمْ أُناسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ) The sentence is in the position of the accusative as the object of their saying; من قريتكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أخرجوهم; إنّ and its noun; أناس is its khabar; the clause is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position — they brought it as an expression of their ridicule and mockery of Lūṭ and his people; the clause يتطهرون is a naʿt (adjective) of أناس. (فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَأَهْلَهُ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَهُ كانَتْ مِنَ الْغابِرِينَ) The fāʾ conjoins to something omitted understood from the context of the speech, i.e. so the punishment descended upon them, and We saved him.
أنجيناه is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أهله is conjoined to the hāʾ, or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); إلا is a particle of exception; أهله is the excepted [Translator's note: so in the source; the excepted is امرأته]. The clause كانت من الغابرين is resumptive, introduced to answer a question arising from her exception, as though it were said: So what was her state?
And it was said: She was among those who stayed behind, i.e. those who remained in their homes, i.e. stayed in them and perished. (وَأَمْطَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ مَطَراً) The wāw is a conjunction; أمطر is a past verb, like مطر; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أمطرنا; مطرا is a mafʿūl bihi, because what is meant by it is the stones, and rain is not meant by it at all. أمطرنا has been made to include the sense of أرسلنا (We sent), and for that reason it is made transitive with على. Had He meant the maṣdar, He would have said إمطارا, as analogy requires. (فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; انظر is an imperative verb; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted khabar of كان; عاقبة is its noun; المجرمين is muḍāf ilayhi.

* Benefits:
A disagreement arose among the lexicographers over مطر and أمطر. Abū ʿUbayda said:
One says مطر of mercy and أمطر of punishment. This is refuted by His words, the Exalted:
«هذا عارض ممطرنا», for by that they meant mercy. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «What is the difference between مطر and أمطر?» And he answered this question, saying: «One says مطرتهم السماء (the sky rained on them), and واد ممطور (a rained-on valley). In Nawābigh al-Kalim: حرى ممطور، حرى أن يكون غير ممطور» — the first حرى meaning side or quarter, and the second meaning worthy and deserving; the first ممطور meaning struck by rain, and the second meaning gone away with [i.e. carried off]. «The meaning of مطرتهم is:
it struck them with rain, like his saying غاثتهم، وبلتهم، جادتهم، رهمتهم. And one says:
أمطرت عليهم كذا, meaning: I sent it to them in the way rain is sent: «فأمطر علينا حجارة من السماء», «وأمطرنا عليهم حجارة من سجيل»; and the meaning of «وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا» is: We sent upon them a wondrous kind of rain, meaning the stones». Al-Zamakhsharī's aim in all this is to refute those who say مطرت السماء for good and أمطرت for evil, imagining that this is a distinction established by original coinage (waḍʿ). So he made clear that «أمطرت» means: sent something in the manner of rain, even if it is not water; so that if Allah sent from the sky kinds of good things and provisions — such as manna and quails, for example — it would be correct to say of it أمطرت السماء خيرات, i.e. it sent them down as rain is sent. So evil has no special connection with this four-letter form; but it happened that the sky did not send anything other than rain except what was a punishment, so what occurred by chance was thought to be intended in the coinage, and al-Zamakhsharī drew attention to the truth of the matter.
[Translator's note: the source reads «حتى أرسل الله», evidently for «حتى لو أرسل الله»; translated in that sense.]
Among those who distinguished between the three-letter and four-letter forms is al-Fīrūzābādī, author of al-Qāmūs, who said: «وأمطرهم الله is said only of punishment».

dervis-irab:28-30.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا فَعَلُوا فاحِشَةً قالُوا: وَجَدْنا عَلَيْها آباءَنا) The و is resumptive — perhaps this is clearer — and it may be a conjunction joining to the ṣila (relative clause) before it; in either case there is in it an emphasis on their persistence in indecency. إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the apodosis, namely قالوا; the clause فعلوا is in the position of the genitive by annexation (as muḍāf ilayhi), and فاحشة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, and the clause وجدنا عليها آباءنا is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَاللَّهُ أَمَرَنا بِها) والله: the و is a conjunction, الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause أمرنا بها is the khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause and falls within the scope of the saying, i.e.:
"and they said: Allah commanded us to do it". (قُلْ: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَأْمُرُ بِالْفَحْشاءِ أَتَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ) The clause of saying is resumptive, set forth to refute their claim and [to show] that blind imitation (taqlīd) is not a proof. The clause إنّ and what falls in its scope is accusative as the object of saying. إنّ and its noun; the clause لا يأمر is its khabar, and بالفحشاء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأمر. The hamza is for interrogation of disapproval and rebuke; تقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تقولون; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a direct object, and the clause لا تعلمون is the ṣila. (قُلْ أَمَرَ رَبِّي بِالْقِسْطِ وَأَقِيمُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ) A resumptive statement, set forth to explain what Allah has truly commanded. The clause أمر ربي is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying, and بالقسط is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أمر. وأقيموا: the و is a conjunction, and أقيموا is an imperative verb conjoined to the implied imperative into which the maṣdar (verbal noun), namely القسط, resolves, in the manner of the saying of Maysūn:
ولبس عباءة وتقرّ عيني ... أحبّ إليّ من لبس الشّفوف
(Wearing a coarse cloak, with my eye content, is dearer to me than wearing sheer fabrics.)
As if He said: "Be just, and set…", to avoid conjoining a performative (inshāʾ) to a declarative (khabar); but this is weak. وجوهكم is a direct object of أقيموا; عند is an adverb of place attached to أقيموا, and كل مسجد is a muḍāf ilayhi. (وَادْعُوهُ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ) Conjoined to what preceded. ادعوه is an imperative verb, fāʿil (agent) and direct object; مخلصين is a ḥāl (circumstantial); له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مخلصين; and الدين is an object of مخلصين because it is an active participle. (كَما بَدَأَكُمْ تَعُودُونَ) كما is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being:
"you will return with a return like [the way] He began you". The clause بدأكم has no grammatical position because it occurs after a particle relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī). (فَرِيقاً هَدى وَفَرِيقاً حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الضَّلالَةُ) فريقا is a direct object of هدى placed first. The second فريقا is accusative by an implied verb explained, in meaning and implied form, by His saying حق عليهم الضلالة: "and He led astray a group against whom [error] was due". Al-Zamakhsharī implied it as «وخذل فريقا» (and He forsook a group), aiming to support his Muʿtazilī doctrine.
The verbal clause and the clause conjoined to it are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of بدأكم, i.e. "He began you, in the state of guiding a group and leading a group astray"; or the two clauses are resumptive. It is far-fetched to parse «فريقا» as a ḥāl, as some parsers have it. The clause حق عليهم الضلالة is an adjective (ṣifa) of «فريقا». (إِنَّهُمُ اتَّخَذُوا الشَّياطِينَ أَوْلِياءَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ) The clause gives the reason and has no grammatical position. إنّ and its noun; the clause اتخذوا الشياطين is the khabar; الشياطين is the first direct object of اتخذوا and أولياء its second object; من دون الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. The و is a conjunction or circumstantial; أنّ and what falls in its scope take the place of the two objects of يحسبون, and مهتدون is the khabar of أنهم.

dervis-irab:31-32.t:
* I'rab:
(يا بَنِي آدَمَ خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ) A resumptive statement, set forth to address the Arabs and induce them to give up excessive strictness and depriving themselves of adornment. يا is a vocative particle, and بني is an annexed munādā (one addressed); خذوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the ن; زينتكم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and عند كل مسجد — the adverb is attached (mutaʿalliq) to خذوا. (وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا وَلا تُسْرِفُوا إِنَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ) Conjoined to خذوا. لا is prohibitive, and تسرفوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا. إنّ and its noun; the clause لا يحب المسرفين is its khabar (predicate), and the clause gives the reason and has no grammatical position. (قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبادِهِ وَالطَّيِّباتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ خالِصَةً يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) The clause of saying is resumptive, set forth to emphasise the permissibility and enjoyment of adornment, eating and drinking, without excess. من is an interrogative noun of disapproval and a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause حرم زينة الله is the khabar of من, and the interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). الطيبات is conjoined to زينة; من الرزق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); خالصة is a second ḥāl; and يوم القيامة is an adverb attached to خالصة. [Translator's note: the source does not parse «التي أخرج لعباده» or the words «هي للذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا» of the verse.] (كَذلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ) Parsings similar to this clause have already been given.

* Benefits:
Ibn ʿAbbās said: the Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked, the men by day and the women by night, saying: "We will not circumambulate in clothes in which we have disobeyed Allah." So [this verse] was revealed.
It is related that al-Rashīd had a skilful Christian physician, who said to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid: "Is there nothing of the science of medicine in your Book?" He said to him:
"Allah has gathered all of medicine in half a verse of His Book." He said: "And what is it?" He said:
"His saying the Exalted: «كلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا»." The physician said: "And is nothing about medicine transmitted from your Messenger?" He said: "Our Messenger gathered medicine in a few words." He said: "And what are they?" He said: "His saying: «The stomach is the house of disease, and abstinence is the head of every remedy»." The physician said: "Your Book and your Prophet have left no medicine for Galen."

dervis-irab:33-34.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أجل): الأجل, with two fatḥas: the term of life from its beginning to its end. He repeated its mention in His saying «فإذا جاء أجلهم» to point to the end of the term. In al-Miṣbāḥ:
«The أجل of a thing is its term and the time at which it falls due. It is the maṣdar of «أجل الشيء إجلالا» [Translator's note: so in the source], of the pattern تعب, and «أجل أجولا», of the pattern قعد, is a dialectal variant. «أجّلته تأجيلا»: I set a term for it. The plural of الأجل is آجال, like سبب and أسباب.»
Among their sayings: «The son of Adam is short of term, long of hope; he prefers the immediate and leaves the deferred.» Also among their sayings: «أجلن عيون الآجال، فأصبن النفوس بالآجال» (They [the women] cast the eyes of wild cows about, and struck souls with death) — a play on آجال as "herds of wild cows" and "appointed terms".

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: إِنَّما حَرَّمَ رَبِّيَ الْفَواحِشَ ما ظَهَرَ مِنْها وَما بَطَنَ) A resumptive statement, set forth to address those who forbid and permit [at will]: Allah did not forbid what you forbid on His account; He forbade only indecencies. قل is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being أنت. إنما is a restraining particle and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and the clause حرم ربي الفواحش is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of الفواحش; the clause ظهر is the ṣila (relative clause); منها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to ظهر; and ما بطن is conjoined to ما ظهر. (وَالْإِثْمَ وَالْبَغْيَ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ) [This is] conjoining the specific to the general, out of concern for it. بغير الحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or to البغي because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). (وَأَنْ تُشْرِكُوا بِاللَّهِ ما لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطاناً) The maṣdar interpreted from أن and what falls in its scope is also conjoined. بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تشركوا; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause لم ينزل is the ṣila. به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, and سلطانا is a direct object of ينزل. (وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ) Also conjoined. على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تقولوا; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a direct object, and the clause لا تعلمون is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلٌ) A resumptive statement, set forth to indicate that the terms are written and lifespans counted, lest man be deluded [by] the draughts of pleasures and their deceptive wonders. لكل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) placed first; أمة is a muḍāf ilayhi, and أجل is a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after it. (فَإِذا جاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ ساعَةً وَلا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ) The ف is resumptive; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause جاء أجلهم is in the position of the genitive by annexation (as muḍāf ilayhi); the clause لا يستأخرون has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. When an imperfect negated by لا occurs as the apodosis of إذا, it may be joined to the ف or not joined to it. ساعة is an adverb of time attached to يستأخرون; it is the shortest of times in people's reckoning: someone in a hurry says, "Do you want that in an hour (ساعة)?", meaning the utmost shortness of time.
ولا يستقدمون is conjoined to His saying لا يستأخرون, or the و is resumptive, as you will see in the Benefits section.

* Benefits:
Below is a summary of the views of the leading scholars on this statement:

The view of al-Wāḥidī:
Al-Wāḥidī said after a long discussion: If it is asked, what is the meaning of this, given the impossibility of coming before the term at the time of its arrival? It is answered: this is built on approach; you say «إذا جاء الشتاء» (when winter comes) when its time approaches. With the approach of the term, coming before it is conceivable, even though it is not conceivable with its expiry. The meaning is: they will not delay beyond their terms when they expire, nor come before them when they are about to expire. This is on the basis that it is conjoined to His saying لا يستأخرون.

The view of al-Karkhī:
Al-Karkhī said: «His saying ولا يستقدمون is conjoined to the conditional sentence, not to the apodosis, because conditional إذا has only the future consequent upon it; i.e. nothing follows from the arrival of the term except what is future, or [Translator's note: the source has «أو لاستقدام سابق», which appears garbled; the sense is that a coming-before would be prior, not consequent] a prior coming-before. So the right view is that «لا يستقدمون» is cut off from the apodosis as a resumption, as al-Taftāzānī established.» [Translator's note: the source does not close this quotation mark.]

The view of al-Bayḍāwī:
The gist of what al-Qāḍī al-Bayḍāwī said is that this is like a proverb, i.e.
nothing is intended by the statement as a whole except that the time does not change or alter; it is parallel to their saying "the pomegranate is sweet-sour", meaning that the predicate is the combination of the two things, not each one separately. This is a fine remark by al-Bayḍāwī, and perhaps it settles the disagreement.

dervis-irab:85-87.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَدْيَنَ): a non-Arabic name. It is the name of a tribe, named after their forefather Madyan son of Ibrāhīm; and Shuʿayb was the son of Mīkāʾīl son of Yashjur son of Madyan — which is the name of a tribe — so he is their brother by lineage, and he is not one of the prophets of the Children of Israel. Madyan is also the name of Shuʿayb's town, so it is a name shared by the town, the tribe and its forefather.
(تَبْخَسُوا): diminish. One says: بخسته حقه, when you have diminished his due to him. In the proverb: «تحسبها حمقاء وهي باخس» (you think her foolish, yet she is one who cheats). Among the remarkable features of the bāʾ and the khāʾ is that when they come together as the first and second radicals of a word, we express by them an effect on things. Among them: البخت, which is luck, and its effect is too well known to be mentioned; بخ لك, a word of admiration and praise for something, said with kasra and tanwīn — the khāʾ may be doubled and the word repeated, so one says بخّ بخّ, and they are then indeclinable on sukūn; بخر الثوب: he gave the garment a pleasant scent with incense, while البخر, with two fatḥas, is foul breath — so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād); البخار, which is water in the gaseous state, and everything that rises from hot liquids, like smoke — its effect in driving trains and other things is well known and familiar; بخص عينه: he gouged out his eye; بخع نفسه: he destroyed himself; and بخل: he held back and withheld.

* I'rab:
(وَإِلى مَدْيَنَ أَخاهُمْ شُعَيْباً قالَ يا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ) This verse has recurred many times, and its i'rab has been given before. (قَدْ جاءَتْكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) The clause falls within the scope of the saying and is in the accusative by it; بينة is the fāʿil (agent) of جاءتكم; من ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of بينة. (فَأَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ وَالْمِيزانَ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa; أوفوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; الكيل is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الميزان is conjoined to الكيل. (وَلا تَبْخَسُوا النَّاسَ أَشْياءَهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تبخسوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is its fāʿil; الناس is a mafʿūl bihi; أشياءهم is a second mafʿūl bihi. One says:
بخسته حقه when you have diminished his due to him. (وَلا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ بَعْدَ إِصْلاحِها) Conjoined to what preceded; لا is prohibitive; تفسدوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive by لا; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تفسدوا; بعد إصلاحها is an adverb of time attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and a muḍāf must be implied, i.e. the reform of its people. (ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) The clause is resumptive; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); خير is the khabar (predicate); لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خير; إن is conditional; كنتم: كان and its noun, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); مؤمنين is the khabar of كنتم; the apodosis of إن is omitted, i.e. then hasten to faith. (وَلا تَقْعُدُوا بِكُلِّ صِراطٍ تُوعِدُونَ)
Also conjoined; بكل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تقعدوا; صراط is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause توعدون is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. and do not sit threatening. (وَتَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ) Also conjoined; عن سبيل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تصدون; من is the object of تصدون; the clause آمن به is the ṣila (relative clause); به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمن. (وَتَبْغُونَها عِوَجاً) تبغونها is a verb, its agent and its object; عوجا is a ḥāl in which the maṣdar (verbal noun) stands in the place of the derived noun, i.e. crooked. It is also possible that the hāʾ is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ) and عوجا is the mafʿūl bihi. This is a sound view, given before in Āl ʿImrān, so refresh your memory of it. (وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ كُنْتُمْ قَلِيلًا فَكَثَّرَكُمْ) Also conjoined; إذ is an adverb of past time in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. remember, giving thanks, the time when your number was small. It may also be an adverb, the mafʿūl bihi being omitted, so that the adverb is governed by that omitted [object], i.e. remember His favour upon you at that time. The clause كنتم is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; كان, its noun and its khabar; فكثركم is conjoined to كنتم, i.e. He made you many through wealth after poverty and through power after weakness. (وَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُفْسِدِينَ) Also conjoined; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted khabar of كان; عاقبة المفسدين is its noun. The interrogative has suspended (ʿallaqa) [the verb of] looking, so the clause is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to انظروا. (وَإِنْ كانَ طائِفَةٌ مِنْكُمْ آمَنُوا بِالَّذِي أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; كان and its noun; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of طائفة; the clause آمنوا is the khabar of كان; بالذي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا; the clause أرسلت به is the ṣila. (وَطائِفَةٌ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا) طائفة is conjoined to the first طائفة, and the clause لم يؤمنوا is conjoined to the clause آمنوا, which is the khabar of كان — a case of conjoining the noun [to the noun] and the khabar to the khabar. What لم يؤمنوا is attached to is omitted, being sufficed by what آمنوا is attached to. (فَاصْبِرُوا حَتَّى يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ بَيْنَنا) The fāʾ connects the apodosis of the condition; حتى is a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition; يحكم is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اصبروا; بيننا is an adverb attached to يحكم. (وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْحاكِمِينَ) The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; هو is a mubtadaʾ and خير الحاكمين its khabar.

dervis-irab:88-89.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لَتَعُودُنَّ): The verb «عاد» has two uses in the language of the Arabs. The first, which is the original: returning to the former state one was in. The second:
its use in the sense of صار (became), in which case it puts the noun in the nominative and the khabar in the accusative. We have followed both parsings.

* I'rab:
(قالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ) This i'rab has been given before word for word. The sentence is resumptive, introduced to set out what they said after they heard the admonitions. (لَنُخْرِجَنَّكَ يا شُعَيْبُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَكَ مِنْ قَرْيَتِنا) The lām is the one that prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); نخرجنك is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذين is conjoined to the kāf, or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); معك is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the expelling, not to the believing. Placing the vocative with the name of Shuʿayb in the middle further shows how deeply sunk they were in insolence and tyranny. من قريتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نخرجنك. (أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِي مِلَّتِنا) أو is a conjunction; لتعودن is conjoined to the answer to the first oath, i.e. by Allah, we will expel you and the believers, or you will return. تعودن here is declinable (muʿrab) because it is not directly joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; its origin is تعودونن: the nūn [of the indicative] was dropped because of the succession of like letters, and the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The wāw is either the fāʿil (agent) or the noun of تعود, according to the two uses. في ملتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تعودن or to the omitted khabar (predicate) of تعودن. (قالَ أَوَلَوْ كُنَّا كارِهِينَ) The sentence of saying is resumptive, introduced to set out the reply of Shuʿayb, peace be upon him. The hamza is for the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī), i.e. disapproval; لو is conditional, merely for linking, not for the non-occurrence of a thing in the past because of the non-occurrence of another thing in it; كان, its noun and its khabar; the clause لو كنا كارهين is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of the implied verb, i.e. shall we return even if we are unwilling? (قَدِ افْتَرَيْنا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً إِنْ عُدْنا فِي مِلَّتِكُمْ) The clause is resumptive, introduced to express astonishment at their persistence in their position. قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); افترينا is a verb and its agent; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to افترينا; كذبا is a mafʿūl bihi, or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); إن is conditional; عدنا في ملتكم is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the i'rab of the rest has been given according to the two uses; the apodosis of إن is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. then we would have fabricated a lie. (بَعْدَ إِذْ نَجَّانَا اللَّهُ مِنْها) بعد is an adverb of time attached to an omitted ḥāl, and the adverb is annexed to another adverb; the clause نجانا is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; الله is the fāʿil; منها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نجانا. (وَما يَكُونُ لَنا أَنْ نَعُودَ فِيها) The wāw is resumptive, introduced to declare returning far-fetched. ما is negating; يكون is an imperfect verb; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; أن and what falls within its scope is the noun of يكون; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نعود or to its omitted khabar, according to the two uses. (إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّنا) There are two views on this exception. One: it is connected (muttaṣil), in which case the exception is from the most general of times or states. The other: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), so the implied sense is: but if Allah wills the return. الله is the fāʿil of يشاء; ربنا is a badal (substitute) of الله. (وَسِعَ رَبُّنا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْماً) The clause is resumptive, introduced to set out the vastness of our Lord's knowledge. وسع is a past verb; ربنا is the fāʿil; كل شيء is a mafʿūl bihi; علما is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil, i.e. His knowledge encompasses everything. (عَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْنا) The clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to توكلنا; توكلنا is a verb and its agent. (رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْفاتِحِينَ) The clause is resumptive; ربنا is a muḍāf vocative (munādā); افتح is an imperative verb; بيننا is an adverb of place attached to افتح, i.e. judge between us and our people; the wāw is likewise circumstantial or resumptive; أنت is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير الفاتحين the khabar.

* Benefits:
These two verses contain many benefits, which we summarize as follows: 1- The difficulty concerning "returning":
If «عاد» has its original meaning, how is it fitting to say
«أو لتعودنّ», i.e. you will surely return to your former state, when Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, was never in their religion or in their creed? This difficulty has been answered in several ways:
1- This was said by their chiefs, who intended by it to confuse and to give the common people the false impression that he had been in their religion and creed.
2- What is meant by his returning is his going back to his state before his mission, namely silence, because before he was sent he concealed his faith and was silent.
3- Giving precedence (taghlīb) to the group over the individual: since they made him accompany his people in the expulsion, they applied to them the ruling of returning to the creed, giving them precedence over him.
Moreover, using عاد in the sense of صار does not require a return to a previous state; rather the opposite, namely moving from a previous state to a new one; and then the difficulty is entirely removed.
There is a subtle, artistic way of answering the difficulty that is not far-fetched, in which عاد keeps its original meaning: that the speech is of the same kind as His words, the Exalted:
«الله وليّ الذين آمنوا يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور، والذين كفروا أولياؤهم الطاغوت يخرجونهم من النور إلى الظلمات». Bringing out requires a previous entry into that from which the bringing out took place, and we know that the believer who grew up in faith and was raised on its heights never entered the darkness of disbelief nor was in it; likewise the original disbeliever never entered the light of faith nor was in it. But since faith and disbelief are among voluntary acts, it is an expression of the cause by the effect, to establish Allah's proof against His servants.

2- Luzūm mā lā yalzam (observing what is not required):
In the first verse there is luzūm mā lā yalzam, namely His words, the Exalted: «لنخرجنك يا شعيب والذين معك من قريتنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا»: the tāʾ has been kept before the nūn [in قريتنا / ملتنا]. This is what is called «luzūm mā lā yalzam»: that the poet in his poetry and the prose writer in his prose commit themselves to one letter, or two letters or more, before the rhyme letter (al-rawiyy), according to his ability and the strength of his talent, on condition that there be no affectation. Much of it will occur in the Quran.

Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī and luzūm:
Abū al-ʿAlāʾ said:
كثيّر أنا في حرفي أهبت له ... في التاء يلزم حرفا غير يلتزم
(I am [like] Kuthayyir in my letter [of rhyme] … in the tāʾ he keeps a letter not [otherwise] kept.) [Translator's note: the verse is garbled in the source and is reproduced as found; the gloss is approximate.]
In his verse our philosopher-poet recorded the history of the art he loved and to which he first devoted himself, namely «luzūm mā lā yalzam». The meaning of the verse is that he followed the example of Kuthayyir ʿAzza, who kept the lām [before the rhyme] in his tāʾ-rhymed ode, which begins:
خليليّ هذا ربع عزّة فاعقلا ... قلوصيكما ثم احللا حيث حلّت
(My two friends, this is the encampment of ʿAzza, so hobble your two young camels, then halt where she halted.)
This much-admired ode numbers, according to the transmission of al-Qālī, thirty-five verses; he built it from beginning to end on keeping a particular letter before the rhyme letter, something in which no poet of the Arabs had preceded him in using this kind, and the poets imitated him. Did al-Maʿarrī mean that? The answer is: no. In our view, al-Maʿarrī, in following Kuthayyir ʿAzza, did not do so because Kuthayyir was the first to use this art — as a group of rhetoricians imagined — but because luzūm mā lā yalzam occurred only rarely in Arabic poetry before Kuthayyir's time, and then in fragments and short pieces; whereas Kuthayyir composed the most famous and longest luzūm ode handed down by the transmitters. Arab poets before and after Kuthayyir often observed what is not required before this feminine tāʾ.
Further, Abū al-ʿAlāʾ reached the utmost in his Luzūmiyyāt: he built one rhyme on دارهم، صدارهم, keeping four letters in it, and built another on ضرائرهم، صرائرهم، سرائرهم, keeping five letters in it.
The discussion would grow long if we wished to cite examples, so what has been given suffices us.

dervis-irab:90-93.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَغْنَوْا): the imperfect of غني بالمكان, "he stayed in the place"; he is غان. المغنى is the dwelling, plural المغاني. The poet of Tayyiʾ said:
غنينا زمانا بالتصعلك والغنى ... وكلا سقاناه بكاسيهما الدهر
(We dwelt for a time in poverty and in wealth, and Time gave us to drink of both its cups.)
فما زادنا بغيا على ذي قرابة ... غنانا ولا أزرى بأحسابنا الفقر
(Our wealth did not make us transgress against a kinsman, and poverty did not disgrace our lineages.)
(آسى): its origin is أأسى with two hamzas, the second turned into an alif. In al-Miṣbāḥ: أسي أسى (of the pattern تعب) means "he grieved".

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ): its i'rab has already been given. (لَئِنِ اتَّبَعْتُمْ شُعَيْباً إِنَّكُمْ إِذاً لَخاسِرُونَ): the oath clause is in the position of the accusative, being the content of what they said. The lām is the preparatory lām of the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), إن is conditional, and اتبعتم شعيبا is a verb, agent and direct object. إن and its noun; إذن is a particle of answer and consequence that does not govern; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); خاسرون is the khabar of إن. The clause إنكم is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position, and it stands in place of the apodosis of the condition, as is the rule when a condition and an oath come together. (فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دارِهِمْ جاثِمِينَ): the فاء is a conjunction; أخذتهم الرجفة is a verb, direct object and agent; فأصبحوا is conjoined to فأخذتهم; the wāw is the noun of أصبحوا and جاثمين its khabar; في دارهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاثمين. (الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا شُعَيْباً كَأَنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيهَا): a resumptive clause explaining the reality of these deniers. الذين is a mubtadaʾ, the clause كذبوا شعيبا is the ṣila, كأن is the lightened form of the heavy كأنّ, its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause لم يغنوا فيها is its khabar. (الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا شُعَيْباً كانُوا هُمُ الْخاسِرِينَ): الذين is a mubtadaʾ, the clause كذبوا شعيبا is the ṣila, and the clause كانوا is the khabar of الذين. This repetition in the mubtadaʾ and khabar is an intensification in rebutting their partisans and in declaring their opinions foolish, and an announcement that what is mentioned within the ṣila is what made them deserve the two punishments. It was attributed to the relative noun in order to magnify (the matter) for those who were not listeners, for the loss of those who denied him indicates the felicity of those who believed him, and this entails the exaltation of Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, who is neither the speaker nor the one addressed in this setting. (فَتَوَلَّى عَنْهُمْ وَقالَ: يا قَوْمِ لَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ رِسالاتِ رَبِّي): the فاء is a conjunction; تولى is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تولى; وقال is conjoined to تولى; the clause لقد أبلغتكم رسالات ربي is the content of the saying; رسالات is the second direct object of أبلغتكم. (وَنَصَحْتُ لَكُمْ فَكَيْفَ آسى عَلى قَوْمٍ كافِرِينَ): conjoined to what precedes; the فاء is resumptive; كيف is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); آسى is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; على قوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آسى; and كافرين is an adjective of قوم.

* Rhetoric:
The verse describes the state of the soul in its wavering. His grief for his people had grown intense; then he rebuked himself and said: how can my grief be intense for a people who are not worthy of being grieved over, because of their disbelief, their persistence in tyranny, and their deserving what befell them? Then this was interspersed with a return to blaming them. He means: "He who warns has excused himself", and he had done the utmost that one zealous for his people can do, short of plunging into the manifold wildernesses of ignorance and its ruinous perils.

dervis-irab:94-96.t:
* Vocabulary:
(عَفَوْا): they became many and grew, in themselves and in their wealth, from the saying عفا النبات, عفا الشحم, and عفا الوبر when they become abundant. It is said: عفا means "became abundant", and عفا means "was effaced"; so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād). In al-Miṣbāḥ it is said that it is both transitive and intransitive, and it is also made transitive by the hamza, so one says أعفيته.

* I'rab:
(وَما أَرْسَلْنا فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is a new sentence, uttered to explain the circumstances of the nations in a general manner, so that together with the story it may be a warning to those warned. ما is negative; أرسلنا is a verb and agent; من is a redundant preposition (ḥarf jarr zāʾid); and نبيّ is genitive in form and accusative in position as a direct object. (إِلَّا أَخَذْنا أَهْلَها بِالْبَأْساءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَضَّرَّعُونَ): إلا is a particle of restriction, so the exception is an emptied (mufarraghan) one, from the most general of circumstances; thus the clause أخذنا is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with an implied "qad", as is the condition for a past verb to occur as a ḥāl, and its discussion has already preceded.
The implied sense is: "We did not send in any town of the destroyed towns any prophet of the prophets in any circumstance except the circumstance of Our having seized (its people)." أهلها is a direct object; بالبأساء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخذنا; الضراء is conjoined to البأساء; لعلهم: لعل and its noun; the clause يضّرّعون is its khabar; and the clause لعلهم يضرعون is a ḥāl clause.
(ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنا مَكانَ السَّيِّئَةِ الْحَسَنَةَ): ثم is a particle of conjunction and delay; بدلنا is conjoined to أخذنا and falls under its ruling. مكان is the direct object of بدلنا, السيئة is a muḍāf ilayhi, and الحسنة is the second direct object; and this is what prevented its being put in the accusative as an adverbial, for الحسنة is the thing taken and obtained, while مكان السيئة is the thing left and gone, and it is that which the preposition باء accompanies in a construction such as this, as has been verified before in (Sūrat) al-Baqara. (حَتَّى عَفَوْا وَقالُوا: قَدْ مَسَّ آباءَنَا الضَّرَّاءُ وَالسَّرَّاءُ): حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive; عفوا is a past verb with its agent; the interpreted maṣdar, governed in the genitive by (an implied) أن, is attached to بدلنا; وقالوا is conjoined to عفوا; the clause قد مس is the content of the saying; آباءنا is a direct object; and الضراء and السراء are conjoined to it. (فَأَخَذْناهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ): فأخذناهم is conjoined to عفوا; بغتة is a ḥāl or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; the wāw in وهم is circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ; the clause لا يشعرون is the khabar; and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْقُرى آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا لَفَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكاتٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ): the wāw is resumptive; لو is conditional, merely for linking; أن and its noun; the clause آمنوا is its khabar; أن and what follows is the agent of an omitted verb, i.e. "their faith was established"; the lām in لفتحنا occurs in the answer to لو; فتحنا is a verb and agent, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فتحنا; بركات is a direct object; and من السماء والأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of بركات. (وَلكِنْ كَذَّبُوا فَأَخَذْناهُمْ بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; لكن is a particle of rectification that does not govern; كذبوا is a verb and agent, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl; فأخذناهم: the فاء is a conjunction, and أخذناهم is a verb, agent and direct object; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخذناهم; ما is a maṣdar particle or a relative; كان and its noun; the clause يكسبون is the khabar; and the clause of "being" is the ṣila of "ما", or the interpreted maṣdar, with no grammatical position after the particle-type relative.

dervis-irab:97-99.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَياتاً): بيات can mean "spending the night" (بيتوتة), as one says بات بياتا; it may also mean "causing to spend the night" (تبييت), like سلام in the sense of تسليم; one says بيته العدو بياتا. So it is permissible that the meaning be: "Our might comes to them while they spend the night", or "at the time of night-spending", or "as night-attackers", or "as night-attacked". And بيات is the assault on enemies by night.
(الضُّحى): the intensifying of the sun and the lengthening of the day. One says ضحي, and one says ضحى and ضحاء; if you give it a ḍamma you shorten it, and if you give it a fatḥa you lengthen it.

* I'rab:
(أَفَأَمِنَ أَهْلُ الْقُرى): the hamza is for an interrogation of denial and rebuke; the فاء is conjoined to أخذناهم بغتة, and what lies between them, namely His saying "ولو أن أهل القرى", is a parenthetical clause between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined. It has already been said that in a construction like this the conjunction is intended to come first, and was delayed only because the hamza was put before it, owing to the hamza's strength in standing at the head of the speech. أمن أهل القرى is a verb and agent. (أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ بَأْسُنا بَياتاً وَهُمْ نائِمُونَ): the maṣdar أن and what is within its scope is the object of أمن; بأسنا is the agent of يأتيهم; بياتا is a ḥāl or an adverbial; the wāw is circumstantial; هم نائمون is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in يأتيهم. (أَوَأَمِنَ أَهْلُ الْقُرى أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ بَأْسُنا ضُحًى وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ): conjoined to the preceding clause, like it in i'rab; ضحى is an adverb of time attached to يأتيهم. (أَفَأَمِنُوا مَكْرَ اللَّهِ): its i'rab has already been given; the repetition is for greater denunciation and rebuke, and the meaning of the "plan of Allah" has been discussed before. (فَلا يَأْمَنُ مَكْرَ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْخاسِرُونَ): the فاء is a conjunction; لا is negative; يأمن مكر الله is a verb and direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction; القوم is the agent; and الخاسرون is an adjective.

dervis-irab:180-186.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْحُسْنى): the feminine of aḥsan (best), like al-kubrā and al-ṣughrā. It was also said that al-ḥusnā is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description, like al-rujʿā, and it is put in the singular just as the description of what is non-rational is put in the singular in His saying: «ولي فيها مآرب أخرى» ("and I have other uses in it"); had it been made to agree [in number], the better construction would have been as in His saying: «من أيام أخر» ("from other days").
(يُلْحِدُونَ): the imperfect of alḥada, meaning to incline and deviate.
(سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ): We shall draw them gradually closer to what will destroy them. Istidrāj is moving [something] step by step, from al-daraj, which is folding; from it comes daraja al-thawb, "he folded the garment."
(وَأُمْلِي): Imlāʾ is granting respite and prolonging.
(جِنَّةٍ): with kasra on the jīm and shadda on the nūn: that is, madness.

* I'rab:
(وَلِلَّهِ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى فَادْعُوهُ بِها): The wāw is resumptive; «ولله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted predicate (khabar); «الأسماء» is a postponed subject (mubtadaʾ); «الحسنى» is an adjective (naʿt). «فادعوه»: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ, introducing an implied condition); «ادعوه» is a verb, agent and direct object; «بها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ادعوه». (وَذَرُوا الَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ فِي أَسْمائِهِ): The wāw is a conjunction; «ذروا» is an imperative verb and agent; «الذين» is a relative noun, a direct object; the clause «يلحدون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; «في أسمائه» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "and leave off naming [Him] by those who incline away from the truth and the right in it." (سَيُجْزَوْنَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): «سيجزون» is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); «ما» is a second direct object; the clause «كانوا يعملون» is the ṣila of the relative noun; the clause «يعملون» is the predicate (khabar) of «كانوا». (وَمِمَّنْ خَلَقْنا أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ): The wāw is a conjunction; «ممن» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted predicate; the clause «خلقنا» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «أمة» is a postponed subject; the clause «يهدون بالحق» is an adjective of «أمة»; «به» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يعدلون». (وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; «الذين» is a subject, and the clause «كذبوا» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «بآياتنا» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «كذبوا»; the clause «سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون» is the predicate. You may also put «الذين» in the accusative by an omitted verb, on the principle of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with a pronoun), the implied form being: "We shall draw gradually those who denied," that is, We shall move them step by step from a height to a depth, that is, We bring them close to destruction by giving them respite. «من حيث» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «نستدرجهم»; the clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of a genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ): It is permissible that the wāw be a conjunction, with «أملي» conjoined to «نستدرجهم», in the manner of an iltifāt (shift of person); but what we hold is that it is resumptive, as the predicate of an omitted subject, that is: "and I give them respite"; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أملي»; «إن كيدي متين»: the sentence stands as the justification of His strength, Exalted is He. (أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا ما بِصاحِبِهِمْ مِنْ جِنَّةٍ): The hamza is for rebuking interrogation, and the wāw is a conjunction; «لم» is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; «يتفكروا» is an imperfect verb jussive by «لم»; «ما» is negative; «بصاحبهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted predicate; «من» is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; «جنة» is genitive in form, nominative in position, as a postponed subject; and the clause is in the position of an accusative, being the object of «يتفكروا», which operates upon it, because of the presence of the suspender (muʿalliq) of the verb, namely the negative «ما». It is also permissible that «ما» be interrogative, in the position of a nominative as a subject, with the predicate being «بصاحبهم», and «من جنة» a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ): «إن» is negative; «هو» is a subject; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «نذير» is a predicate; «مبين» is an adjective. (أَوَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا فِي مَلَكُوتِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): The parsing of its like has preceded. «في ملكوت السموات والأرض» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ينظر»; «ما» is conjoined to «ملكوت»; the clause «خلق» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «من شيء» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَأَنْ عَسى أَنْ يَكُونَ قَدِ اقْتَرَبَ أَجَلُهُمْ): The wāw is a conjunction; the clause is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding «ما», that is: "in [the fact] that"; «أن» is the lightened form of the heavy «أنّ», its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and its predicate the clause «عسى»; the noun of «عسى» is a latent pronoun, and «أن» with what follows it is its predicate; the noun of «يكون» is also the pronoun of the matter, and the clause «قد اقترب أجلهم» is its predicate. (فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ يُؤْمِنُونَ): The fāʾ is resumptive; «بأي» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يؤمنون»; the clause is resumptive, put forward to express astonishment, that is: if they do not believe in this discourse, how will they believe in any other! The pronoun refers back to the Qur'an or to the Messenger. (مَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلا هادِيَ لَهُ): «من» is a conditional noun that puts its clause in the jussive, in the position of an accusative as a fronted direct object of «يضلل»; «الله» is the agent; the fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ (of the apodosis); «لا» is the lā of generic negation; «هادي» is its noun; «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted predicate of it. (وَيَذَرُهُمْ فِي طُغْيانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ): The wāw is resumptive; the clause «يذرهم» is resumptive; the hāʾ is a direct object; «في طغيانهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يعمهون»; the clause «يعمهون» is a ḥāl from the hāʾ. It was also read «ويذرهم» in the jussive, conjoined to the position of His saying «فلا هادي له», which is jussive [in position].

dervis-irab:155-157.t:
* Vocabulary:
(هُدْنا): we repented and returned from disobedience and came to You apologizing for it. It is from هاد يهود, "he returned". The root meaning of الهود is "returning gently", and from it the Jews (اليهود) were named. It was a name of praise before their law was abrogated; after that it became a name of blame that clings to them forever, by which they are labelled for all time. الهود is the plural of هائد, which means "one who repents". One of them said:
يا راكب الذّنب هدهد ... واسجد كأنك هدهد
(O you who ride sin, repent [hadhid]; and prostrate yourself as if you were a hoopoe [hudhud].)
He likened his clinging to sin to the rider's clinging to his mount, and likened the one prostrating to the hoopoe, because of how often it bows its head to the ground.
(الْأُمِّيَّ): ascribed to الأم (the mother), as though he remained in the state in which he was born. What is meant by it is the one who neither reads writing nor writes. This description is among the things peculiar to Muhammad ﷺ. It is also possible that the ascription is to الأمة (the nation), namely the Arab nation, because the Arabs neither reckon nor write. It is also possible that it is ascribed to الأم, the verbal noun of أمَّ يؤمُّ, that is "he aimed at, he sets out for"; the meaning on this view is: this noble Arab Prophet is the one whom everyone aims at. If it is asked: the ascription should have been أَمّيّ with fatḥa on the hamza, we say that this is one of the alterations that occur in nisba formations. More on this description will come in the section on benefits.
(الإصر): the heavy burden that binds (يأصر) its bearer, that is, holds him back from movement because of its weight. What is meant by الإصر here is the covenant and pledge taken from the Children of Israel to act according to the rulings of the Torah.
(الْأَغْلالَ): plural of غلّ; الغُلّ with ḍamma is a ring of iron placed on the neck.

* I'rab:
(وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا لِمِيقاتِنا): a resumptive speech, introduced to relate the story of those who did not worship the calf; Allah had commanded him to choose seventy of them. The details are in the longer works. اختار موسى is a verb and agent; قومه is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "from his people": the preposition was omitted and the verb reached it directly; سبعين is the direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of اختار. The discussion has already preceded about the verbs that govern two objects, one of them directly and the other by means of a preposition; these are restricted to what is heard from the Arabs, and they are: اختار, استغفر, أمر, كنى, دعا, زوّج and صدق. Then the preposition is omitted and the verb governs the noun directly. So you say: اخترت زيدا من الرجال and اخترت زيدا الرجال. The poet said:
اخترتك الناس إذ رثّت خلائقهم ... واعتلّ من كان يرجى عند السّول
(I chose you out of the people when their characters grew worn, and he who was hoped for at the time of asking fell ill.)
رجلا is a tamyīz (specification). لميقاتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "for the appointed time at which We promised that they would come, in order to apologize for the worship of the calf".
(فَلَمَّا أَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ): the فاء is a conjunction; لما is a connective (rābiṭa) or temporal; its i'rab has often preceded. أخذتهم الرجفة is a verb, direct object and agent.
(قالَ: رَبِّ لَوْ شِئْتَ أَهْلَكْتَهُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَإِيَّايَ): the clause of speech is resumptive, to explain what Moses said. The clause of the vocative is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl). لو is conditional; شئت is a verb and agent, and the direct object is omitted, i.e. "if You had willed their destruction". أهلكتهم is a verb, agent and direct object, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أهلكتهم. إياي is a detached pronoun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the هاء.
(أَتُهْلِكُنا بِما فَعَلَ السُّفَهاءُ مِنَّا): the interrogative here means negation together with a plea for mercy, i.e. "It is not possible that You would punish us for what others than us did." Al-Mubarrad has a fine expression; he said: "What is meant by the interrogative is the interrogative of magnification" - as if he were saying (Moses knew that no one is destroyed for the sin of another, but it is of the kind of the saying of ʿĪsā: «إن تعذبهم فانهم عبادك»). تهلكنا is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تهلكنا; ما is a relative or maṣdar (verbal noun) particle, i.e. "because of that which the fools did" or "because of the deed of the fools". منا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا فِتْنَتُكَ): إن is negative; هي is the mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction; فتنتك, i.e. "Your trial", is the khabar (predicate).
(تُضِلُّ بِها مَنْ تَشاءُ وَتَهْدِي مَنْ تَشاءُ): the clause is a ḥāl, i.e. "causing to go astray by it and guiding". من is a relative noun in the position of accusative as direct object, and likewise the second «من».
(أَنْتَ وَلِيُّنا فَاغْفِرْ لَنا وَارْحَمْنا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْغافِرِينَ): أنت is the mubtadaʾ and ولينا the khabar. فاغفر: the فاء is the fāṣiḥa (the eloquent فاء, introducing the consequence of an omitted condition); اغفر is an imperative verb expressing supplication; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اغفر; وارحمنا is conjoined to اغفر. وأنت: the واو is circumstantial or resumptive; أنت is the mubtadaʾ and خير الغافرين the khabar.
(وَاكْتُبْ لَنا فِي هذِهِ الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ): واكتب is conjoined to فاغفر; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اكتب; في هذه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; حسنة is the direct object; وفي الآخرة is conjoined to «في هذه الدنيا», and the first object suffices, i.e. "and in the Hereafter a good (reward)".
(إِنَّا هُدْنا إِلَيْكَ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to give the reason for the supplication, because that is among the things that make it deserve acceptance. إن and its noun; the clause هدنا إليك is the khabar of إن.
(قالَ عَذابِي أُصِيبُ بِهِ مَنْ أَشاءُ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to make known Allah's answer. عذابي is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause أصيب; or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ and the clause أصيب is a ḥāl. به is a preposition and its genitive noun; من is a relative noun, a direct object; the clause أشاء is the ṣila (relative clause).
(وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ): conjoined to the preceding clause.
(فَسَأَكْتُبُها لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ): the فاء is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, introduced to allude to his people; the سين is a particle of futurity; اكتبها is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to سأكتبها; the clause يتقون has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative; and the clause ويؤتون الزكاة is conjoined to the clause يتقون.
(وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِآياتِنا يُؤْمِنُونَ): والذين is conjoined to the preceding الذين; هم is the mubtadaʾ and the clause يؤمنون the khabar; بآياتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤمنون; the nominal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative.
(الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الرَّسُولَ النَّبِيَّ الْأُمِّيَّ الَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوباً عِنْدَهُمْ فِي التَّوْراةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ): الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of الذين or a badal (substitute) for it; the clause يتبعون is the ṣila of the relative; الرسول is the direct object; النبي is the first adjective and الأمي the second adjective, and الذي the third adjective; the clause يجدونه has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative; مكتوبا is the second direct object of يجدونه; عندهم is an adverb attached to «مكتوبا»; and في التوراة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(يَأْمُرُهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهاهُمْ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ): the clause is a ḥāl; بالمعروف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأمرهم; and ينهاهم عن المنكر is conjoined to the preceding clause.
(وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ الطَّيِّباتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْخَبائِثَ): conjoined to what preceded.
(وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَالْأَغْلالَ الَّتِي كانَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ): also conjoined; إصرهم is the direct object, and الأغلال is conjoined to إصرهم; التي is an adjective of الأغلال; the clause كانت عليهم is a ṣila; and عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of كانت.
(فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِهِ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ): the فاء is resumptive, and الذين is the mubtadaʾ; the clause آمنوا is a ṣila; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا; and عزروه and نصروه are conjoined to آمنوا.
(وَاتَّبَعُوا النُّورَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مَعَهُ): واتبعوا is also conjoined; النور is the direct object; الذي is an adjective; the clause أنزل is a ṣila; and معه is an adverb of place attached to أنزل.
(أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ): the nominal clause is the khabar of the relative noun; the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second mubtadaʾ; and المفلحون is the khabar of أولئك, or the khabar of «هم», and the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك.

* Benefits:
The meaning of الأميّ:
We spoke at length in the section on vocabulary about the meaning of الأمّيّ, and we now ask with those who ask: did the Prophet know how to read and write? Most of the Orientalists say that the word «أمّيّ» with which the Prophet was described is obscure and does not indicate conclusively that he did not know how to read, and they consider it probable that it is an ascription to the word أمّة (nation), as we mentioned at the proper place.

The false rumours of the Encyclopaedia of Islam:
As for the Encyclopaedia of Islam, it raises another difficulty. In Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt there is the verse: «وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك إذا لارتاب المبطلون». It said: "It indicates that he learned to read in later life, that is, after the revelation of the Qur'an, although the expression is obscure."
It is clear that the expression is not obscure, but the interpretation the Encyclopaedia put forward is corrupt. The wording of the verse is perfectly explicit and perfectly clear - as will come at its proper place - and it indicates, without any ambiguity, that the people of Mecca knew before the revelation came to him that he did not recite any book and did not write with his right hand; had he been so, the falsifiers would have been in doubt, since they would have said that he used to retire by himself, write the Qur'an and prepare it, then go out to the people and recite it to them.
Another verse cited by the Encyclopaedia of Islam is: «وقالوا: أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا». Nothing of what they want to load onto this verse can be understood from it, for it simply indicates that the disbelievers of Quraysh claimed that the Messenger of Allah was writing down what was dictated to him of the tales of the ancients; and not everything the disbelievers claim is correct. Rather, this is an outright attack and a plain slander intended to discredit and to weaken the standing of the Qur'an. Perhaps the Qur'an itself undertook to expose these false rumours in the verse before it, which is: «وقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا إفك افتراه وأعانه عليه قوم آخرون فقد جاءوا ظلما وزورا، وقالوا: أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا، قل: أنزله الذي يعلم السر في السموات والأرض إنه كان غفورا رحيما».

Al-Bājī and the claim that he was not unlettered:
It is not only the Encyclopaedia of Islam and other books of the Orientalists that try to raise these doubts; hints touching on this subject are scattered in Muslim books too. Ibn Kathīr mentioned: "Whoever of the later jurists, such as the judge Abū al-Walīd al-Bājī and those who followed him, claimed that the Prophet, peace be upon him, wrote on the day of al-Ḥudaybiya: «هذا ما قاضى عليه محمد بن عبد الله», what led him to that was a report in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: «ثم أخذ فكتب», and this is to be read in light of the other report: «ثم أمر فكتب». For this reason the denunciation of whoever said the saying of al-Bājī was severe, and they disowned him, recited verses on that subject and preached about it in their gatherings.
