Yet the decisive word in this is what came in the Qur'an itself: it affirmed in many places that the Qur'an was sent down upon the heart of the Messenger of Allah, and that he was charged with memorizing it, and that the Muslims were to memorize it, not to write it: «فإنه نزله على قلبك بإذن الله مصدّقا لما بين يديه». So the Prophet did not write what was revealed to him, and we do not know precisely how the Qur'an was written in the Meccan period.

The story of ʿUmar's conversion to Islam:
But we do mention the widespread report that tells of the conversion of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: that he found in the hand of his sister Fāṭima a leaf (ṣaḥīfa) bearing verses of the Qur'an. Although there are other reports that omit the story of Fāṭima and what happened between her and ʿUmar, we may rely on it to learn that there were leaves on which parts of the Qur'an were written, whether those leaves were with Fāṭima, ʿUmar's sister, or with someone else. The word صحيفة does not denote paper as we know it today, but it is in any case something light to carry on which one writes easily. The word صحيفة occurs in the Qur'an, as in His saying, the Exalted: «في صحف مكرّمة مرفوعة مطهرة». Yet memorization was the basis of knowledge of the Qur'an, and it is not recitation from written pages, but rather «آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم».
More of this delicate topic will come in particular places in this book.

dervis-irab:130-132.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السنون): the plural of سنة (year), which is twelve months. It is pluralised as سنين, سنوات and سنهات; its diminutive is سنيّة, سنينة and سنيهة; the relative adjective derived from it is سنويّ and سنهيّ. The plural is declined with letters (wāw/yāʾ and nūn), by analogy with the sound masculine plural, and it is sometimes declined with vowel marks. سنة also means drought and famine, and verbs have been derived from it: they said أسنت القوم, meaning "the people suffered drought and famine".
(يَطَّيَّرُوا): the original form is يتطيروا; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ because they are close in articulation. التطيّر, as in the lexicons, means pessimism, taking evil omens. Its origin is that wealth was distributed and "flew" (yaṭīr) among the people, so that each one's share and portion "flew" to him; the word was then applied predominantly to an evil share and lot.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ بِالسِّنِينَ): The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, introduced to begin the detailed account of how they were destroyed and of the events that preceded it. The lām is the lām of an omitted oath (the answer to an omitted oath), and قد is a particle of certainty. أخذنا is a verb and agent; آل فرعون is the direct object (mafʿūl bihi); بالسنين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخذنا. (وَنَقْصٍ مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ): The wāw is a conjunction; نقص is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السنين; من الثمرات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نقص — what is meant is the destruction of the harvest by various blights. لعل and its noun; the clause يذكرون is its predicate; the clause لعلهم يتذكرون is circumstantial (ḥāl). (فَإِذا جاءَتْهُمُ الْحَسَنَةُ قالُوا: لَنا هذِهِ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb of the future containing the sense of a condition; the clause جاءتهم الحسنة is in the position of a genitive as the second term of an annexation (muḍāf ilayhi) — what is meant is the ease and fertility that befell them; the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted predicate; هذه is a demonstrative in the position of nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is in the position of accusative as the content of their saying (maqūl qawlihim). (وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَطَّيَّرُوا بِمُوسى وَمَنْ مَعَهُ): The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; تصبهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the هاء being the direct object, and سيئة the agent; يطيروا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); بموسى is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يطّيّروا; من is conjoined to موسى; معه is an adverb of place attached to an omitted element, which has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (أَلا إِنَّما طائِرُهُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): ألا is a particle of opening and alerting; إنما is a restricting particle (kāffa) together with the restricted one (makfūfa); طائرهم is the mubtadaʾ; عند الله is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar; and the clause is resumptive, uttered by Him, Exalted is He, in rebuttal of their claim, and to state that what befell them is a just recompense for their evil deeds recorded with Him. (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): The wāw is circumstantial; لكن and its noun; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl, and the clause لا يعلمون is the predicate of لكنّ. (وَقالُوا: مَهْما تَأْتِنا بِهِ مِنْ آيَةٍ لِتَسْحَرَنا بِها): The wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a verb and agent; مهما is a jussive-conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; تأتنا is the protasis, with its direct object; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تأتنا; من آية is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; لتسحرنا: the lām is the lām of purpose, and تسحرنا is an imperfect verb put in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām of purpose, with نا as its direct object; the preposition and its genitive noun «the lām of purpose and the interpreted maṣdar after it» are attached to تأتنا; and بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تسحرنا. (فَما نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ): The fāʾ links to the apodosis; ما is a negative in the Ḥijāzī manner (working like laysa); نحن and its noun; لك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مؤمنين; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and مؤمنين is genitive in form but accusative in position because it is the predicate of «ما». The clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the clause of the protasis and its apodosis is the predicate of مهما.

* Rhetoric:
In the definiteness of الحسنة and the indefiniteness of سيئة there is a wondrous art among the arts of the science of meanings (ʿilm al-maʿānī). He made الحسنة definite and mentioned it with the particle of certainty because of how frequently it occurs and because the will is bound to bringing it about, whereas He made سيئة indefinite and brought it with a particle of doubt because of its rarity and because it is not intended, except incidentally. Between الحسنة and السيئة there is a beautiful antithesis (ṭibāq).

* Benefits:
1- Superstition (al-ṭiyara): We gave the lexical sense of الطِّيَرة in the Vocabulary section. Psychologists then settled on a more established meaning for it, regarding it as an illness belonging to the branch of fear-disorders arising from weakness and disorder of the nerves, though it is a particular fear with its own causes and symptoms, the first of which is weakness of the nerves. The healthy man does not take omens or pessimistic views, because he expects good from the world and feels no estrangement between himself and it, and hence he feels no fear of it and no superstition about it. One may regard ṭiyara as a temporary pessimism summoned by sudden circumstances and by an atmosphere suited to passing states of despair and gloom, so that the superstitious man borrows in advance the terror of an evil before it happens.

Ibn al-Rūmī, the poet of superstition:
Among our poets famous for superstition was Ibn al-Rūmī. He felt deep within himself that he was a timid, wary man, and at the same time felt that his wariness did not ward off from him what was intended for him; yet he saw that he had no alternative to holding fast to it, and so that he might feel the security that had gone and the trembling anxiety:
فآمن ما يكون المرء يوما ... إذا لبس الحذار من الخطوب
(The man is safest on any day when he has put on wariness against misfortunes.)
Some critics see among the tributaries of superstition in Ibn al-Rūmī a taste for beauty and the association of ideas. The soul that is naturally disposed to savour beauty rejoices and exults at enticing, captivating sights, and conversely recoils and contracts at ugly, deformed ones. As for the association of ideas, its possessor is prey to impulses, exposed to groundless interpretations, drawing from whispered words or passing thoughts matters against which a man is wary and which he fears. Ibn al-Rūmī used to take his friend Jaʿfar as an ill omen during his illness, though he did not do so before the illness. He claimed that Jaʿfar was derived from "hunger" (jūʿ) and "flight" (firār), and that «al-khān» (the inn) reminded him of betrayal (khiyāna):
فكم خان سفر خان فانقضّ فوقهم ... كما انقضّ صقر الدجن فوق الأرانب
(How many travellers did the inn betray, for it swooped down upon them as the falcon of the overcast day swoops upon hares.)
He said about Ibn Ṭālib the scribe:
وهل أشبه المرّيخ إلا وفعله ... لفعل نذير السوء شبه مقارب
وهل يتمارى الناس في شؤم كاتب ... لعينيه لون السيف والسيف قاصب
ويدعى أبوه طالبا وكفاكم ... به طيرة أن المنيّة طالب
ألا فاهربوا من طالب وابن طالب ... فمن طالب مثليهما طار هارب
(Is he like Mars except that his deed closely resembles the deed of the herald of evil? Do people doubt the ill omen of a scribe whose eyes have the colour of the sword, and the sword is cutting? His father is called Ṭālib ("seeker") — and that is omen enough for you, that death is a seeker. So flee from Ṭālib and the son of Ṭālib; whoever is sought by the likes of those two flies away in flight.)
In the ḥadīth, the Prophet ﷺ liked good omens (al-fāl) and disliked superstition (al-ṭiyara). It is related with a raised chain: "When you suspect, do not verify, ... and when you take an ill omen, go ahead and put your trust in Allah." Among the curious tales of the superstitious is what is told that stars fell in the time of one of the caliphs, and he took it as an ill omen. He summoned the astrologers and the scholars, but they gave no answer. Then a poet said:
هذي النجوم تساقطت ... لرجوم أعداء الأمير
(These stars have fallen to stone the enemies of the emir.)
So he took it as a good omen and ordered a splendid gift for him.
2- What is said about مهما: Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about «مهما» and he said: It is «ما» with another «ما» added to it, but they found the repetition of a single word ugly, so they replaced the first one's alif with a hāʾ. Some scholars have argued that it is a particle, from the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā:
ومهما تكن عند امرئ من خليقة ... وإن خالها تخفى على الناس تعلم
(Whatever trait a man may have, even if he thinks it hidden from people, becomes known.)
These scholars parse «خليقة» as the noun of تكن, with من redundant, so the verb is necessarily devoid of a pronoun, and «مهما» has no grammatical position, since only the position of mubtadaʾ would suit it, and that is impossible for want of a link (rābiṭ); and when it is established that it has no position, it must be a particle. The truth is that the noun of تكن is latent, «من خليقة» is an explanation of مهما, مهما is the mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar. In the verse the two pronouns in «به» and «بها» both refer to مهما, except that one is masculine according to the form of the word and the other feminine according to the meaning, because it has the sense of the verse (āya).
What al-Zamakhsharī denied — that «مهما» is not used as an adverb of time — was held by Ibn Mālik, who mentioned it in al-Tashīl and in his other works. He did not, however, restrict its meaning to an adverb of time; rather he said: «ما» and «مهما» may occur as adverbs of time. In his long rajaz poem called al-Shāfiya al-Kāfiya he said:
وقد أتت مهما وما ظرفين في ... شواهد من يعتضد بها كفى
(Both «مهما» and «ما» have occurred as adverbs in attestations; whoever relies on them is satisfied.)
In his commentary on the verse he said: All the grammarians make «ما» and «مهما» like «من» in being free of adverbial use, although their use as adverbs is established in the usage of the eloquent Arabs. He recited verses from the Arabs in which he claimed that «ما» and «مهما» are two adverbs of time. His son, the Shaykh Badr al-Dīn ibn Muḥammad, has spared us the refutation of him; we ourselves have also interpreted some of them differently and mentioned that in our book al-Takmīl li-Sharḥ al-Tashīl. It is enough of a refutation that he himself related, from all the grammarians, the opposite of what he said; but whoever practises a science needs to stand before the shaykhs. As for whoever explained «مهما» in the verse as an adverb of time, he is, as al-Zamakhsharī said, an impious deviator concerning the verses of Allah.
[Translator's note: the source text reads «هما» here, where «مهما» is evidently meant; the translation follows what is written.]
The words of al-Zamakhsharī:
"This word is among the words distorted by one who has no hand in the science of Arabic, who puts it in the wrong place and supposes «مهما» to mean «متى ما» and says «مهما جئتني أعطيتك» ('whenever you come to me I will give you'). That is his own invention and is not at all from the speech of the founders of Arabic. Then he goes and explains «مهما تأتني به من آية» with the meaning of time, and so he deviates impiously concerning the verses of Allah without realising it. This and its like make it necessary to kneel before the student of Sībawayh's book."

dervis-irab:133-136.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الطُّوفانَ): The statements of the lexicographers differ about it. Some said: it is a generic noun (ism jins), like قمح and قمحة (wheat), شعير and شعيرة (barley). It was also said that it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) like النقصان and الرجحان, which is the view of al-Mubarrad. In the language it is applied to a drowning water or flood, to the intensity of the darkness of night, and to sweeping, devastating death. And الطوفان of anything is whatever is abundant.
(الْجَرادَ): the plural of جرادة; the male and the female are the same in it. One says: جرادة ذكر and جرادة أنثى, like نملة and حمامة. It has two kinds: the flier, which is the one that mostly flies, and the crawler.
(الْقُمَّلَ): The statements about it differ greatly. It was said: it is ticks. It was said: a creature resembling them but smaller. It was said: it is the weevil that comes out of wheat. It was said: a kind of locust smaller than it. And it was said: it is القَمل, with fatḥa on the qāf, the louse found on a person's body and clothes, in which case there are two dialectal forms in it.
(الضَّفادِعَ): the plural of ضفدع, on the pattern of درهم; the dāl may also take kasra, giving the pattern of زبرج. The ضفدع is feminine and not masculine, so the masculine and feminine are distinguished by the adjective: one says ضفدع ذكر and ضفدع أنثى; the plural is ضفادع and ضفادي.
(الرِّجْزُ): the punishment.

* I'rab:
(فَأَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمُ الطُّوفانَ وَالْجَرادَ وَالْقُمَّلَ وَالضَّفادِعَ وَالدَّمَ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; أرسلنا is a verb and agent; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أرسلنا; الطوفان is the direct object, and what follows is conjoined to it. (آياتٍ مُفَصَّلاتٍ فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا وَكانُوا قَوْماً مُجْرِمِينَ): آيات is a ḥāl from the five things mentioned, and مفصلات is an adjective; فاستكبروا is conjoined to أرسلنا; وكانوا قوما مجرمين: كان and its noun, قوما its predicate, and مجرمين an adjective. (وَلَمَّا وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّجْزُ): The wāw is a conjunction; لما is a linking particle (rābiṭa) or a temporal one («when»); وقع is a past verb; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to وقع; الرجز is the agent; the clause وقع has no grammatical position, or is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (قالُوا يا مُوسَى ادْعُ لَنا رَبَّكَ بِما عَهِدَ عِنْدَكَ): the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; يا is a vocative particle; موسى is a vocative, a proper noun in the singular form; ادع is an imperative; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ادع»; ربك is the direct object; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ادع», and ما is a maṣdar particle or a relative; the clause عهد has no grammatical position in any case; عندك is an adverb of place attached to عهد. (لَئِنْ كَشَفْتَ عَنَّا الرِّجْزَ لَنُؤْمِنَنَّ لَكَ): The lām is the lām that prepares for an oath; إن is conditional; كشفت is a past verb and agent, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis; عنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كشفت; الرجز is the direct object; لنؤمنن: the lām is the answer to the oath, and نؤمنن is an imperfect verb indeclinable on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; لك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نؤمننّ. (وَلَنُرْسِلَنَّ مَعَكَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): conjoined to what precedes; معك is an adverb of place attached to نرسلن; بني إسرائيل is the direct object. (فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنا عَنْهُمُ الرِّجْزَ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is a linking or temporal particle; the clause كشفنا has no position, or is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; كشفنا is a verb and agent; الرجز is the direct object; عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كشفنا. (إِلى أَجَلٍ هُمْ بالِغُوهُ إِذا هُمْ يَنْكُثُونَ): إلى أجل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; هم is a mubtadaʾ; بالغوه is its khabar; the nominal clause is an adjective of أجل; إذا is the particle of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya) — it was mentioned earlier that we preferred the view that it is a particle; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause ينكثون is its khabar; the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. Sībawayh took this verse as evidence that «لما» is a particle of "occurrence because of occurrence" (ḥarf wujūb li-wujūb), that is, a linking particle and not an adverb meaning «when» — as some claimed — because (as an adverb) it would need an operator governing it, and it does not admit an implied one, and what follows إذا of surprise does not govern what precedes it. (فَانْتَقَمْنا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْناهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ): فانتقمنا is a conjoined clause; منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to انتقمنا; فأغرقناهم is also conjoined; في اليم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أغرقناهم. (بِأَنَّهُمْ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَكانُوا عَنْها غافِلِينَ): بأنهم: the bāʾ and what is within its scope form a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أغرقناهم, the bāʾ having the sense of cause, i.e. "because of the fact that"; the clause كذبوا is the khabar of أن; كانوا is conjoined to كذبوا; عنها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to غافلين; and غافلين is the khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
The secret of the use of «القمّل»:
The word «القمّل» occurs in a verse of the Qur'an as good and pleasing, whereas it occurs in a line of al-Farazdaq as not good, but repellent. It is:
من عزّه احتجزت كليب عنده ... زربا كأنهم لديه القمّل
(Through his might Kulayb sheltered in his presence in a pen, as though they were, beside him, lice.)
The word is good in the verse and not in the poem only because in the verse it comes embedded within well-proportioned speech and the speech does not stop at it, while in the poem it comes as the rhyme-word, that is, the end at which the speech stops. The verse contains five words: الطوفان, الجراد, القمل, الضفادع and الدم. The best of these five are الطوفان, الجراد and الدم. When the five were mentioned together, الطوفان and الجراد were put first and the word الدم last, and القمل and الضفادع were placed in the middle, so that the ear is first struck by the good among the five words and ends with it. Moreover the word «الدم» is better than «الطوفان» and «الجراد» and lighter in usage, which is why it was brought last. Observing such secrets and subtleties in the use of words is beyond human ability.

dervis-irab:100-102.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَهْدِ): "makes clear", from هدى يهدي.

* I'rab:
(أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لِلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ أَهْلِها): the hamza is for an interrogation of denial and the wāw is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, reversal (of tense) and jussive; the meaning of يهدي is "to become clear", and it is jussive by "لم"; للذين is attached to يهد; the clause يرثون الأرض is the ṣila; and من بعد أهلها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يرثون. (أَنْ لَوْ نَشاءُ أَصَبْناهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ): أن here is the lightened form of the heavy أنّ, its noun is the pronoun of the matter, and the clause نشاء is its khabar; أن and what follows is the agent of يهد. It is also permissible that the agent of "يهد" be a latent pronoun, namely the pronoun for "Allah", or a pronoun referring back to what is understood from the context of the speech, i.e. "Did what happened to the earlier nations not make clear...?"; in that case أن and what is within its scope are, in interpretation, a maṣdar in the position of the object. On the first view the implied sense is: "Did Allah not make clear and explain to those who inherit their end and the outcome of their affair, (namely) Our striking them for their sins?", and the direct object is omitted as we have supplied it.
On the second view the implied sense is: "Did Allah, or what happened to the nations, not make clear and explain Our striking them, had We willed that?" أصبناهم is a verb, agent and direct object, and بذنوبهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it. (وَنَطْبَعُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is a new sentence. It is not permissible to conjoin it to the answer of "لو", because that would make the sealing negated by the force of "لو", whereas it is established for them. على قلوبهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نطبع. (فَهُمْ لا يَسْمَعُونَ): the فاء is a conjunction, expressing that the not-hearing follows upon the sealing of the heart; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يسمعون is its khabar. (تِلْكَ الْقُرى نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبائِها): تلك is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; القرى is a badal of تلك; and the clause نقص is the khabar of تلك. It is also permissible that القرى be the khabar and the clause نقص a ḥāl clause, on the pattern of His saying, the Exalted: «هذا بعلي شيخا»; عليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نقصّ; and من أبنائها [Translator's note: the source prints أبنائها, but the verse reads أَنْبائِها] is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to نقص, and من is partitive, i.e. "some of its tidings", and they have other tidings that We have not related to you. The clause of indication is resumptive, uttered to explain that admonitions and lessons are of no avail with these people, and that sermons have no effect on them, so they died persisting in their obstinacy; no stubbornness of theirs softened and no obstinacy of theirs subsided. (وَلَقَدْ جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ): the wāw is resumptive or conjunctive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; جاءتهم is a verb and direct object; رسلهم is the agent; and بالبينات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاءتهم. (فَما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِما كَذَّبُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ): the فاء is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان and its noun; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); يؤمنوا is an imperfect verb put in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām of denial; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar, i.e. "they were not intending to believe"; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤمنوا; ما is a relative noun or a maṣdar particle; and من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كذبوا. If "ما" is a relative, the returning pronoun is omitted and is in the genitive, like His saying, the Exalted, in Sūrat Yūnus: «فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا به». This belongs to the unity of what is attached, in meaning, and the explanation of its being of that kind is that the whole of "ما كانوا ليؤمنوا" has the meaning of "كذبوا به", so the two attached elements are united in meaning.
It may also be said: His saying, the Exalted, «ليؤمنوا» is made transitive with the particle باء, and يؤمن is the opposite of يكذب, so he treated it like it, for they sometimes take a thing as the opposite of something, as they take it as its like. (كَذلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِ الْكافِرِينَ): the كاف with what follows it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "in the likeness of that sealing upon the hearts of the people of the towns, from whom faith was negated, Allah seals the hearts of the disbelievers who come after them". (وَما وَجَدْنا لِأَكْثَرِهِمْ مِنْ عَهْدٍ): the wāw is parenthetical, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is parenthetical; ما is negative; وجدنا is a verb and agent; لأكثرهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of عهد; من is a redundant preposition; and عهد is, in position, the direct object of وجدنا. It is also permissible that لأكثرهم be the second object of وجدنا, preferring that it is a verb of knowing, not of finding (wijdān). (وَإِنْ وَجَدْنا أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَفاسِقِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن is the lightened form of the heavy إنّ, rarely not governing; it may also govern, with its noun the pronoun of the matter, and its ruling will come in the section on Benefits; وجدنا أكثرهم is a verb, agent and direct object; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); and فاسقين is the second direct object of وجدنا.

* Benefits:
When "إن" with a kasra on the hamza is lightened, it is necessarily made non-governing if a verb follows it, as in His saying, the Exalted: «وإن نظنك لمن الكاذبين». If a noun follows it, the more common case is also that it does not govern, as in: إن أنت لصادق ("You are indeed truthful"); and it is seldom made to govern, as in: إن زيدا لمنطلق. Whenever it is lightened and made non-governing, the lām with a fatḥa necessarily accompanies it, to distinguish it from the negative "إن", and it is called the distinguishing lām.

dervis-irab:103-106.t:
* I'rab:
(ثُمَّ بَعَثْنا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ مُوسى بِآياتِنا إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَائِهِ فَظَلَمُوا بِها): ثم is a particle of conjunction and delay; بعثنا is a verb and agent; من بعدهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, and the pronoun refers to the messengers or to the nations; موسى is a direct object; بآياتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بعثنا; and إلى فرعون is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to بعثنا; ملئه is conjoined to فرعون, i.e. to his people; فظلموا: the فاء is for conjunction and succession; بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ظلموا; and wrongdoing was treated like disbelief because they are of one branch. (فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُفْسِدِينَ): the i'rab of its like has already been given, so renew your acquaintance with it. (وَقالَ مُوسى يا فِرْعَوْنُ إِنِّي رَسُولٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is uttered to detail what was stated in summary earlier. يا is a vocative particle for the middle distance; فرعون is a vocative, a singular proper noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and it is his title, his real name being al-Walīd ibn Muṣʿab ibn al-Rayyān, and his kunya Abū Murra; إن and its noun; and من رب العالمين is its khabar; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying. (حَقِيقٌ عَلى أَنْ لا أَقُولَ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْحَقَّ): حقيق is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "I am worthy (ḥaqīq)", in the sense of "deserving", and the clause is resumptive; على أن لا أقول is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حقيق, because it is a faʿīl form in the sense of fāʿil or mafʿūl; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أقول; إلا is a particle of restriction; and الحق is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except the true saying", and it may be a direct object because it contains the sense of a clause. (قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِبَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): the clause is an adjective of رسول; قد is a particle of affirmation; جئتكم is a verb, agent and direct object; ببينة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جئتكم; and من ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of بينة. (فَأَرْسِلْ مَعِيَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): the فاء is the eloquent فاء (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), i.e. "if you have listened to my words and returned to right guidance, then leave their affair and let go their way, so that they may go with me".
أرسل is an imperative verb; معي is an adverbial attached to أرسل; and بني إسرائيل is a direct object. Moses' aim was to free them from servitude and to deliver them from the bond of captivity and humiliation. (قالَ: إِنْ كُنْتَ جِئْتَ بِآيَةٍ فَأْتِ بِها إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ): the clause قال is resumptive, due to Pharaoh's demand to bring a sign from his Lord, and the conditional clause is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying; إن is conditional; كان and its noun; the clause جئت is the khabar of كنت; بآية is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جئت; the فاء links the apodosis; أت is an imperative verb; بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it; كنت is كان and its noun, in the position of the jussive as the protasis; من الصادقين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of كنت; and the apodosis of إن is omitted because what precedes indicates it, i.e. "then bring it".

* Rhetoric:
Among the practices of the Arabs in their speech is inversion (qalb), and it is of two kinds. The first is turning the literal into the figurative for some reason of exaggeration, and Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī clung to its hem when he said:
والسيف يشقى كما تشقى الضلوع به ... وللسّيوف كما للناس آجال
(The sword suffers as the ribs suffer by it; for swords, as for people, there are appointed terms.)
By the "suffering of the sword" is meant its breaking in the ribs of the one struck, in the manner of his saying in another verse:
طوال الرّدينيّات يقصفها دمي ... وبيض السّريجيّات يقطعها لحمي
(The long Rudaynian spears are broken by my blood, and the white Surayjī swords are cut by my flesh.)
The second kind is bare of this eloquent meaning, as in their saying:
خرق الثوب المسمار, and the like.
(Literally "the garment tore the nail", for "the nail tore the garment".)

dervis-irab:187-188.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السَّاعَةِ): the Resurrection (al-qiyāma). It was so named because it occurs suddenly, or because of the speed of its reckoning, or, on the contrary, because of its length, or because with Allah, for all its length, it is like one of the hours with creation. It is one of the names that have come to be used predominantly for one thing, like al-najm for the Pleiades.
(مُرْساها): a maymī maṣdar (verbal noun with initial mīm) from arsā; irsāʾ is settling and fixing in place. The triliteral verb is rasā; rasā al-shayʾ means the thing became firm, and rasat al-safīna means the ship stopped moving.
(يُجَلِّيها): makes it manifest.
(حَفِيٌّ): one who is excessive in asking. What is meant is as though you had knowledge of it, because one who is excessive in asking about a thing and probing into it has his knowledge of it made firm and solid. This construction means intensification; from it comes iḥfāʾ al-shārib (clipping the moustache closely).

* I'rab:
(يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْساها): A resumptive clause, put forward to show one type of their errors. «يسألونك» is a verb, agent and direct object; «عن الساعة» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يسألونك»; «أيان» is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as a temporal adverbial (ẓarf zamān) — its derivation will come in the section on Benefits — and it is attached to an omitted fronted predicate; «مرساها» is a postponed subject; the clause is a substitute (badal) for «الساعة». It was also said: «أيان» is attached to an omitted [verb], that is, "they ask you [when]", and «مرساها» is the agent of this omitted verb. (قُلْ: إِنَّما عِلْمُها عِنْدَ رَبِّي لا يُجَلِّيها لِوَقْتِها إِلَّا هُوَ): «إنما» consists of a restraining and a restrained element (kāffa and makfūfa); «علمها» is a subject; the adverbial is attached to an omitted predicate; the clause «لا يجليها» is a ḥāl; «لوقتها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يجليها»; the clause «إنما» and what is within its scope is in the position of an accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (what is said); «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «هو» is the agent of «يجليها», or an emphasis (tawkīd) of the latent agent. (ثَقُلَتْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): The clause is resumptive; «في السموات» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ثقلت», whether «في» is in the sense of «على» or in its basic sense of containment; the meaning is that its heaviness occurred — that is, its severity, or the intensity of its concealment — in these two containers, or upon them. (لا تَأْتِيكُمْ إِلَّا بَغْتَةً): The clause is resumptive, confirming the content of what precedes it. «لا تأتيكم» is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «بغتة» is a ḥāl or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (يَسْئَلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنْها): The clause is resumptive, and the secret of this repetition will come in the section on Rhetoric. «يسألونك» is a verb, agent and direct object; the clause «كأنك» is a circumstantial clause (ḥāliyya); «كأن» and its noun, and «حفي» is its predicate; «عنها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «حفي». (قُلْ إِنَّما عِلْمُها عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): Its parsing has been given a little earlier. (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): Its parsing has preceded. (قُلْ: لا أَمْلِكُ لِنَفْسِي نَفْعاً وَلا ضَرًّا إِلَّا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ): The clause is resumptive, put forward to cut off their hopes after he declared that he washed his hands of them. The clause «لا أملك» is in the position of an accusative as the maqūl al-qawl; «لا» is negative, «أملك» is an imperfect verb with a latent agent; «نفعا» is a direct object; «لنفسي» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أملك», or to an omitted ḥāl from «نفعا», because it would originally have been an adjective of it had it been placed after it; «إلا» is a particle of exception; «ما» is excepted from «نفعا وضرا», or a substitute for them. It was also said: the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), in which case the accusative as exception is obligatory. (وَلَوْ كُنْتُ أَعْلَمُ الْغَيْبَ لَاسْتَكْثَرْتُ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ): The wāw is resumptive; «لو» is conditional; «كان» and its noun, and the clause «أعلم» is its predicate; «الغيب» is a direct object; «لاستكثرت»: the lām occurs in the apodosis of «لو»; «استكثرت» is a verb and agent; «من الخير» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «استكثرت»; the clause has no grammatical position. (وَما مَسَّنِيَ السُّوءُ): The wāw is a conjunction; the clause «ما مسني السوء» is conjoined to «استكثرت»; «ما» is negative. (إِنْ أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ وَبَشِيرٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ): «إن» is negative; «أنا» is a subject; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «نذير» is a predicate; «بشير» is conjoined to «نذير»; «لقوم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «نذير» and «بشير»; the clause «يؤمنون» is an adjective of «قوم».

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «يسألونك كأنك حفيّ عنها» there is a kind of repetition (takrīr) that the scholars of rhetoric have not recorded in their discussions of repetition. It is that when speech is built upon a certain purpose, and an interruption comes in the course of it, and then it is desired to return to complete the first purpose, and the connection with it has grown distant, it is refreshed by mentioning the first purpose, so that its end joins its beginning. This has been pointed out before, and this is one such case. For when He began the speech with His saying «يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها», then there intervened the mention of the answer contained in His saying «قل إنما علمها عند ربي» up to His saying «بغتة», it was desired to complete their question about it with a form of rebuke against them, which is what is contained in His saying «كأنك حفيّ عنها»; this is closely tied to the question, and its mention had grown distant, so it was refreshed with a general refreshing. We never see that it is refreshed except in a kind of summary form, like a reminder of the first, dispensing with its detail by what has preceded. Hence it is said «يسألونك» without mentioning what was asked about — namely the Hour — being content with what preceded. And when the question was repeated for this benefit, the answer was repeated too, in summary, and He said: «قل إنما علمها عند الله».

* Benefits:
(أَيَّانَ) has the meaning of «متى» (when), whether it is an interrogative noun or a conditional noun. It was said that its derivation is from «أي», and that it is a fiʿlān form from it, because its meaning is "which time and which act," from «أويت إليه» (I took refuge with him), because a part takes refuge in the whole and leans upon it. This was said by Ibn Jinnī, who refused that it be from «أين», because that is [a term of] time while «أين» is [a term of] place. Others said: the origin of «أيان» is «أي آن», so it is compounded of «أي», which contains the meaning of condition, and «آن», meaning "time"; after compounding they became one noun, conditional in future time, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the redundant «ما» is often attached to it for emphasis, as in his saying:
إذا النعجة الأدماء بانت بقفرة ... فأيّان ما تعدل به الريح تنزل
(When the tawny ewe has left [her place] for a wasteland, then whenever the wind turns her aside, she will alight.)

dervis-irab:137-138.t:
* Vocabulary:
(كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ): They stated that this word is written with the tāʾ majrūra (i.e. the extended tāʾ, tāʾ mabsūṭa), whereas every other such word in the Qur'an is written with the hāʾ, as is the original form. What is meant by "the word" is His, Exalted is He, promise to them in His saying: «ونريد أن نمنّ» and so on.
(يَعْرِشُونَ): with ḍamma on the rāʾ and with kasra; both were recited in the Seven.
That is, they raise up buildings. [This is stated] as a preparation for beginning the story of the Children of Israel and the kinds of disbelief, types of obstinacy and excess that they produced after their rescue from Pharaoh, whose evidences still speak out their realities.

* I'rab:
(وَأَوْرَثْنَا الْقَوْمَ الَّذِينَ كانُوا يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ مَشارِقَ الْأَرْضِ وَمَغارِبَهَا): The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; أورثنا القوم is a verb, agent and direct object; الذين is an adjective of القوم; the clause كانوا is the ṣila of the relative noun; the clause يستضعفون is the khabar of كانوا; يستضعفون is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent; مشارق الأرض is the second direct object; ومغاربها is conjoined to مشارق. (الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ الْحُسْنى عَلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ بِما صَبَرُوا): التي is a relative noun, an adjective of المشارق والمغارب; the clause باركنا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to باركنا; تمت كلمة ربك is conjoined to «أورثنا»; كلمة is the agent; الحسنى is an adjective of كلمة; على بني إسرائيل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تمت; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to صبروا. (وَدَمَّرْنا ما كانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ وَقَوْمُهُ وَما كانُوا يَعْرِشُونَ): The wāw is a conjunction; دمرنا is a verb and agent; ما is a relative noun in the position of accusative as direct object; the clause كان is the ṣila; the noun of كان is a latent pronoun; the clause يصنع is the khabar of كان; فرعون is its agent; وقومه is conjoined to فرعون; «ما» is conjoined to the first «ما»; the clause كانوا يعرشون is the ṣila of «ما», and the clause يعرشون is the khabar of كانوا. (وَجاوَزْنا بِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ الْبَحْرَ): The wāw is resumptive; the speech is resumptive, brought to begin the story of the Children of Israel and the innovations they produced, for the sake of taking a lesson and admonition from the state of man, who is naturally disposed to evil. وببني إسرائيل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاوزنا; البحر is the direct object; and it is permissible that «ببني» be attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فَأَتَوْا عَلى قَوْمٍ يَعْكُفُونَ عَلى أَصْنامٍ لَهُمْ): فأتوا is conjoined to جاوزنا; على قوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أتوا; the clause يعكفون is an adjective of قوم; على أصنام is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يعكفون; ولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of أصنام. (قالُوا: يا مُوسَى اجْعَلْ لَنا إِلهاً كَما لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ): Resumptive speech, brought to show their obstinacy and presumption and their asking for gods and for seeing Allah openly, and other kinds of disobedience. The clause اجعل is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اجعل, or to an omitted first direct object; إلها is the second direct object. In كما the kāf is a preposition, and ما is a relative noun meaning «that which» (alladhī); لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila; آلهة is a substitute (badal) for the latent pronoun in «لهم», the implied meaning being "like that which is established for them, gods"; the kāf and its genitive noun are an adjective of إلها. Al-Zamakhsharī preferred that «ما» be a restricting particle (kāffa) for the kāf, so that it is a kāffa with a makfūfa, and for that reason the clause comes after it. (قالَ: إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ): Resumptive speech to show Moses' answer to them; إن with its noun and khabar; the clause تجهلون is an adjective of قوم; the clause إنكم is the content of the saying.

dervis-irab:158-160.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَسْباطاً): plural of سبط, which is the child of a child, like the grandson (ḥafīd). This is the linguistic understanding; restricting سبط to the daughter's child and ḥafīd to the son's child is a matter of custom. In al-Qāmūs and elsewhere: "the child of a child, and it predominantly applies to the daughter's child, as opposed to ḥafīd, which is the son's child." The سبط among the Jews is in the position of the tribe among the Arabs.
(انبجست): in al-Miṣbāḥ: بجس الماء بجسا, of the pattern قتل, means "I made the water burst forth and it burst forth." Others said: الانبجاس is opening up widely and abundantly. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
وانحلبت عيناه من فرط الأسى ... وكيف غربي دالج تبجّسا
(His eyes streamed from excess of grief, like the dripping of the two buckets of a drawer of water, which burst forth.)
والوكيف is a verbal noun put in the accusative by انحلبت, because its meaning is وكفت (dripped); الغرب is the large bucket; and الدالج is the one who takes the bucket from the well and empties it into the trough. He says: the tears of his eyes poured out because of the intensity of grief, like the pouring of the two buckets of a man who empties them into the trough, bursting forth abundantly. In it the two eyes are likened to the two buckets.
(الْمَنَّ): it is الترنجبين (manna), a sweet substance that used to descend upon them like snow, from dawn until sunrise, and each person would take a ṣāʿ.
(السَّلْوى): it is the quail bird (السّمانى), with the mīm lightened and the final alif shortened (maqṣūra), on the pattern of حبارى. It is a kind of migratory bird, used for both singular and plural. It was also said that the singular is سماناة. It is what is known among us as الفري, and it is also called السلوى; its plural is سمانيات.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعاً): resumptive speech, introduced to direct the address to the Prophet ﷺ. The vocative clause is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech, and its i'rab has already preceded. إن and its noun; رسول الله is its khabar; إليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to رسول; and جميعا is a ḥāl from the pronoun in إليكم.
(الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): the relative noun is a naʿt of الله; it is also possible to cut it off and make it nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. وله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ملك السموات والأرض is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative.
(لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): this clause has no grammatical position because it is a badal (substitute) for the preceding ṣila. The i'rab of the word of testimony has already preceded in detail, with the differing opinions.
(يُحيِي وَيُمِيتُ): the clause is also a badal, so it has no position.
(فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ النَّبِيِّ الْأُمِّيِّ الَّذِي يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَكَلِماتِهِ): the فاء is the fāṣiḥa; آمنوا is an imperative verb; بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا; ورسوله is conjoined to الله; النبي is an adjective, and likewise الأميّ, and likewise [the following]. The clause يؤمن بالله has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative; وكلماته is conjoined to الله, and what is meant by it is what was sent down upon him.
[Translator's note: the source text here has a printing slip. After «والمراد بها ما أنزل عليه» the words «وَاتَّبِعُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ) عطف على الله، والمراد بها ما أنزل عليه» are repeated, and the words «وكذلك وجملة» are muddled. The repeated passage is translated once below.]
(وَاتَّبِعُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ): conjoined to آمنوا; لعل and its noun; the clause تهتدون is its khabar; and the clause of hope is a ḥāl.
(وَمِنْ قَوْمِ مُوسى أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ): the واو is resumptive; ومن قوم موسى is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; أمة is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause يهدون بالحق is an adjective, in the manner of narrating a past state; بالحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "being associated with the truth"; and به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يعدلون.
(وَقَطَّعْناهُمُ اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ أَسْباطاً أُمَماً): the واو is a conjunction; قطعناهم is a verb, agent and direct object; اثنتي عشرة is a ḥāl from the direct object of قطعناهم, i.e. "We divided them, being counted by this number". Al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that قطعناهم means "We made them", in which case اثنتي عشرة would be a second direct object. أسباطا is a badal from اثنتي عشرة, i.e. "a group" (firqa). Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj said: "It is not permissible that it be a tamyīz, because if it were a tamyīz it would be singular." More will be said on it in the section on benefits. أمما is a badal from «أسباطا», so it is a badal from the badal, which is الأسباط.
(وَأَوْحَيْنا إِلى مُوسى إِذِ اسْتَسْقاهُ قَوْمُهُ): conjoined to قطعناهم; إلى موسى is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوحينا; إذ is an adverb of past time, also attached to أوحينا; the clause استسقاه قومه is in the position of genitive by annexation; and استسقاه قومه is a verb, direct object and agent.
(أَنِ اضْرِبْ بِعَصاكَ الْحَجَرَ): it is possible that «أن» is the explicative one for the revelation, because it carries the meaning of saying without its letters; and it is possible that it is the maṣdar one, whose like has already preceded. بعصاك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اضرب, and الحجر is the direct object.
(فَانْبَجَسَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتا عَشْرَةَ عَيْناً): the فاء is the fāṣiḥa, i.e. "he struck, and so there burst forth"; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to انبجست; اثنتا عشرة is the agent of انبجست; and عينا is a tamyīz.
(قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُناسٍ مَشْرَبَهُمْ): the clause is resumptive and has no position; قد is a particle of confirmation; علم كل أناس is a verb and agent; أناس is a muḍāf ilayhi, and it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) whose singular is إنسان; it was also said that it is a broken plural of it; and مشربهم is the direct object.
(وَظَلَّلْنا عَلَيْهِمُ الْغَمامَ وَأَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوى): وظللنا is a verb and agent; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ظللنا; الغمام is the direct object; وأنزلنا is conjoined to ظللنا; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزلنا; المن is the direct object; and السلوى is conjoined to المنّ.
(كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّباتِ ما رَزَقْناكُمْ): the clause كلوا is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech of an omitted saying, i.e. "and We said"; كلوا is an imperative verb and the واو is the agent; من طيبات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كلوا; ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive by annexation to طيبات; and the clause رزقناكم has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative.
(وَما ظَلَمُونا وَلكِنْ كانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ): the واو is resumptive; ما is negative; ظلمونا is a verb, agent and direct object; the واو is circumstantial; لكن is the neglected, lightened one (i.e. it does not act); كان and its noun; أنفسهم is a fronted direct object of يظلمون; and the clause يظلمون is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

* Benefits:
Between al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: the specification of what follows ten is singular, so what is the reason for its coming in the plural? Why was it not said اثني عشر سبطا? I say: if that had been said it would not have been precise, because what is meant is: 'We divided them into twelve tribes', and each tribe is أسباط (several asbāṭ), not a single سبط. So he put «أسباطا» in the place of «قبيلة» (tribe). Its like is: «بين رماحي مالك ونهشل»."
Abū Ḥayyān rejected this comparison with his saying: "It is not its like, because this is the dual of a plural, which is not permissible except in poetic necessity." It is as if he is pointing out that, had it not been taken into account in the plural that a kind of spears was intended, dualizing it would not have been sound; likewise here, the plural أسباط was taken to have the meaning of "tribe", so it was used as the specifier as a singular is used.

The opinion of al-Ḥawfī:
Al-Ḥawfī said: "It is possible that it is by omission, the implied form being اثنتي عشرة فرقة (twelve groups), and «أسباطا» is an adjective of فرقة, then the described was omitted and the adjective put in its place." A parallel for describing a singular tamyīz by a plural out of regard for the meaning is the saying of ʿAntara:
فيها اثنتان وأربعون حلوبة ... سودا كخافية الغراب الأسحم
(In it are forty-two milch camels, black like the wing-feather of the jet-black raven.)
He did not say سوداء (feminine singular).

The opinion of al-Tawḍīḥ and al-Taṣrīḥ:
In al-Tawḍīḥ and al-Taṣrīḥ: "As for His saying, the Exalted, «وقطعناهم اثنتي عشرة أسباطا أمما», أسباطا is not a tamyīz because it is a plural. It is only a badal (total substitute) from «اثنتي عشرة», and the tamyīz is omitted, i.e. اثنتي عشرة فرقة. Had أسباطا been a tamyīz of اثنتي عشرة, the two numerals would have been mentioned in the masculine and it would have been said اثني عشر, with both of them masculine and stripped of the feminine marker, because the سبط - the singular of الأسباط - is masculine."

The opinion of Ibn Mālik:
Ibn Mālik claimed in Sharḥ al-Kāfiya that there is no omission and that «أسباطا» is a tamyīz, and that two things favoured feminine agreement in «أسباطا», because it was described by «أمما», plural of أمة, just as the feminine was favoured in «شخوص» (masculine) when كاعبان ومعصر were mentioned in the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
فكان مجّني دون من كنت أتّقي ... ثلاث شخوص كاعبان ومعصر
(My shield against those I feared was three persons: two maidens with swelling breasts and one just reaching puberty.)
By analogy it should have been «ثلاثة شخوص», because الشخص is masculine; but when he explained it by كاعبان ومعصر - both feminine - he favoured its being feminine. And what the versifier [Ibn Mālik] mentioned about the verse contradicts what he said in Sharḥ al-Tasḥīl, that «أسباطا» is a badal and not a tamyīz.
[Translator's note: the sentence beginning "وزعم ابن مالك ... وإن ذكرا مما رجح حكم التأنيث" is garbled in the source; it is rendered as closely as the text allows.]
This view of substitution from اثنتي عشرة is problematic given their rule that the thing substituted from is generally in the intention of being discarded; and had it been said "and We divided them into tribes", the point of the quantity of the number would be lost, and it would be taken to a non-general case, and it is not permissible to interpret the Qur'an by it.
The view that it is a tamyīz is problematic given their rule that the tamyīz of a compound number is singular, whereas «أسباطا» is plural. Al-Ḥawfī said: "It is possible that «أسباطا» is an adjective of فرقة, then the described was omitted and the adjective put in its place, and «أمما» is an adjective of «أسباطا»; and the number is feminine though it applies to الأسباط, which is masculine, because it has the meaning of فرقة and أمة, as in: ثلاثة أنفس, meaning men." End of quotation. So he committed to describing with a non-derived noun (jāmid), while the more frequent is the opposite. Al-Farrāʾ held that the pluralization of the tamyīz is permissible, and the apparent sense of the verse supports him.

2 - The ruling of the compound number:
أحد عشر up to تسعة عشر are indeclinable (mabnī), except اثني عشر; and the ruling for the last of its two parts is the ruling of the dual nūn, and for this reason it is not annexed in the manner of its sisters, so one does not say هذه اثنا عشرك, as one says هذه أحد عشرك. As for «اثنا عشر», the first noun is declinable (muʿrab), because the second noun has taken the place of the nūn in it, so the change occurs on the alif together with the noun with which it was built, just as the change occurs on it with the nūn. In the feminine of these compounds you say: إحدى عشرة, اثنتا عشرة or ثنتا عشرة, ثلاث عشرة, and ثماني عشرة; the feminine marker is retained in one of the two parts to place them in the position of one thing; and you decline اثنتين as you decline الاثنين.
As for the شين of العشرة, the people of the Ḥijāz put sukūn on it and Banū Tamīm put kasra on it. The Arabs fatḥa the yā' in «ثماني عشرة», and some of them put sukūn on it.

dervis-irab:107-112.t:
* I'rab:
(فَأَلْقى عَصاهُ فَإِذا هِيَ ثُعْبانٌ مُبِينٌ): the فاء is a conjunction of succession; ألقى is a past verb; عصاه is a direct object; فإذا: the فاء is likewise a conjunction, and إذا is the "sudden" إذا (al-fujāʾiyya), which has already been discussed; the grammarians took three views of it: an adverb of place, an adverb of time, or a particle. هي is a mubtadaʾ, ثعبان the khabar, and مبين an adjective. (وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ فَإِذا هِيَ بَيْضاءُ لِلنَّاظِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; نزع يده is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object, i.e. he drew it out of his collar-opening (jayb), which is the neckband of his shirt; the فاء is a conjunction; إذا is sudden; هي is a mubtadaʾ; بيضاء is the khabar; and للناظرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بيضاء. The meaning is: "and behold, it was white to the onlookers, with a wondrous, dazzling whiteness that broke the ordinary course, although he was very dark-skinned (ādam), i.e. of strong brownness." You may also attach the preposition and its genitive noun to an omitted adjective of بيضاء. (قالَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْ قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّ هذا لَساحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ): a new sentence, uttered so that the chiefs of his people might announce their amazement. There is no contradiction between what appears here, that the speech issued from them, and what appears in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ, where it is ascribed to Pharaoh, for he may have been the speaker and they reported his words. قال الملأ is a verb and agent; من قوم فرعون is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; إن and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; ساحر is the khabar; عليم is an adjective; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying. (يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ فَماذا تَأْمُرُونَ): the clause يريد is a second adjective of ساحر; أن and what is within its scope are, in interpretation, a maṣdar, the direct object of يريد; يخرجكم is an imperfect verb in the accusative by أن; من أرضكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يخرجكم; the فاء is a conjunction; ماذا is an interrogative noun, a fronted object of تأمرون, or "ما" is a mubtadaʾ and "ذا" a relative noun, its khabar, and the clause تأمرون has no grammatical position; and "ماذا" and its i'rab have already been discussed at length. (قالُوا أَرْجِهْ وَأَخاهُ): the speech is a new sentence, uttered to explain the reply of the chiefs of his people.
The clause أرجه is accusative as the content of the saying; أرجه is an imperative verb, i.e. "postpone him and defer him"; the hamza has been dropped for ease; the هاء is a direct object; وأخاه is conjoined to the هاء; and you may put it in the accusative as an object of accompaniment (mafʿūl maʿahu). (وَأَرْسِلْ فِي الْمَدائِنِ حاشِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; أرسل is an imperative verb; في المدائن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أرسل; and حاشرين is an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. "men who gather the magicians"; it is also said that it is accusative as a ḥāl, with the object of حاشرين omitted, i.e. "the magicians". المدائن is the plural of مدينة, whose mīm is radical and whose yāʾ is additional, derived from مدن يمدن مدونا, "he stayed"; and when the yāʾ is additional in the singular, it turns into a hamza in the plural. (يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ ساحِرٍ عَلِيمٍ): يأتوك is an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the answer to a request; the wāw is the agent; the kāf is a direct object; بكل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأتوك; ساحر is a muḍāf ilayhi; and عليم is an adjective.

* Benefits:
The discussion of the "sudden" إذا was given in full earlier; here we cite the Zunbūrī question (al-masʾala al-zunbūriyya), a debate that took place between Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī. Their story is that Sībawayh came to the Barmakids, and Yaḥyā ibn Khālid resolved to bring the two together, and set a day for it. When Sībawayh arrived, al-Farrāʾ and Khalaf came forward to him, and Sībawayh said: "I will not speak to you two until your companion is present." So al-Kisāʾī came, and said to him: "Will you ask me or shall I ask you?" Sībawayh said to him: "You ask." So he asked him about the Zunbūrī question, which is that the Arabs said: «قد كنت أظنّ أن العقرب أشد لسعا من الزنبور فإذا هو هي» ("I used to think that the scorpion stung harder than the hornet, and behold, it is it"). And they also said: «فإذا هو إياها» ("and behold, it is it", with the accusative pronoun).
Sībawayh said: "The accusative is not permissible." Yaḥyā said: "You two differ, and you are the leaders of your two cities, so who will judge between you?" Al-Kisāʾī said: "The Arabs are at your door; the people of both cities have heard from them, so let them be brought in and asked." Yaḥyā and Jaʿfar said: "You have been fair." So they were brought in and agreed with al-Kisāʾī, and Sībawayh was humbled. Yaḥyā ordered ten thousand dirhams for him, and he left for Fārs and stayed there until he died, and did not return to Basra. It is said that the Arabs had been bribed over this [Translator's note: the source text reads "ارشوا", apparently a corruption of "رُشوا", "were bribed"; and "ولم بعد" apparently stands for "ولم يعد"], and that they knew the standing of al-Kisāʾī with al-Rashīd.

dervis-irab:113-116.t:
* I'rab:
(وَجاءَ السَّحَرَةُ فِرْعَوْنَ): a verb, agent and direct object, and the clause is resumptive. (قالُوا: إِنَّ لَنا لَأَجْراً): قالوا is a verb and agent, and the clause is resumptive, uttered to present their answer, as if someone had asked: "What did they say?" The indefiniteness of أجر is meant to express exaggeration in abundance. إن is a particle resembling the verb; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar, fronted; the lām is the shifted lām; أجرا is its noun [Translator's note: the source says "its khabar" (خبرها), but أجرا is the noun of إنّ in the accusative]; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying. (إِنْ كُنَّا نَحْنُ الْغالِبِينَ): إن is conditional; كان and its noun; نحن is emphasis for "نا", and it may be a separation pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or ʿimād; الغالبين is the khabar; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted because something indicates it. (قالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ لَمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ): the speech is a new sentence, uttered to present Pharaoh's answer. نعم is a particle of answer that contains the confirmation of the abundant reward they demanded; وإنكم: the wāw is a conjunction on something omitted, for which the particle of answer stands, as if he had said: "Yes, you will have a reward, and you...". إنكم: إن and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; and من المقربين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of إنّ. (قالُوا: يا مُوسى إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ): a resumptive clause containing the magicians' address to Moses, and in it is much of the lofty courtesy exchanged between members of one profession, as craftsmen do when they meet. إما is a conditional particle containing the sense of giving a choice, and in it the fineness of their manners shines. أن is a maṣdar particle, interpreted with what is within its scope as a maṣdar in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied sense being: "either your casting is what is begun with"; or as a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied sense being: "and either your command is casting"; and it is permissible that the maṣdar be put in the accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "do either our casting or your casting". (وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ نَحْنُ الْمُلْقِينَ): conjoined to what precedes. (قالَ: أَلْقُوا فَلَمَّا أَلْقَوْا سَحَرُوا أَعْيُنَ النَّاسِ وَاسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ): the clause ألقوا is in the position of the accusative as the content of his saying [Translator's note: the source reads "مقول قوله"], and the clause قال is resumptive; the فاء is resumptive; لما is a linking particle or a temporal one; ألقوا is a verb and agent; the clause سحروا is the answer to لما; أعين الناس is a direct object; and استرهبوهم is conjoined to سحروا, as if they had sought to arouse fear in them. (وَجاؤُ بِسِحْرٍ عَظِيمٍ): likewise a conjunction; بسحر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاءوا; and عظيم is an adjective of سحر.

dervis-irab:117-122.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَلْقَفُ): the imperfect of لقف, like علم يعلم. One says لقفت الشيء ألقفه لقفا and تلقّفته أتلقّفه تلقّفا when you take it quickly and eat it or swallow it.
It is also said that لقف and لقم have one meaning.
(يَأْفِكُونَ): الإفك is originally the turning of a thing from its face; hence the liar is called أفّاك, because he turns speech from its correct face to falsehood.

* I'rab:
(وَأَوْحَيْنا إِلى مُوسى أَنْ أَلْقِ عَصاكَ): the wāw is resumptive; أوحينا is a verb and agent; إلى موسى is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوحينا; "أن" may be explicative (mufassira), because it occurs after something containing the meaning of saying without its letters, and it may be a maṣdar particle, in which case it and what follows are the object of أوحينا; ألق is an imperative verb; and عصاك is the direct object of ألق. (فَإِذا هِيَ تَلْقَفُ ما يَأْفِكُونَ): the فاء is a conjunction on something omitted which the context requires, the implied sense being: "so he cast it, and behold, it..."; إذا is the sudden إذا; هي is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause تلقف is the khabar; "ما" may be a relative noun meaning "that which", the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "that which they falsify"; it may be a maṣdar particle, interpreted with what follows as a maṣdar in the accusative as the object of تلقف; and the clause يأفكون has no grammatical position in either case. (فَوَقَعَ الْحَقُّ وَبَطَلَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): the فاء is a conjunction; وقع الحق is a verb and agent; بطل is a past verb; "ما" is a relative or a maṣdar particle, and it, or it with what is within its scope, is in the position of the nominative as an agent; كان and its noun; and the clause يعملون is its khabar. (فَغُلِبُوا هُنالِكَ وَانْقَلَبُوا صاغِرِينَ): the فاء is a conjunction; غلبوا is a passive past verb; the wāw is the deputy agent; هنالك is a demonstrative in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, i.e. "they were defeated in the place in which their magic occurred"; انقلبوا is conjoined to غلبوا; and صاغرين is a ḥāl. (وَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ ساجِدِينَ): conjoined to what precedes; السحرة is the deputy agent of ألقي; and ساجدين is a ḥāl from السحرة. (قالُوا: آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position, and it may be a ḥāl clause, i.e. "they were cast down while prostrating, saying"; the clause آمنا is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying; and برب العالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنا. (رَبِّ مُوسى وَهارُونَ): رب is a badal of رب العالمين or an adjective of it. They put Moses before Aaron, although Aaron was older than he, for two reasons: the first is his superiority over him in rank, and the second is that it came as a verse-ending (fāṣila), and observing the verse-endings is almost invariable in the Qur'an.

dervis-irab:189-192.t:
* I'rab:
(هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ): Resumptive speech, addressing the people of Mecca. «هو» is a subject (mubtadaʾ), «الذي» is its predicate (khabar), the clause «خلقكم» is the ṣila (relative clause); «من نفس» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «خلقكم»; «واحدة» is an adjective (naʿt). (وَجَعَلَ مِنْها زَوْجَها لِيَسْكُنَ إِلَيْها): «جعل» is in the sense of «خلق» (created), conjoined to «خلقكم», and its agent is a latent pronoun; «منها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «جعل»; «زوجها» is a direct object; the lām is for justification (taʿlīl); «يسكن» is an imperfect verb in the accusative, and its agent is "he"; «إليها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يسكن». What is meant by «النفس» is Adam, and the pronoun is feminine in accordance with the form of the word «النفس». (فَلَمَّا تَغَشَّاها حَمَلَتْ حَمْلًا خَفِيفاً فَمَرَّتْ بِهِ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; «لما» is a connective or a temporal particle; the clause «حملت» has no grammatical position; «حملا», if it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and if it is in the sense of the foetus, it is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi); «خفيفا» is an adjective brought to signal the absence of the harm that pregnant women ordinarily suffer from the pains of pregnancy, or as an allusion to its beginning and its being a drop (nuṭfa) that does not weigh down the belly. The fāʾ is a conjunction, «مرت» is conjoined to «حملت»; «به» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «مرت», that is: she went back and forth in carrying out her tasks and doing them without hardship or distress. (فَلَمَّا أَثْقَلَتْ دَعَوَا اللَّهَ رَبَّهُما): The fāʾ is a conjunction; «لما» is a connective or temporal; «دعوا الله» is a past verb, agent and direct object; «ربهما» is a substitute (badal). (لَئِنْ آتَيْتَنا صالِحاً لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ): The lām is the one that prepares for an oath; the oath clause is resumptive, to indicate the clause of the oath; «إن» is conditional; «آتيتنا» is a verb and agent, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); «نا» is a direct object; «صالحا» is an adjective of an omitted direct object that it replaces, that is: "a righteous child"; the lām occurs in the answer to the oath because the oath precedes; «لنكونن» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we"; «من الشاكرين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted predicate of it. The clause «لئن آتيتنا» is explicative of the clause «دعوا الله», as if it were said: "And what was their supplication?" It was what they said. You may also make it the matter said of an omitted saying, its implied form being: "so they said: if You give us...". The clause «لنكونن» is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, as established. (فَلَمَّا آتاهُما صالِحاً جَعَلا لَهُ شُرَكاءَ فِيما آتاهُما): «شركاء» is the direct object of «جعلا»; «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of «شركاء» and was fronted; «فيما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of «شركاء»; the clause «آتاهما» is a ṣila. The meaning is: He gave their children; and this is indicated by His saying: (فَتَعالَى اللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ), where the pronoun is made plural, and Adam and Eve are free of associating partners with Allah. The fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause «تعالى الله» is conjoined to «خلقكم», with what is between them a parenthetical clause (iʿtirāḍ). It is also permissible that the fāʾ be resumptive and the clause resumptive; the secret of this address and what the scholars said about it will come in the section on Benefits. «الله» is its agent, «عما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تعالى», and the clause «يشركون» has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila of the relative noun. (أَيُشْرِكُونَ ما لا يَخْلُقُ شَيْئاً وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ): The hamza is for rebuking interrogation; «يشركون» is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent; «ما» is a direct object; the clause «لا يخلق» is the ṣila of the relative noun; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «هم» is a subject; the passive clause «يخلقون» is the predicate of «هم», and the wāw is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); the clause is resumptive, put forward to reproach them for what they committed. This pronoun refers back to the idols, which are expressed by «ما»; they are expressed by «ما» because the unbelievers held about them what they hold about rational beings. It is also permissible that it refer back to the unbelievers, that is: they are created by Allah, so if they reflected on that they would believe. (وَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ لَهُمْ نَصْراً وَلا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَنْصُرُونَ): The clause is conjoined to the one before it; «أنفسهم» is a fronted direct object of «ينصرون».

* Benefits:
The meaning intended in the address occurring in these verses has occupied the scholars and the commentators, and they have plunged deeply into it, and there is no room here to relate what they said on this matter.
The safest of what we see, and the closest to what is right and reasonable, is that what is meant is the two kinds, male and female, with no particular individual intended. The meaning then is: He created you as one kind, and made your spouses from yourselves also, that you might find rest in them; then when the kind that is the male covered the kind that is the female, such and such happened between the two kinds. It was also said: The address is to Quraysh who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — that is, the family of Quṣayy. Do you not see his saying in the story of Umm Maʿbad:
فيا لقصيّ ما زوى الله عنكم ... به من فخار لا يبارى وسؤدد
(O Quṣayy's people, what Allah has withheld from you through him of unrivalled pride and nobility!)
And before this verse:
جزى الله ربّ الناس خير جزائه ... رفيقين حلّا خيمتي أم معبد
(May Allah, Lord of mankind, give His best reward to two companions who alighted at the two tents of Umm Maʿbad.)
هما نزلا بالبرّ ثمّ ترحّلا ... فيا فوز من أمسى رفيق محمد
(The two alighted in goodness, then departed; what a triumph for him who became Muḥammad's companion!)
And after it:
ليهن بني سعد مقام فتاتهم ... ومقعدها للمؤمنين بمرصد
(Let Banū Saʿd be glad of the standing of their young woman, and her seat for the believers is in an observation place.)
The speaker is unknown.
History relates that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out of Mecca as an emigrant, accompanied by Abū Bakr, and their people did not know their news after they left the cave, the callers cried out with these words. Umm Maʿbad was a woman of Banū Saʿd, with whom they alighted. «يا لقصيّ»: its origin is «يا آل قصي» ("O family of Quṣayy"), or the lām is the lām of appeal for help (istighātha), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verbal meaning contained in «يا».

dervis-irab:193-195.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى الْهُدى لا يَتَّبِعُوكُمْ): The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, put forward to address the worshippers of idols, that is: if you call your gods to seek guidance and right direction as you seek it from Allah, they will not follow you in what you want. «إن» is conditional; «تدعوهم» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the wāw is the agent, and the hāʾ is a direct object referring back to the idols; «إلى الهدى» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تدعوهم»; «لا» is negative; «يتبعوكم» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive. (سَواءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ أَمْ أَنْتُمْ صامِتُونَ): «سواء» is a fronted predicate; «عليكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «سواء»; the hamza is for interrogation, and it is the hamza of equalization (hamzat al-taswiya), after which what follows is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), as was mentioned in al-Baqara; it and what falls within its scope are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, in the position of a nominative as a postponed subject. You may also parse «سواء» as the predicate of an omitted subject, with the interpreted maṣdar the agent of «سواء», which is treated like the verbal nouns. «أم» is a conjunction, called the connected («متصلة»), and it has already been mentioned; «أنتم» is a subject, «صامتون» is a predicate, and the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ عِبادٌ أَمْثالُكُمْ): The clause is resumptive, put forward to confirm what precedes it. «إن» and its noun; the clause «تدعون» is a ṣila; «من دون الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). «عباد» is the predicate of «إنّ»; «أمثالكم» is an adjective of «عباد». The idols are described as servants like them although they are inanimate things, whereas the word «العباد» is applied only to living, rational beings, and they are referred to [as rational] out of necessity in His saying «فادعوهم» and His saying «فليستجيبوا لكم». All this is permissible because, since they believed in their divinity, it necessarily followed for them that they are living and rational, even if in reality they are otherwise; but the expressions came in accordance with what their belief demanded. More investigation of this will come in the section on Benefits. (فَادْعُوهُمْ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ), that is: if that is sound — and it is sound only in their belief and custom — then call them. «ادعوهم» is an imperative verb, agent and direct object; and His saying «فليستجيبوا»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, the lām is the lām of command, and «يستجيبوا» is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يستجيبوا»; «إن» is conditional; «كنتم صادقين» is the protasis, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, that is: "then call them"; «صادقين» is the predicate of «كنتم». (أَلَهُمْ أَرْجُلٌ يَمْشُونَ بِها): Resumptive speech in the manner of a reproach to them for their deficient minds. The hamza is for rebuking interrogation together with negation; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted predicate; «أرجل» is a postponed subject; the clause «يمشون بها» is an adjective. (أَمْ لَهُمْ أَيْدٍ يَبْطِشُونَ بِها): «أم» is a conjunction in the sense of «بل» (rather), and the clause is conjoined to the preceding one, and likewise His saying: (أَمْ لَهُمْ أَعْيُنٌ يُبْصِرُونَ بِها؟ أَمْ لَهُمْ آذانٌ يَسْمَعُونَ بِها) that is: they have none of that at all of what you have, so how do you worship them, when you are more complete than they and more perfect in state? (قُلِ: ادْعُوا شُرَكاءَكُمْ ثُمَّ كِيدُونِ فَلا تُنْظِرُونِ): The clause «ادعوا شركاءكم» is the matter said (maqūl al-qawl); «ثم» is a particle of conjunction and delay; «كيدون» is conjoined to «ادعوا»; the fāʾ is a conjunction and «لا» is prohibitive; «تنظرون» is an imperfect verb jussive by the prohibitive «لا», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the nūn is the protective nūn, and the yāʾ of the first person is omitted; the discussion of the permissibility of omitting it has preceded in al-Baqara.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ألهم أرجل يمشون بها» up to His saying «فلا تنظرون» there is a rhetorical device known as "negating a thing by affirming it". It is that the speaker affirms something in the apparent surface of his speech, on condition that what is affirmed is figurative (mustaʿār), and then negates, figuratively, what stems from it, while what is negated in reality, in the inner part of the speech, is what he affirmed, not what he negated. In the preceding verses it requires negating divinity altogether from any of the gods taken besides Allah the Exalted who sees and hears — so how much more from those of them that neither hear nor see. Examples of it have preceded, and more will come.

* Benefits:
The best-known commentators saw no difficulty in applying the word «عباد» (servants) to the idols. Ibn Jarīr — who was the most careful of them to settle everything that was counted a difficulty and its answer — did not raise it in the verse, and explained the servants as angels. As for those after him among the commentators, they raised it and answered it with two answers that al-Rāzī reported.

The words of al-Rāzī:
The first: that when the polytheists claimed that they harm and benefit, it became necessary that they believe them to be rational and understanding; so of necessity this verse came in accordance with their beliefs, and for that reason He said «فادعوهم فليستجيبوا لكم», and He said «إن الذين» and did not say «التي».
[Translator's note: «يعقتدوا» in the Arabic is a misspelling of «يعتقدوا»; «معفول» and «تعبونهم» in the preceding passages of the Arabic appear to be misprints of «مفعول» and «تعبدونهم»; I have translated the intended sense.]
The second answer is that this is idle talk that came by way of mockery of them, that is: the utmost of their case is that they be living and rational; and if that is established, they are servants like you and have no merit over you, so why did you make yourselves slaves and make them gods and lords?

dervis-irab:139-141.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُتَبَّرٌ): shattered. It is a passive participle of تبّر, that is, "destroyed and ruined"; the verbal noun is التتبير. From it comes التِّبر, which is gold dust, because people rush headlong after it.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ مُتَبَّرٌ ما هُمْ فِيهِ): Resumptive speech, brought to show the end to which they will come. إن is a particle resembling the verb; هؤلاء is a demonstrative, the noun of إن; متبر may be the khabar of إن; ما is a relative noun in the position of nominative as the deputy agent of متبر; هم فيه is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause has no position because it is a ṣila. It is also possible that the relative noun be a mubtadaʾ, with متبر its khabar fronted before it, and the clause the khabar of إن.
