(وَباطِلٌ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): The wāw is a conjunction; باطل is a fronted khabar; ما is a delayed mubtadaʾ; كانوا يعملون — كان with its noun and khabar — is the ṣila of «ما». You may also conjoin «باطل» to «متبر» and make «ما» the agent of باطل, since it is an active participle. (قالَ: أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِيكُمْ إِلهاً): Resumptive speech, brought to begin the exposition of the matters of Allah that require devotion to be reserved for Him alone. The hamza is for an interrogative of denial and rebuke; غير is a direct object of an omitted verb, i.e. "Shall I seek for you a god other than the one who deserves worship?"; the clause أبغيكم is the content of the saying; إلها is a specification (tamyīz) or a ḥāl. It is also possible that «غير» is a fronted direct object of أبغيكم, with the kāf accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "Shall I seek for you something other than Allah?" On this reading «غير» may be parsed as a ḥāl, and إلها is the direct object. (وَهُوَ فَضَّلَكُمْ عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ): The wāw is circumstantial; هو is a mubtadaʾ; the clause فضلكم is the khabar, and the whole clause is circumstantial; على العالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فضلكم. The wāw may also be resumptive, the clause being resumptive with no grammatical position. (وَإِذْ أَنْجَيْناكُمْ مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ): The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; إذ is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "Remember the time when We saved you"; the clause أنجيناكم is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; من آل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنجيناكم; فرعون is muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of genitive being fatḥa because it is a diptote. (يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذابِ): The clause is accusative as a ḥāl from آل فرعون; يسومونكم is an imperfect verb, agent and first direct object; سوء العذاب is the second direct object. (يُقَتِّلُونَ أَبْناءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِساءَكُمْ): The clause «يقتلونكم» is a substitute (badal) for the clause يسومونكم, and the clause يستحيون نساءكم is conjoined to it. [Translator's note: the source writes «يقتلونكم» in the parsing where the verse has «يُقَتِّلُونَ أَبْناءَكُمْ»; the translation follows what is written.] (وَفِي ذلِكُمْ بَلاءٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ): The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; في ذلكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; بلاء is a delayed mubtadaʾ; من ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of بلاء; and عظيم is a second adjective.

dervis-irab:142-143.t:
* I'rab:
(وَواعَدْنا مُوسى ثَلاثِينَ لَيْلَةً وَأَتْمَمْناها بِعَشْرٍ): The wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, brought to give in detail what He stated summarily in Sūrat al-Baqara, namely His saying, Exalted is He: «وإذ واعدنا موسى أربعين ليلة». واعدنا موسى is a verb, agent and direct object; ثلاثين is a second direct object of واعدنا, and in it there is an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "the completion of thirty"; ليلة is a specification; and that was so that he might fast them until We spoke to him. أتممناها is conjoined to واعدنا; بعشر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أتممناها. (فَتَمَّ مِيقاتُ رَبِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً): The fāʾ is a conjunction; تم ميقات is a verb and agent; ربه is muḍāf ilayhi; أربعين is a ḥāl, i.e. "it was completed, reaching this number"; ليلة is a specification. The reason for its being accusative as a ḥāl will come in the Benefits section. It was also said that it is the object of «تم» because its meaning is «reached»; and it cannot be an adverb for the completion, because the completion occurs only with the last part of those periods of time. (وَقالَ مُوسى لِأَخِيهِ هارُونَ): The wāw is a conjunction; قال موسى is a verb and agent; لأخيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قال. هارون is a substitute (badal) for أخيه or an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān). (اخْلُفْنِي فِي قَوْمِي وَأَصْلِحْ وَلا تَتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ): The clause is the content of Moses' saying; اخلفني is an imperative and direct object; في قومي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اخلفني; أصلح is conjoined to اخلفني; in ولا تتبع the wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تتبع is an imperfect verb jussive by the prohibitive لا; سبيل المفسدين is the direct object. (وَلَمَّا جاءَ مُوسى لِمِيقاتِنا): The wāw is a conjunction; لما is a linking or temporal particle containing the sense of a condition; the clause جاء موسى has no position, or is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; لميقاتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاء, the lām being for specification, as when you say: "I came to him on the tenth that had passed of the month". (وَكَلَّمَهُ رَبُّهُ قالَ: رَبِّ أَرِنِي أَنْظُرْ إِلَيْكَ): وكلمه ربه is conjoined to جاء, and ربه is the agent of كلمه. The clause قال has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; رب is a vocative in a construct (muḍāf) from which the vocative particle is omitted; أرني is an imperative of supplication, its agent latent, the nūn being the protective nūn and the yāʾ the first direct object, while the second object of the seeing is omitted, its implied form being "Yourself"; أنظر is a jussive imperfect because it is the answer to a request, and the clause of the request and its answer is the content of the saying; إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنظر. (قالَ لَنْ تَرانِي): The clause is the content of the saying; لن is a particle of negation, accusative-causing and futurity; تراني is an imperfect verb put in the accusative by لن, and the yāʾ is the direct object. (وَلكِنِ انْظُرْ إِلَى الْجَبَلِ فَإِنِ اسْتَقَرَّ مَكانَهُ فَسَوْفَ تَرانِي): The wāw is a conjunction; لكن is a particle of rectification, lightened and inoperative; انظر is an imperative; إلى الجبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to انظر; فإن: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إن is conditional; استقر is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; مكانه is an adverb of place attached to استقر; فسوف: the fāʾ links to the apodosis, and سوف is a particle of futurity; تراني is an imperfect verb, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّى رَبُّهُ لِلْجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُ دَكًّا): The fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is a linking or temporal particle; تجلى ربه is a verb and agent; للجبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجلى; جعله is a verb and direct object, and the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; دكا is the second direct object of جعله, since it is a maṣdar with the meaning of a passive participle, i.e. "crushed" (madkūk); it may also be accusative as a maṣdar, the implied form being "He crushed it a crushing". (وَخَرَّ مُوسى صَعِقاً): صعقا is a ḥāl. (فَلَمَّا أَفاقَ قالَ: سُبْحانَكَ تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is a linking or temporal particle; the clause أفاق has no position, or is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause قال has no position; سبحانك is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of an omitted verb; تبت is a verb and agent; إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تبت; وأنا: the wāw is a conjunction, and أنا is a mubtadaʾ; أول المؤمنين is the khabar.

* Benefits:
The vision of Allah in the Hereafter:
Al-Zamakhsharī and others among the imams of the Muʿtazila argued from «لن» for the impossibility of seeing Allah, Exalted is He, in the Hereafter, saying that it is for emphasis and perpetuity. The scholars of the Sunna answered them, and a long dispute arose about this, which drew into mutual disparagement and the hurling at one another of harsh reckonings and accusations, matters for which our book has no room. So refer to the longer works for it.

dervis-irab:161-162.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قِيلَ لَهُمُ: اسْكُنُوا هذِهِ الْقَرْيَةَ): the واو is a conjunction; the adverb is attached to an omitted «اذكر» ("remember"); the clause قيل is in the position of genitive, the adverb being annexed to it; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قيل; the clause اسكنوا is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech; هذه is a demonstrative in the position of accusative as direct object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); and القرية is a badal (substitute). This verse occurred in al-Baqara with its wording, with a slight change. There is no harm in the difference between the two expressions when there is no contradiction, and there is no contradiction between His saying «اسكنوا هذه القرية وكلوا منها» and His saying «فكلوا», because if they dwelt in the town and their dwelling became the cause of eating from it, then they have combined in existence dwelling in it and eating from it. And whether they put forward the saying of ḥiṭṭa before entering the gate or put it later, they are combining the two in what they do. Omitting the mention of رغدا (abundantly) does not contradict its affirmation.
(وَكُلُوا مِنْها حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ وَقُولُوا حِطَّةٌ): its i'rab has preceded in al-Baqara, so renew your acquaintance with it there. As for حطّة, we said that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "our request is ḥiṭṭa", that is, that our sins be lowered (taḥuṭṭa) from us.
(وَادْخُلُوا الْبابَ سُجَّداً نَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطِيئاتِكُمْ): its i'rab has also preceded in Sūrat al-Baqara, so there is no need to repeat it.
(سَنَزِيدُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object.
(فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ قَوْلًا غَيْرَ الَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمْ): the فاء is a conjunction; بدّل الذين is a verb and agent; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila of the relative and has no position; منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. In the speech there is an omission, and the omitted item is the second direct object of بدّل, its implied form being "for that which was said to them". قولا is a direct object; غير is an adjective; and الذي is a relative noun in the position of genitive by annexation. The clause قيل لهم is a ṣila with no position. That is, they said "ḥabba" (a grain) instead of "ḥiṭṭa", and they had no reason for that except the intention of mocking Moses and angering him.
(فَأَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِجْزاً مِنَ السَّماءِ بِما كانُوا يَظْلِمُونَ): فأرسلنا is conjoined to فبدّل; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أرسلنا, the باء being causal; ما is a relative noun or a maṣdar particle; كانوا is كان and its noun; and the clause يظلمون is its khabar.

dervis-irab:163-166.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حاضِرَةَ الْبَحْرِ): adjoining it, near it, and lying on its shore.
There is disagreement about this town. It was said: it is Ayla; it was said: Madyan; and it was said: Tiberias.
The Arabs call a city a "town" (qarya). It is reported from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ: "I have not seen two townsmen (qarawiyyayn) more eloquent than al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥajjāj", meaning two men from the people of cities.
Within this question there is a weighty benefit, which is to let the Jews know that this is among the things the Messenger of Allah knows, and that his being informed of it can only be through a report from Allah, Glorified be He, so it is evidence of his truthfulness.
(يَعْدُونَ): they transgress, or they overstep.
(سَبْتِهِمْ): السبت is the verbal noun of سبتت اليهود, when the Jews venerate their Sabbath by abandoning hunting and busying themselves with worship. السبت in the language means "cutting off". It is as if, by choosing the Sabbath as a festival, they chose that in which their being cut off lay. It is said: سبتوا سبتا, of the pattern ضرب, and أسبتوا with an alif is a dialectal form of it.
(شُرَّعاً): plural of شارع, from شرع عليه, when he came near and looked over, that is: they come to them visibly on the surface of the water, floating on top of it, near the shore.
(بَئِيسٍ): severe, of the pattern فعيل, from بؤس يبؤس when it became intense.
(عَتَوْا): they were arrogant.
(خاسِئِينَ): abased.

* I'rab:
(وَسْئَلْهُمْ عَنِ الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كانَتْ حاضِرَةَ الْبَحْرِ): the واو is a conjunction; اسألهم is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object; عن القرية is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اسألهم; التي is a relative noun, an adjective of القرية; the clause كانت has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; the noun of كانت is latent, i.e. "it"; and حاضرة البحر is the khabar of كانت.
(إِذْ يَعْدُونَ فِي السَّبْتِ): إذ is an adverb attached to an omitted muḍāf, the implied form being "about the state of the town"; يعدون is an imperfect verb with its agent, and the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation.
(إِذْ تَأْتِيهِمْ حِيتانُهُمْ يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ شُرَّعاً وَيَوْمَ لا يَسْبِتُونَ لا تَأْتِيهِمْ): the adverb is a badal from the preceding adverb, or is attached to يعدون, i.e. "when they transgressed on the Sabbath, when their fish came to them"; the clause تأتيهم is in the position of genitive by annexation; حيتانهم is the agent of تأتيهم; شرعا is a ḥāl from حيتانهم; ويوم is conjoined to إذ; and the clause لا يسبتون is in the position of genitive by annexation.
(كَذلِكَ نَبْلُوهُمْ بِما كانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ): the كاف and its genitive noun are in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "We test them with a test like this severe one". It is also possible that it is a ḥāl, i.e. "such a coming as that does not come", but the first is preferable. The باء is causal, and ما is a maṣdar particle, i.e. "We test them because of their wickedness"; and the clause يفسقون is the khabar of كانوا.
(وَإِذْ قالَتْ أُمَّةٌ مِنْهُمْ): conjoined to «إذ يعدون», and its ruling in i'rab is the same: a badal from the omitted item, which is the state of the town and its predicate, or its people. The clause قالت is in the position of genitive by annexation; أمة is the agent; and منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of أمة.
(لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوْماً اللَّهُ مُهْلِكُهُمْ أَوْ مُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذاباً شَدِيداً): اللام is a preposition, and the interrogative ما has had its alif dropped because the preposition entered it - its discussion has already preceded - and the reason for this omission is to distinguish the interrogative from the declarative. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تعظون; قوما is the direct object of تعظون; الله is the mubtadaʾ and مهلكهم the khabar; the nominal clause is an adjective of «قوما»; أو is a conjunction; ومعذبهم is conjoined to مهلكهم; عذابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; and شديدا is an adjective.
(قالُوا: مَعْذِرَةً إِلى رَبِّكُمْ وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ): the clause of speech is resumptive, introduced to explain their answer. As for معذرة, Ḥafṣ alone read it in the accusative. There are three strong aspects to it. The first: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "we admonished them for the sake of excuse". The second: it is accusative in the manner of a maṣdar, by an implied verb from its own wording, i.e. "we make an excuse". The third: it is accusative in the manner of a direct object, because المعذرة contains speech within it, and a single word containing speech, when it occurs after the verb "to say", is put in the accusative as a direct object, as in قلت خطبة. The majority read معذرة in the nominative. Sībawayh said, in his preference for the nominative: "Because they did not intend to make a fresh excuse, but it was said to them: 'Why do you admonish?' and they said: 'Our admonition is an excuse.'" المعذرة has the meaning of الاعتذار, which is disclaiming blame for a sin. وإلى ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to معذرة; لعل and its noun; the clause يتقون is its khabar; and the clause of hope is a ḥāl.
(فَلَمَّا نَسُوا ما ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ): the فاء is resumptive, and لما is a connective or temporal; the clause نسوا has no position, or is in the position of genitive by annexation; نسوا is a verb and agent; ما is a direct object; the clause ذكروا, in the passive, has no position because it is a ṣila, and the واو is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ذكروا.
(أَنْجَيْنَا الَّذِينَ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ السُّوءِ): the clause أنجينا has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; الذين is the direct object; the clause ينهون is the ṣila of the relative; and عن السوء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينهون.
(وَأَخَذْنَا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا): conjoined to what preceded.
(بِعَذابٍ بَئِيسٍ بِما كانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ): بعذاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخذنا; بئيس is an adjective of عذاب; and in بما the باء is a preposition of cause, i.e. "because of their wickedness".
(فَلَمَّا عَتَوْا عَنْ ما نُهُوا عَنْهُ قُلْنا لَهُمْ: كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خاسِئِينَ): the فاء is a conjunction, and لما is a connective or temporal; عما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عتوا; the clause قلنا has no position; the clause كونوا is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech; قردة is the khabar of كونوا; and خاسئين is an adjective.

dervis-irab:123-126.t:
* Vocabulary:
(خِلافٍ): the exegetes almost unanimously agree that the meaning is that a limb be cut from each side, so that the right hand and the left foot are cut off.
They said: the first to cut off from opposite sides and to crucify was Pharaoh. In the language, خالفه خلافا (with a kasra on the خاء) and مخالفة mean the opposite of "he agreed with him", and خالف بين رجليه means he advanced one of them and set back the other; perhaps it is taken from this meaning. The view of those who explained it as "opposition", i.e. "I will cut off your hands and your feet because of your opposing me", with "من" causal, is remote, because that conflicts with the eloquent style of the Qur'an.
(تَنْقِمُ): in al-Miṣbāḥ: نقمت عليه أمره and نقمت منه نقما (of the pattern ضرب), and نقوما. And نقمته أنقمته (of the pattern تعب) is a dialectal form: when you blame him and detest him with the strongest detestation for his evil deed.

* I'rab:
(قالَ فِرْعَوْنُ: آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ لَكُمْ): the clause قال فرعون is resumptive, uttered in denunciation of the magicians, rebuking them for what they had done.
The clause آمنتم is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying; it is with a single hamza followed by the alif which is the fāʾ of the word, and this is one of the four readings of this word. It may be a pure statement containing rebuke, or it may be an interrogative whose particle is omitted because the meaning is understood. به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنتم; قبل is an adverb of time also attached to آمنتم; أن and what is within its scope are a maṣdar in a construct state; آذن originally was أأذن, an imperfect verb in the accusative by أن, the first hamza being the speaker's hamza that enters the imperfect, and the second turned into an alif because it occurs quiescent after another hamza; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آذن; and the clause آمنتم is in the position of the accusative as the content of his saying. (إِنَّ هذا لَمَكْرٌ مَكَرْتُمُوهُ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ): a new sentence which Pharaoh brought to affirm to them that their faith rested on collusion between them and Moses; then he followed the speech by saying that it was strong, and so he inclined to threatening. إن and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; مكر is its khabar; the clause مكرتموه is an adjective of مكر; and في المدينة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مكرتموه. (لِتُخْرِجُوا مِنْها أَهْلَها فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ): the lām is causal; تخرجوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to مكرتموه; منها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تخرجوا; أهلها is a direct object; the فاء is the eloquent فاء; سوف is a particle of futurity; تعلمون is an imperfect verb and agent, whose object is omitted as it is known, i.e. "you will know what of the blows of punishment will befall you". (لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلافٍ): the lām is the preparatory lām of the oath; أقطعن is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of an oath, explicative of the vagueness arising from the omission of the direct object; أيديكم is a direct object; أرجلكم is conjoined to أيديكم; and من خلاف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e.
"differing"; "من" may be causal, in which case the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb itself. (ثُمَّ لَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ): ثم is a particle of conjunction and delay; لأصلبنكم is conjoined to لأقطعن; and أجمعين is emphasis for the kāf. (قالُوا: إِنَّا إِلى رَبِّنا مُنْقَلِبُونَ): a new sentence, uttered to deliver their answer at his threatening them, (saying) that they do not care about death because of their return to their Lord and His mercy, and that they are dying and returning to their Lord, so what you do is only what is unavoidable [Translator's note: the source text of this last clause is somewhat garbled]; إن and what follows are the content of the saying; إنا: إن and its noun; إلى ربنا is attached to منقلبون; and منقلبون is the khabar of إن. (وَما تَنْقِمُ مِنَّا إِلَّا أَنْ آمَنَّا بِآياتِ رَبِّنا لَمَّا جاءَتْنا): the wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is strung on to their earlier answer; ما is negative; تنقم is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you"; منا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تنقم, i.e. "you find fault with us only for our faith"; إلا is a particle of restriction; أن is a maṣdar particle which with what it governs is a maṣdar, the object of تنقم, and the maṣdar may be an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), so it is in every case an emptied exception; بآيات ربنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنا; لما is a linking particle or a temporal one; and the clause جاءتنا has no grammatical position, or is in the position of the genitive by annexation. (رَبَّنا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنا صَبْراً وَتَوَفَّنا مُسْلِمِينَ): a new sentence in which they turned away from addressing him to taking refuge in Allah and committing affairs to Him. ربنا is a vocative in construct; أفرغ is a verb of supplication, out of courtesy; علينا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أفرغ; صبرا is a direct object; توفنا is conjoined to أفرغ; and مسلمين is a ḥāl. The meaning of الإفراغ here is pouring, i.e. "pour upon us a wide reward which flows over us and engulfs us as water is poured". The answer of "لما" is omitted, its implied form being: "when it came to us we believed in it without hesitation". The answer clause has no grammatical position in any case.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is a charming art, namely the strengthening of praise by what resembles blame, or praise in the guise of blame. It is of two kinds:
1- That an attribute of praise be excepted from a negated attribute of blame in regard to something, on the supposition that it falls within the attribute of blame. This kind is the well-known one, and from it is the saying of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم ... بهنّ فلول من قراع الكتائب
(There is no fault in them, save that their swords have notches from clashing with the battalions.)
And from it is the verse with which we are dealing; a similar verse in al-Māʾida has also passed.
2- That an attribute of praise be affirmed for something, and that this be followed by a particle of exception followed by another attribute of praise for it, as in: أنا أفصح العرب بيد أني من قريش ("I am the most eloquent of the Arabs, except that I am from Quraysh"). And from it is also the saying of al-Nābigha:
فتى كملت أوصافه غير أنه ... جواد فما يبقي على المال باقيا
(A young man whose qualities are complete, except that he is so generous that he leaves no wealth remaining.)

dervis-irab:127-129.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَسْتَحْيِي): i.e. "we will keep their women alive [Translator's note: the source prints نسبقي, apparently for نستبقي] for service."

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْ قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ): the wāw is resumptive or conjunctive, and the speech is a new sentence to explain what the chiefs of Pharaoh said and their incitement against Moses and his people, or it is conjoined to what precedes. قال الملأ is a verb and agent, and من قوم فرعون is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from الملأ. (أَتَذَرُ مُوسى وَقَوْمَهُ لِيُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَيَذَرَكَ وَآلِهَتَكَ): the interrogation is one of denial, to incite Pharaoh against Moses and his people; تذر is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, and the clause is the content of the saying; موسى is a direct object; قومه is conjoined to موسى; the lām is causal; يفسدوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the causal lām; the preposition, namely the causal lām, and the interpreted maṣdar after it are attached to تذر; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يفسدوا; and as for ويذرك, it may be conjoined to يفسدوا and so be put in the accusative like it, or the wāw may be the wāw of accompaniment and [Translator's note: the source prints "ويذكرك"] ويذرك be put in the accusative by an implied أن after the wāw in the answer to the interrogation; the kāf is a direct object; and آلهتك is conjoined to the pronoun or is an object of accompaniment. The meaning is: how can it be that you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption in the land, and (at the same time) that they leave you and the worship of your gods? (قالَ: سَنُقَتِّلُ أَبْناءَهُمْ وَنَسْتَحْيِي نِساءَهُمْ): the clause of saying is resumptive, uttered to relate Pharaoh's state after his fear [Translator's note: the source prints "فرقه", apparently "فرَقه", "his fear"] of inflicting any harm upon Moses, peace be upon him, and he turned to the repetition of killing and heavy slaughter among his people. It was read سنقتّل with a shadda and a ḍamma on the nūn; with the lightened reading the nūn has a fatḥa. The clause سنقتل is in the accusative as the content of his saying; أبناءهم is a direct object; and نستحيي نساءهم is conjoined. (وَإِنَّا فَوْقَهُمْ قاهِرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; إن and its noun; قاهرون is its khabar; and the adverb is attached to قاهرون or to an omitted ḥāl. (قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ: اسْتَعِينُوا بِاللَّهِ): a resumptive clause, uttered to relate Moses' saying to his people, asking them to seek help in Allah, and the clause استعينوا is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying. (وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ الْأَرْضَ لِلَّهِ يُورِثُها مَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ وَالْعاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ): conjoined to استعينوا; إن and its noun; لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of it, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is a causal clause; the clause يورثها is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the name of majesty, or a khabar after a khabar for إنّ; من is a relative noun, the second direct object of يورثها; والعاقبة: the wāw is resumptive, and العاقبة is a mubtadaʾ; and للمتقين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar. (قالُوا: أُوذِينا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَأْتِيَنا وَمِنْ بَعْدِ ما جِئْتَنا): a new sentence, uttered to explain what the people of Moses said, and complained of, because of the kinds of servile work in which they were demeaned and the sorts of torment they were made to suffer before Moses' birth, peace be upon him, and after his birth, for Pharaoh and his people used to employ them in hard labour. The clause أوذينا is in the accusative as the content of their saying; من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوذينا; أن and what is within its scope are, in interpretation, a maṣdar in the genitive by annexation; من بعد is conjoined to من قبل; and ما is a maṣdar particle, interpreted with what follows as a maṣdar in the genitive by annexation. (قالَ عَسى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يُهْلِكَ عَدُوَّكُمْ): a resumptive clause, uttered to explain Moses' answer, peace be upon him, to his people's complaint against him, in accordance with their nature; the clause of hope is in the position of the accusative as the content of his saying, and in it is an allusion to the good tidings of Pharaoh's destruction. عسى is a past verb, one of the verbs of hope; ربكم is its noun; أن يهلك is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative as its khabar; and عدوكم is a direct object. (وَيَسْتَخْلِفَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ): conjoined to what precedes. (فَيَنْظُرَ كَيْفَ تَعْمَلُونَ): the فاء is a conjunction of succession; ينظر is conjoined to يستخلفكم; and كيف is an interrogative in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl or as an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq).

dervis-irab:144-146.t:
* I'rab:
(قالَ: يا مُوسى إِنِّي اصْطَفَيْتُكَ عَلَى النَّاسِ بِرِسالاتِي وَبِكَلامِي): Resumptive speech, brought to console Moses, peace be upon him, for what he missed of the vision. The vocative clause is in the position of accusative as the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); إن and its noun; the clause اصطفيتك is the khabar; على الناس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اصطفيتك; برسالاتي is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to اصطفيتك. He made الرسالة plural because that with which he was sent consisted of various kinds and sorts. وبكلامي is conjoined to برسالاتي. He put the message first to signal the ascent to the nobler, for speaking with him was a special distinction for him, and he repeated the preposition to signal that the choosing is distinct from the speaking. (فَخُذْ ما آتَيْتُكَ وَكُنْ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ): The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), and the clause after it has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; the clause آتيتك is the ṣila of «ما»; وكن من الشاكرين is conjoined to خذ; and من الشاكرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of «كن». (وَكَتَبْنا لَهُ فِي الْأَلْواحِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ): The wāw is resumptive; كتبنا is a verb and agent; له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كتبنا; في الألواح is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and من كل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted direct object — what is meant is the tablets of the Torah. [Translator's note: the source reads «جاء ومجرور» here, evidently a slip for «جار ومجرور»; the translation follows the sense.] (مَوْعِظَةً وَتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ): موعظة is a substitute (badal) for the position of «من كل شيء», because it is a direct object, as preceded. It is also permissible to parse «موعظة» as an object of purpose, i.e. "We wrote for him those things for the sake of admonition and detailing"; ولكل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تفصيلا» or an adjective of it. (فَخُذْها بِقُوَّةٍ وَأْمُرْ قَوْمَكَ يَأْخُذُوا بِأَحْسَنِها سَأُرِيكُمْ دارَ الْفاسِقِينَ): The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, or a conjunction of an omitted clause to كتبنا, the implied form being "and We said: Take it"; خذ is an imperative and the hāʾ is the direct object. وبقوة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of خذها; the clause مر is conjoined to خذها; قومك is the direct object; and يأخذوا is a jussive imperfect because it is the answer to a request. He singled out "the best" for taking, though all that is in it is required, as an exaggeration in seeking out and taking well, and choosing the firmest and most precise; or else the comparative sense is not intended, as in their saying "Summer is hotter than winter", i.e. summer is more extreme in its heat than winter in its cold, so that preferring the heat of summer over the cold of winter is not intended. Since by «الأحسن» what is commanded was intended — being more extreme in goodness than what is forbidden is in ugliness — it followed that taking what is forbidden is not permitted. The clause سأريكم دار الفاسقين is resumptive, brought to emphasise the command to take the best and to urge it, and so it stands in the place of a reason; and what the shift of person (iltifāt) adds of emphasis and exaggeration to taking the best is not hidden. As for دار الفاسقين, it was said that it is the abode of Pharaoh and his followers, as something to take a lesson from, and it was said that it is something else, and there is no room for independent judgement here. (سَأَصْرِفُ عَنْ آياتِيَ الَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ): Resumptive speech, brought to warn against arrogance, which turns minds away from true thinking. وعن آياتي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أصرف; الذين is a relative noun in the position of accusative as direct object; the clause يتكبرون is the ṣila; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتكبرون; بغير الحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from «الذين يتكبرون», i.e. "while they are bound up with a religion that is not the truth". (وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كُلَّ آيَةٍ لا يُؤْمِنُوا بِها): The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; يروا is the protasis and the wāw is the agent; كل آية is the direct object; the clause لا يؤمنوا is the apodosis; بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤمنوا. (وَإِنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الرُّشْدِ لا يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلًا): conjoined to what preceded; سبيلا is the second direct object. (وَإِنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الغَيِّ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلًا): also conjoined to what preceded. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَكانُوا عَنْها غافِلِينَ): The demonstrative is in the position of nominative or accusative. Nominative, on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the preposition and its genitive noun after it, i.e. "that turning away is because of their denial"; accusative, on the basis that it means "He turned them away with that very turning away", making it a maṣdar used as a direct object. In any case the clause is an initial one with no grammatical position; the clause كذبوا is the khabar of أن; بآياتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كذبوا; كانوا is conjoined to كذبوا, and the wāw is the noun of كان; عنها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to غافلين; and غافلين is the khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
1- The shift of person (iltifāt) in His saying «سأريكم دار الفاسقين», to draw attention, as we mentioned earlier.
2- The antithesis (ṭibāq) between سبيل الرشد and سبيل الغيّ. And since the contrast between them is by negation, its beauty appears plainly.

dervis-irab:147-148.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حُلِيِّهِمْ): the plural of حلي, like ثدي and ثديّ. Its original form is حلويّ: the wāw and yāʾ came together with the first of them having a sukūn, so the wāw was changed into yāʾ and assimilated into the yāʾ, and the lām was given kasra because of the yāʾ. الحلي is a noun for what one adorns oneself with of gold and silver.
(خُوارٌ): with ḍamma on the khāʾ, as is the rule for the most part in names of sounds, either on the pattern فعال or فعيل, like زئير.

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَلِقاءِ الْآخِرَةِ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ): The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, to show another kind of their disobedience and their presumption against Allah. The relative noun is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause كذبوا بآياتنا is the ṣila; ولقاء الآخرة is conjoined to بآياتنا; and the clause حبطت أعمالهم is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. (هَلْ يُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): The hamza (in هل) is interrogative, what is meant by it being negation, and for that reason «إلا» entered after it; يجزون is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the deputy agent; إلا is a particle of restriction; ما is a relative noun in the position of accusative as the second direct object; the clause كانوا is the ṣila of the relative noun, and the clause يعملون is the khabar. I see no need to suppose an omitted element, as al-Wāḥidī said, whose text is: "Here an omitted element must be supposed, i.e. «إلا بما كانوا», or «على ما كانوا», or «جزاء ما كانوا»." I say: the corresponding recompense is clearer, so there is no need for this strained effort. (وَاتَّخَذَ قَوْمُ مُوسى مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ عِجْلًا جَسَداً لَهُ خُوارٌ): The wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, brought to recount another kind of their wrongdoing; it is also possible that the wāw be a conjunction, from the conjoining of one story to another. قوم موسى is the agent; من بعده is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اتخذ; من حليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اتخذ, or to an omitted element in the position of ḥāl, because had it been delayed it would have been an adjective, as is the rule. عجلا is the direct object; جسدا is a substitute (badal), and he brought this substitute to ward off the supposition that it was a carved image of a calf; له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; خوار is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is in the position of accusative as an adjective of His saying «عجلا». (أَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّهُ لا يُكَلِّمُهُمْ وَلا يَهْدِيهِمْ سَبِيلًا): Resumptive speech, brought to rebuke them for their bad choice and for their persistence in riding the back of excess. The hamza is for an interrogative of denial; لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; the wāw is the agent of يروا; أن and what is within its scope take the place of the two objects of يروا; the clause لا يكلمهم is the khabar; ولا يهديهم سبيلا is conjoined to لا يكلمهم; and سبيلا is the second direct object, or is accusative by removal of the preposition. (اتَّخَذُوهُ وَكانُوا ظالِمِينَ): A resumptive clause, brought to be an answer to a question arising from the flow of the speech, i.e. "How, then, did they take it?" The wāw is a conjunction; كان and its noun; and ظالمين is its khabar.

dervis-irab:167-170.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَأَذَّنَ): he resolved. It is of the pattern تفعّل from الإيذان, that is, informing, because one who resolves on a matter speaks to himself of it and informs himself of it. They said: it was made to run in the course of an oath, like علم الله and شهد الله, and for that reason it is answered with what an oath is answered with. Al-Wāḥidī said: "Most of the people of the language hold that التأذّن has the meaning of الإيذان, which is informing." It was also said that its meaning is "decreed and obligatory". In al-Qāmūs: تأذن means "he swore".
(عَرَضَ): with two fatḥas, it is that which has no permanence, and from it the theologians borrowed "accident" (ʿaraḍ) as opposed to substance. Abū ʿUbayda said: العرض with fatḥa is all the goods of this world other than the two currencies (gold and silver), and with sukūn it is money and values; from it: «الدنيا عرض حاضر، وظلّ زائل» ("This world is a present commodity and a passing shade"). Al-Zamakhsharī explained it as "refuse" (ḥuṭām) and said: "That is, the refuse of this lowly thing, meaning this world and what is enjoyed of it. In His saying 'this lowly thing' there is disparagement and contempt. الأدنى is either from دنو in the sense of nearness, because it is immediate and near, or from the lowliness of the state, its fall and paltriness. What is meant is what they used to take as bribes in judgments in return for distorting the words, to make it easy for the common people." Both meanings were combined in a verse of Abū al-Ṭayyib:
لولا العقول لكان أدنى ضيغم ... أدنى إلى شرف من الإنسان
(Were it not for minds, the lowest lion would be closer to honour than man.)
The first «أدنى» is in the sense of "lesser and baser", and the second «أدنى» is in the sense of "nearer".

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكَ): the adverb is accusative as an object, by an implied verb conjoined to واسألهم, the implied form being "and remember the time when your Lord proclaimed"; the clause تأذّن is in the position of genitive, the adverb being annexed to it; and ربك is the agent.
(لَيَبْعَثَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ مَنْ يَسُومُهُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذابِ): the lām is the answer to the oath understood from the verb تأذن; يبعثن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يبعثنّ or to تأذّن; من is a relative noun, the object of يبعثن; the clause يسومهم has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; and سوء العذاب is the second direct object of يسومهم.
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَسَرِيعُ الْعِقابِ وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the clause of إن with its noun and khabar is explanatory of cause and has no position; and the clause وإنه لغفور رحيم is conjoined to it; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).
(وَقَطَّعْناهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أُمَماً): the واو is a conjunction; قطّعناهم is a verb, agent and direct object; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قطعناهم; and أمما is a ḥāl, or a second direct object, and في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(مِنْهُمُ الصَّالِحُونَ وَمِنْهُمْ دُونَ ذلِكَ): the clause is an adjective of «أمما»; منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and الصالحون is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ومنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar as well; and دون is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted described noun, which is the postponed mubtadaʾ. The meaning: "and among them are people who fall short of righteousness". Like it is His saying, the Exalted: «وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم», i.e. "and there is none of us but has a known station", so the described noun was omitted and its adjective put in its place, as in their saying: منّا ظعن ومنا أقام ("among us are those who departed and among us are those who stayed").
(وَبَلَوْناهُمْ بِالْحَسَناتِ وَالسَّيِّئاتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ): وبلوناهم is conjoined to قطعناهم; بالحسنات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بلوناهم; السيئات is conjoined to الحسنات; لعل and its noun; and the clause يرجعون is its khabar.
(فَخَلَفَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ وَرِثُوا الْكِتابَ): the فاء is a conjunction; خلف is a past verb; من بعدهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and خلف is the agent. الخلف - with sukūn on the lām and with fatḥa - is the one who succeeds another; and the clause ورثوا الكتاب is an adjective of خلف.
(يَأْخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هذَا الْأَدْنى): the clause is a second adjective; عرض is the object of يأخذون; هذا is a muḍāf ilayhi; and الأدنى is a badal from the demonstrative.
(وَيَقُولُونَ: سَيُغْفَرُ لَنا): the واو may be a conjunction to what precedes it or circumstantial; and the clause سيغفر لنا is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech.
(وَإِنْ يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ مِثْلُهُ يَأْخُذُوهُ): the واو is circumstantial, i.e. "while they, if there comes to them..."; it may also be for resumption; إن is conditional; يأتهم is the protasis, and the هاء is a direct object; عرض is the agent; مثله is an adjective; and يأخذوه is the apodosis, its jussive marker being the omission of the nūn.
(أَلَمْ يُؤْخَذْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِيثاقُ الْكِتابِ): the hamza is for an affirmative interrogative (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; يؤخذ is an imperfect verb jussive by لم; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤخذ; and ميثاق الكتاب is the nāʾib fāʿil.
(أَنْ لا يَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْحَقَّ): أن is a maṣdar particle, and it with what is within its scope is a maṣdar whose position is nominative as a badal from ميثاق, because the saying of the truth is the covenant of the Book; or accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, its meaning being "lest they say". It is also possible that «أن» is explicative of ميثاق الكتاب, because it has the meaning of saying without its letters, and «لا» then is prohibitive, and يقولوا is an imperfect verb jussive by it. But on the view that it is a maṣdar particle, «لا» is negative and the verb is accusative by the maṣdar أن. على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقولوا; إلا is a particle of restriction; and الحق may be a direct object or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "the saying of the truth".
(وَدَرَسُوا ما فِيهِ): the واو is a conjunction; درسوا is a past verb conjoined to «ألم يؤخذ عليهم», as if it had been said: "the covenant of the Book was taken from them, and they studied what is in it". ما is the object of درسوا; and فيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted item that has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative.
(وَالدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ): the واو is resumptive or circumstantial; الدار is the mubtadaʾ; الآخرة is an adjective; خير is the khabar of الدار; للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خير; the clause يتقون has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; the hamza is for an interrogative of denial (istifhām inkārī); the فاء is conjoined to an omitted item - and parallels of this have preceded; لا is negative; and تعقلون is conjoined to this omitted item.
(وَالَّذِينَ يُمَسِّكُونَ بِالْكِتابِ وَأَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ): the واو is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, introduced to show the distinction of prayer and its exalted merit.
(إِنَّا لا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُصْلِحِينَ): the clause is the khabar of الذين, or you may make it parenthetical, in which case the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "rewarded". إن and its noun; لا is negative; and the clause لا نضيع أجر المصلحين is the khabar of إن. We repeat its i'rab for its fixing in the mind: الذين is the mubtadaʾ; the clause يمسكون بالكتاب is the ṣila of الذين and has no position; the clause وأقاموا الصلاة is conjoined to the ṣila; the clause إنا لا نضيع أجر المصلحين is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; and the link between them is the repetition of the mubtadaʾ in its meaning, since «المصلحين» are those who hold fast to the Book, by conjunction to «الذين يتقون». And if that is not conceded, then the link is generality, because «المصلحين» is more general than those mentioned; or an omitted pronoun, i.e. "among them".

dervis-irab:196-200.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَلِيِّيَ): my helper and the one who takes charge of my affairs.
(الْعَفْوَ): ease, the opposite of strain. That is: take what comes easily to you of people's character and deeds, and what comes from them, and be easy-going without affectation or hardship, and do not put them in difficulty and burden them. The Prophet ﷺ said in this sense: «يسّروا ولا تعسّروا» ("Make things easy and do not make them hard"). And [the poet] said:
خذي العفو مني تستديمي مودّتي ... ولا تنطقي في سورتي حين أغضب
(Take the easy side from me and you will keep my affection, and do not speak in my fit of anger when I am angry.)
(العرف): with ḍamma on the ʿayn: the good (al-maʿrūf), and every fine deed. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
من يفعل الخير لا يعدم جوازيه ... لا يذهب العرف بين الله والناس
(Whoever does good will not lack its recompense; goodness is not lost between Allah and the people.)
(النزغ): goading and pricking. The whispering of Satan is likened to the prick of a driver on what he drives.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ وَلِيِّيَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْكِتابَ): «إن» with its noun and its predicate; «الذي» is an adjective of «الله», and the clause «نزل الكتاب» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (وَهُوَ يَتَوَلَّى الصَّالِحِينَ): The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction; «هو» is a subject (mubtadaʾ); the clause «يتولى الصالحين» is the predicate (khabar). (وَالَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَكُمْ وَلا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَنْصُرُونَ): Conjoined to what precedes; its parsing has just been given; «أنفسهم» is a fronted direct object of «ينصرون». (وَإِنْ تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى الْهُدى لا يَسْمَعُوا): Likewise a conjunction; «إن» is conditional, with its protasis and apodosis. (وَتَراهُمْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ وَهُمْ لا يُبْصِرُونَ): The wāw is resumptive; «تراهم» is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you", and the hāʾ is a direct object; the clause «ينظرون إليك» is circumstantial; the wāw is circumstantial; «هم» is a subject, the clause «لا يبصرون» is the predicate, and the clause «وهم لا يبصرون» is also a ḥāl (circumstantial). (خُذِ الْعَفْوَ وَأْمُرْ بِالْعُرْفِ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْجاهِلِينَ): «خذ» is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; «العفو» is a direct object; the other two imperative verbs are conjoined to it. (وَإِمَّا يَنْزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ نَزْغٌ فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): The wāw is a conjunction and «إن» is conditional, its nūn assimilated into the redundant (zāʾida) «ما»; «ينزغنك» is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). «من الشيطان» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «نزغ»; «نزغ» is the agent. «فاستعذ»: the fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis, because the apodosis after it is a request (ṭalabī); «استعذ» is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; «بالله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «استعذ»; «إن» with its noun and predicate; the clause «إن» and what falls within its scope is for justification and is resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
The Arabs greatly admired His saying, Exalted is He, «خذ العفو» to the end of the verse, because of its ease of composition, sweetness of wording, and soundness of structure, together with the distant allusions and unending hints it contains. They gave this kind of style the name of a figure called «الانسجام» (flowing harmony), which is that the speech descends like flowing water, so that the sentence in prose, or the verse in poetry, has an impact on souls and an effect on hearts that nothing else has.

Poetic examples of flowing harmony:
Among the poetic examples of this figure, which are free of ornament except where it comes within the ease, without intent, is the saying of one of them, attributed to Dīk al-Jinn, the poet of Ḥimṣ:
يا بديع الدّلّ والغنج ... لك سلطان على المهج
إنّ بيتا أنت ساكنه ... غير محتاج إلى السّرج
وجهك المأمول حجّتنا ... يوم تأتي الناس بالحجج
(O you of wondrous coquetry and allure, you hold sway over hearts. A house in which you dwell needs no lamps. Your hoped-for face is our proof on the day when people come with their proofs.)
And by Bahāʾ al-Dīn Zuhayr:
لحاظك أمضى من المرهف ... وريقك أشهى من القرقف
ومن سيف لحظك لا أتّقي ... ومن خمر ريقك لا أكتفي
أقاسي المنون لنيل المنى ... ويا ليت هذا بهذا يفي
زها ورد خدّيك لكنه ... بغير النواظر لم يقطف
وقد زعموا أنه مضعف ... وما علموا أنه مضعفي
(Your glances are sharper than the thin blade, and your saliva is sweeter than wine. From the sword of your glance I do not guard myself, and of the wine of your saliva I am never satisfied. I endure death to attain my desire, and would that this repaid that. The rose of your cheeks has bloomed, but it is not plucked except by eyes. They claimed that it weakens, and did not know that it is what weakens me.)
And of what deserves to be sung is the saying of Ṣafī al-Dīn, which reached the utmost of flowing harmony:
قالت: كحلت الجفون بالوسن ... قلت: ارتقابا لطيفك الحسن
قالت: تسلّيت بعد فرقتنا ... قلت: عن مسكني وعن سكني
قالت: تشاغلت عن محبتنا ... قلت: بفرط البكاء والحزن
قالت: تخلّيت، قلت عن جلدي ... قالت: تغيّرت، قلت: في بدني
قالت: أذعت الأسرار، قلت لها: ... صيّر سري هواك كالعلن
قالت: فماذا تروم؟ قلت لها: ... ساعة سعد بالوصال تسعفني
قالت: وعين الرقيب ترقبنا ... قلت: فإنّي للعين لم أبن
أنحلتني بالبعاد عنك فلو ... ترصّدتني العيون لم ترني
(She said: "You have lined your eyelids with sleeplessness." I said: "In expectation of your lovely phantom." She said: "You have consoled yourself after our parting." I said: "Away from my dwelling and my peace." She said: "You have been occupied away from loving us." I said: "With excess of weeping and grief." She said: "You have given up." I said: "My endurance." She said: "You have changed." I said: "In my body." She said: "You have spread the secrets." I said to her: "Your love has made my secret like the open." She said: "What then do you seek?" I said to her: "An hour of happiness with union, to help me." She said: "The eye of the watcher watches us." I said: "I have not appeared to the eye. You have wasted me by distance from you, so that were the eyes to watch for me they would not see me.")
We close this selection with the following story. It is said that one of the men of letters passed by the house of al-Sharīf al-Raḍī, which time had ravaged, taking away its splendour and wearing out its brocade, while the remains of its traces bore witness to its former freshness. He stopped before it, wondering at the turns of time, and recited these verses:
ولقد وقفت على ربوعهم ... وطلولها بيد البلى نهب
فبكيت حتى ضجّ من لغب ... نضوي وعجّ بعذلي الرّكب
وتلفتت عيني فمذ خفيت ... عني الطّلول تلفّت القلب
(I stood by their abodes, whose ruins were plunder to the hand of decay. I wept until my worn-out mount groaned from weariness and the riders cried out in blame of me. My eye turned about, and when the ruins vanished from me, my heart turned about.)
A man passed and said to him: "Do you know these verses?" He said: "No." He said: "By Allah, they are by the owner of this house." They marvelled at this strange coincidence; and a thing recalls a thing.

dervis-irab:201-206.t:
* Vocabulary:
(طائِفٌ): it may be an active participle from ṭāfa bihi al-khayāl yaṭīfu ṭayfan (the phantom visited him), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) of it. The people of Basra read «طيف» (ṭayf), and likewise the people of Mecca; the people of Medina and Kufa read «طائف» (ṭāʾif).
(اجْتَبَيْتَها): ijtabā al-shayʾ means jabāhu li-nafsihi, that is, he gathered it.
(الغدو): with two ḍammas, plural of ghudwa, with ḍamma on the ghayn and sukūn on the dāl; it is from the rising of dawn to the rising of the sun.
(الْآصالِ): plural of aṣīl, which is from the afternoon (ʿaṣr) to sunset.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذا مَسَّهُمْ طائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ): «إن» and its noun; the clause «اتقوا» is a ṣila; «إذا» is an adverbial (ẓarf) for what is future in time, containing the meaning of condition; the clause «مسهم» is in the position of a genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), because it occurs after the adverbial; the hāʾ is a direct object of «مس», and «طائف» is its agent; «من الشيطان» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of «طائف». «إذا», its condition and its following apodosis are the predicate of «إن». (تَذَكَّرُوا فَإِذا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ): The clause «تذكروا» has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the fāʾ is a conjunction; «إذا» is the «إذا» of suddenness (fujāʾiyya), which has been discussed before; «هم» is a subject and «مبصرون» a predicate. (وَإِخْوانُهُمْ يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِي الغَيِّ ثُمَّ لا يُقْصِرُونَ): The statements of the parsers and commentators on this verse are in disarray, and to avoid being lost in the mazes of the branching opinions we content ourselves with the best-known statements and those closest to reason and logic. So we say: «وإخوانهم»: the wāw is resumptive, «إخوانهم» is a subject, and the pronoun in it refers back to Satan, because what is meant by it is not the single one but the kind; the accusative pronoun in «يمدونهم» refers back to the unbelievers and the nominative one refers to Satan, the implied form being: "and the brothers of the devils, the devils extend them [in error]". On this basis the predicate is made to run on something other than the one it belongs to in meaning; do you not see that the extending is attributed to the devils, while in wording it is a predicate about «إخوانهم»? Al-Zamakhsharī said:
This is the most apt aspect, because «إخوانهم» stands in contrast to «الذين اتقوا». «في الغي» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يمدونهم»; «ثم» is a particle of conjunction and delay; «لا يقصرون» is conjoined to «يمدونهم», and «لا» is negative. There are other aspects that return to it in outcome, so we content ourselves with it. (وَإِذا لَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ بِآيَةٍ قالُوا: لَوْلا اجْتَبَيْتَها): The wāw is a conjunction, «إذا» is a future adverbial containing the meaning of condition; the clause «لم تأتهم» is in the position of a genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi; «بآية» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تأتهم»; the clause «قالوا» has no grammatical position; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), so the speech is a request, that is: choose it and invent it from yourself, as is your habit. (قُلْ إِنَّما أَتَّبِعُ ما يُوحى إِلَيَّ مِنْ رَبِّي): «إنما» consists of a restraining and a restrained element (kāffa and makfūfa) [Translator's note: the Arabic prints «مكفوقة»; the intended word is «مكفوفة»]; «أتبع» is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; «ما» is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as a direct object; the passive clause «يوحى» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; «إلي» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يوحى»; «من ربي» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (هذا بَصائِرُ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ): This clause is a completion of the saying, falling within its scope. «هذا» is a demonstrative in the position of a nominative as a subject; «بصائر» is its predicate; «من ربكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of «بصائر»; «هدى» is conjoined to «بصائر», and likewise «رحمة»; «لقوم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «رحمة», and the clause «يؤمنون» is an adjective of «قوم». (وَإِذا قُرِئَ، الْقُرْآنُ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنْصِتُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ): The wāw is resumptive and the clause resumptive; it is possible that it be a conjunction, with the speech part of the commanded matter said. «إذا» is a future condition; the clause «قرئ القرآن» is in the position of a genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi; «القرآن» is a deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); the fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ; the clause «استمعوا له» has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «استمعوا». There is disagreement about listening and what is meant by it, and the most apparent view is that it is listening and keeping silent at the time of reciting the Qur'an, in prayer or outside prayer. It was said that the meaning of «فاستمعوا» is: act upon what is in it and do not transgress it. «لعل» and its noun, the clause «ترحمون» is its predicate, and the clause of hope is circumstantial. (وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعاً وَخِيفَةً): The wāw is a conjunction; «اذكر» is an imperative verb; «ربك» is a direct object; «في نفسك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, and it is general for all kinds of remembrance; for the accusative of «تضرعا وخيفة» there are two aspects: one, that they are two objects of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi); the second, that they are two maṣdars standing in the place of a ḥāl, that is: humbly and fearfully. (وَدُونَ الْجَهْرِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصالِ وَلا تَكُنْ مِنَ الْغافِلِينَ): The wāw is a conjunction; «دون» is an adverbial attached to an omitted [word] conjoined to «في نفسك», that is: in secret and in the open; «من القول» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; «بالغدو والآصال» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «اذكر»; the wāw is a conjunction, «لا» is prohibitive, «تكن» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb jussive by the prohibitive «لا», and «من الغافلين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted predicate. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبادَتِهِ وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُ وَلَهُ يَسْجُدُونَ): Resumptive speech, put forward to mention the believers who deserve nearness to Allah. «إن» and its noun; «عند ربك» is an adverbial attached to an omitted [word] with no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; the clause «لا يستكبرون» is the predicate of «إن»; what is meant by "with" (ʿindiyya) is nearness to Allah and closeness to Him; «عن عبادته» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يستكبرون»; «يسبحونه» is conjoined to what precedes; in «وله» the wāw is a conjunction and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يسجدون»; «يسجدون» is conjoined to «يسبحونه». It is also permissible that the wāw be circumstantial or resumptive, and the clause «يسبحونه» be the predicate of an omitted subject, that is: "and they glorify Him".

* Benefits:
This is an enjoyable passage by Imam al-Ghazālī, some of which we relate because of its relevance and its preciousness.
He said: "Because of the nobility of the remembrance of Allah, the rank of martyrdom is great, for what is sought is the ending (khātima); and by the ending we mean taking leave of this world and coming before Allah the Exalted while the heart is absorbed in Allah, Mighty and Majestic. One cannot die in that state except in the battle line, for he has cut off hope from his life and his family, his wealth and his child, indeed from the whole world, for he wants it for his life. He has made his life light on his heart in love of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and in seeking His pleasure, and there is no greater detachment than that; therefore the matter of martyrdom is great.
When ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī was martyred on the day of Uḥud, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Jābir: 'Shall I not give you glad tidings, Jābir?' He said: 'Yes, may Allah give you glad tidings of good.' He said: 'Allah has brought your father to life and seated him before Him, and there is no veil between Him and him, nor a messenger. And the Exalted said: Ask of Me, My servant, whatever you wish, and I shall give it to you.' He said: 'My Lord! That You return me to the world until I am killed for You and for Your Prophet once again.' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The decree has gone forth from Me that they do not return to it.'
Then killing is the cause of the ending in such a state."
The testament of ʿUmar to one of his commanders:
I am pleased by the call of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to the remembrance of Allah and fear of Him, hoping for His help and mercy, in a testament to one of his commanders: "I counsel you and those of the soldiers with you to fear Allah in every state, for fear of Allah is the best equipment against the enemy and the strongest stratagem in war; and that you and those with you be more on guard against acts of disobedience among yourselves than against your enemy, for the sins of an army are more to be feared for them than their enemy; and were it not for that we would have no strength against them, because our numbers are not like their numbers, nor our equipment like their equipment. If we are equal in disobedience, they will have the advantage over us in strength; and if we are not given victory over them through our obedience, we will not overcome them by our strength. Know that you have guardians from Allah over you in your marches, who know what you do, so be ashamed before them, and ask Allah for help against your own selves as you ask Him for victory over your enemy."

dervis-irab:171-173.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَتَقْنَا): نتق means to uproot and raise; from it comes نتق السقاء when one shakes the skin so as to pull the butter out of it. The expressions of the people of the language differ about النتق. Abū ʿUbayda said: it is uprooting a thing from its place and throwing it; from it نتق ما في الجراب, when one shakes it and throws out what is in it; and a woman is called ناتق and منتاق when she bears many children. In the ḥadīth: «عليكم بزواج الأبكار، فإنهن أنتق أرحاما، وأطيب أفواها، وأرضى باليسير» ("Take virgins in marriage, for they are more fertile of wombs, sweeter of mouths, and more content with little"). It was also said: النتق is pulling with force; from it نتقت السقاء when you pull it hard to extract the butter from its mouth. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is raising. Ibn Qutayba said: it is shaking violently. Yet these differences go back to a single meaning. What draws attention is that whenever the nūn and the tāʾ are used as the fāʾ and ʿayn of a word, the meaning circles around pulling out, uprooting and bringing forth. As is our custom, we shall present the combination of these two letters. Among them: نتأ in the sense of "he threw"; نتأ the girl's breast in the sense that it protruded and rose; نتأ الشيء: it came out of its place without separating; نتجت الناقة: she gave birth to her young; and figuratively: الريح تنتج السحاب ("the wind brings forth the clouds"). Al-Rāʿī said:
أربّت بها شهري ربيع عليهم ... جنائب ينتجن الغمام المتاليا
(Two months of spring lingered over them with southerly winds that bring forth the successive clouds.)
And in the proverb: «إن العجز والتوائي تزاوجا فأنتجا الفقر» ("Incapacity and dawdling married and produced poverty"). And this premise yields no true conclusion if it has no praiseworthy outcome. نتح العرق من مناتحه: the sweat oozed from its pores, and رشح من مراشحه. تتخت الشوكة من رجلي بالمنتاخ, i.e. with the tweezers (المنقاش). نتخ البازي اللحم بمنسره: the hawk tore the meat with its beak. نتخ فلان من أصحابه: he withdrew from them. ونتخته المنية من بين قومه: death plucked him from among his people. نتر الثوب: he pulled it hard. نتر الوتر: he stretched the string until the bow almost broke. In the ḥadīth: «إذا بال أحدكم فلينتر ذكره ثلاث نترات» ("When one of you urinates, let him pull his member three times"). نتش الشوكة بالمنتاش, and ونقشها بالمنقاش: he extracted the thorn with tweezers. وما نتش منه شيئا: he took nothing from him; and هو ينتش من كل علم: he picks up something from every branch of knowledge. نتف شعره وانتتفه: he plucked his hair; and فلان منتوف: one fond of plucking his beard. Figuratively: أعطاه نتفة من الطعام وغيره: a little of it. The saying of the common people نتفة is correct, but with ḍamma on the mīm [sic]; and Abū ʿUbayda used to say of al-Aṣmaʿī: "That is a man of the nutfa." ونتن الشيء: its stench rose. In the ḥadīth: «إذا رأى أحدكم امرأة فأعجبته فليذكر مناتنها» ("When one of you sees a woman and she pleases him, let him remember her foul places"). This is among the subtleties of Arabic, so reflect on it.
[Translator's note: the source text of this paragraph is rendered as it stands; "ولكن بضم الميم" (with ḍamma on the mīm) and the Abū ʿUbayda remark appear as printed and do not seem consistent, since the word نتفة has no mīm.]
(ظُلَّةٌ): الظّلة with ḍamma on the ẓāʾ is everything that shades you, whether a roof or a cloud,
[Translator's note: the entry ends here in the source, breaking off mid-sentence.]

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ نَتَقْنَا الْجَبَلَ فَوْقَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُ ظُلَّةٌ): the واو is a conjunction; إذ is an adverb of time attached to an omitted «اذكر» conjoined to what preceded; the clause نتقنا is in the position of genitive by annexation; نا is the agent; الجبل is the direct object; فوقهم is an adverb of place attached to an omitted item as a ḥāl from الجبل, and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because at the time of the uprooting it was not actually above them, but became above them by the uprooting; or it is attached to نتقنا. The clause كأنه ظلة is also a ḥāl from الجبل, so the ḥāl is multiple. كأن with its noun and khabar.
(وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُ واقِعٌ بِهِمْ): it is possible that the clause is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause نتقنا, which is genitive by annexation; it is possible that the واو is circumstantial with an implied «قد», and an expression like this and the discussion of it have preceded - the owner of the ḥāl is الجبل, i.e. "as though it were a canopy while it was thought to be about to fall on them". You may also make the واو resumptive, in which case the clause is resumptive with no position. أن and what is in its scope fill the place of the two objects of ظنّ; أن with its noun and khabar; and بهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to واقع.
(خُذُوا ما آتَيْناكُمْ بِقُوَّةٍ): the clause خذوا is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech of an omitted saying, i.e. "and We said to them: take"; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; the clause آتيناكم has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; and بقوة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "resolved to bear its hardships and the multitude of its obligations".
(وَاذْكُرُوا ما فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ): conjoined to what preceded; لعلكم: لعل and its noun; the clause تتقون is its khabar; and the clause of hope is a ḥāl.
(وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ): conjoined to what preceded, and its mention has already come; ربك is the agent of أخذ; من بني آدم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخذ; and من ظهورهم is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of genitive, a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from بني آدم, or a badal of part from whole with the repetition of the preposition. The meaning of bringing out their offspring from their backs is bringing them out of their loins as progeny and making them bear witness against themselves. The discussion of that will come in the section on rhetoric. ذريتهم is the direct object.
(وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ): conjoined to أخذ, and على أنفسهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أشهدهم.
(أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ؟ قالُوا: بَلى): the clause is the quoted speech of an omitted saying, i.e. "saying"; and the clause of speech is a ḥāl; the hamza is for an affirmative interrogative; the تاء is the noun of ليس; the باء is a redundant preposition and ربكم is genitive in form, in the position of the khabar of ليس; the clause قالوا is resumptive; and بلى is a particle of response, which is specific to a negative and serves to refute it, whether the negative is bare or accompanied by an affirmative interrogative, as here. For that reason it was said: if they had said "نعم" they would have been disbelievers, because «نعم» is an affirmation of the reporter, whether in negation or affirmation, so it would be as if they acknowledged that He was not their Lord.
(شَهِدْنا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ: إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هذا غافِلِينَ): شهدنا is a verb and agent; أن and what is in its scope are in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "We did that lest you say"; يوم القيامة is an adverb attached to تقولوا; the clause of إن and what is in its scope is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech; the clause كنا is the khabar of إنا; غافلين is the khabar of كنا; and عن هذا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to غافلين.
(أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّما أَشْرَكَ آباؤُنا مِنْ قَبْلُ): أو تقولوا is conjoined to أن تقولوا, i.e. "and lest you say"; إنما is a particle that restricts and is restricted (kāffa wa-makfūfa); the clause إنما أشرك آباؤنا is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech; and من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ): the واو is a conjunction; كان and its noun; ذرية is its khabar; and من بعدهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of ذرية.
(أَفَتُهْلِكُنا بِما فَعَلَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ): the hamza is for an interrogative of denial; the فاء is a conjunction; تهلكنا is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; the باء is a preposition and expresses causality; ما is a maṣdar particle; فعل المبطلون is a verb and agent; and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by the باء.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «وإذ نتقنا الجبل فوقهم كأنه ظلة» there is a mursal simile (tashbīh mursal, a simile with its particle mentioned), and its benefit here is to bring what custom does not run to into what custom does run to.
2- In His saying «وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم» to the end of the verse, the later scholars of rhetoric agreed that there was no bringing out, no speech and no witnessing, and that all of this is to be taken as a representational figurative expression (majāz tamthīlī). For He, Glorified be He, likened the state of the human species after its actual existence, endowed with the attributes of obligation, in that the proofs of His lordship, Glorified be He, were set up - proofs which require that it speak and acknowledge accordingly - to the actual taking of the covenant from it by acknowledging what was mentioned. As for the earlier scholars, they say: He, the Exalted, brought some of them out of the loins of others, gave them intellect and speech, and inspired them with that. Each has his own point of view.

dervis-irab:149-151.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سُقِطَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ): The statements of the lexicographers are confused about the origin of this expression, which is used for regret and bewilderment. Abū Marwān the philologist said: The saying of the Arabs "سقط في يده" is among what has tired me out as to its meaning. Al-Wāḥidī said: It has become clear from the statements of the exegetes and the lexicographers that «سقط في يده» means "he regretted", and that it is used to describe the regretful; but as for its derivation and origin, I did not see anything from any of the imams of the language with which I am satisfied. Al-Zajjāj said: His saying, Exalted is He, «سقط في أيديهم» means "they regretted"; this expression was not heard before the Qur'an, and the Arabs did not know it in verse or prose, in the pre-Islamic period or in Islam. When they heard it, the manner of its use was hidden from them, because it had not struck their ears; so Abū Nuwās said: «في نشوة قد سقطت منها يدي» ("in a state of intoxication from which my hand has fallen") — though he was the consummate scholar — and he erred in using it. The words of al-Farrāʾ: Both سقط and أسقط are permissible; omitting the hamza is the more frequent and better; and سقط with fatḥa and active voice is a rare dialectal form. Al-Akhfash said: It has been read so among the irregular readings, as though he implied the regret, i.e. "regret fell into their hands". Al-Muṭarrizī said: «سقط في يده» is a proverb applied to the regretful and bewildered, and its meaning is "he regretted", because it is the way of one whose regret is intense that he bites his hand, so that his hand becomes something fallen upon, as though his mouth had fallen into it. So much; and you will see more discussion of this expression in the Rhetoric section.

* I'rab:
(وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ): The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to show their end after committing their offence. لما is a linking or temporal particle; سقط is passive; and في أيديهم stands in the place of the deputy agent, في meaning «على», i.e. "upon their hands". (وَرَأَوْا أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ ضَلُّوا): conjoined to سقط في أيديهم; أن and what is within its scope take the place of the two objects of رأوا, because it means "they knew"; the clause قد ضلوا is the khabar of أن. (قالُوا: لَئِنْ لَمْ يَرْحَمْنا رَبُّنا وَيَغْفِرْ لَنا): the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; the lām prepares for an oath; إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; يرحمنا is an imperfect verb jussive by لم, and نا is the direct object; ربنا is a delayed agent; ويغفر: the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause يغفر is conjoined to يرحمنا; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يغفر. (لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ): the lām is the answer to the oath; نكونن is an imperfect verb indeclinable on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no position, and the clause of the oath is in the position of accusative as the content of the saying; من الخاسرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of نكونن. (وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسى إِلى قَوْمِهِ غَضْبانَ أَسِفاً): The wāw is resumptive, or a conjunction; لما is a linking or temporal particle; the clause رجع موسى has no position, or is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; إلى قومه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to رجع; غضبان is the first ḥāl and أسفا the second ḥāl, from Moses. (قالَ بِئْسَما خَلَفْتُمُونِي مِنْ بَعْدِي): بئس is an inert past verb to form blame, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", obligatorily so here in particular; ما is an indefinite described noun in the position of accusative as a specification (tamyīz), the meaning being "succession"; the clause خلفتموني is an adjective of ما; the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "your succession"; and من بعدي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ): The hamza is for an interrogative of denial and rebuke; عجلتم, meaning "you outstripped", is a verb and agent; أمر ربكم is the direct object; and all of it is the completion of their saying. [Translator's note: the source says "their saying" (مقولهم) where the context suggests Moses' saying; the translation follows what is written.] (وَأَلْقَى الْأَلْواحَ وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُ إِلَيْهِ): The wāw is a conjunction; ألقى is conjoined to قال, and what is meant here is the overpowering of anger; أخذ is conjoined to ألقى; برأس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخذ; أخيه is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause يجره إليه is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun of Moses in أخذ, i.e. "he took him, dragging him to himself by his head". (قالَ ابْنَ أُمَّ): ابن أم are two nouns indeclinable on fatḥa because they are compounded in the manner of the numerals, like خمسة عشر, or of adverbs, like صباح مساء; on this view ابن is not annexed to أم but compounded with it, so their vowel is a vowel of indeclinability. The Kufans held that ابن is annexed to أمّ, and أم is annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, which was converted to alif as it is converted in a vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, then the alif was dropped and the fatḥa sufficed in its place, as the yāʾ suffices in place of the kasra; in that case the vowel of ابن is a vowel of declension, it is annexed to أم, and أم is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. In any case the vocative particle is omitted, i.e. «يا ابن أم». He confined his address to the mother, although he was his full brother, because mentioning the mother is more touching to his heart. (إِنَّ الْقَوْمَ اسْتَضْعَفُونِي وَكادُوا يَقْتُلُونَنِي): The clause stands as a reason for how they treated him. إن and its noun; the clause استضعفوني is its khabar; كادوا is conjoined to استضعفوني, the wāw being the noun of كاد, and the clause يقتلونني its khabar. (فَلا تُشْمِتْ بِيَ الْأَعْداءَ): The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, i.e. "if you know my excuse, do not gladden the enemies by what you do to me of the disagreeable"; بي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تشمت; الأعداء is the direct object. (وَلا تَجْعَلْنِي مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ): The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تجعلني is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; مع is an adverb of place attached to تجعلني; القوم is muḍāf ilayhi and الظالمين an adjective. (قالَ: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِأَخِي): The clause is resumptive, brought to ask forgiveness for himself and his brother; رب is a vocative from which the vocative particle is omitted; اغفر is a verb of supplication; لي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اغفر; ولأخي is conjoined to «لي».
