(وَأَدْخِلْنا فِي رَحْمَتِكَ وَأَنْتَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ): conjoined to اغفر; في رحمتك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أدخلنا; وأنت: the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; أنت is a mubtadaʾ; and أرحم الراحمين is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The kināya (metonymy) in His saying «سقط في أيديهم», for regret: it is customary that when a person regrets something he bites his fingers with his mouth, so the falling of mouths upon hands is a concomitant of regret; thus the name of the concomitant is used and the thing entailed is meant, by way of kināya. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ولما سقط في أيديهم»: when their regret and anguish at worshipping the calf became intense — for it is the way of one whose regret and anguish are intense that he bites his hand in grief, so his hand becomes something fallen upon, because his mouth has fallen into it."
Al-Quṭb said in his commentary on al-Kashshāf: On al-Zajjāj's explanation it is an allegorical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya), because he likened the state of regret in the heart to the state of a thing in the hand. It was said: on his explanation it is a metaphor of the implicit kind (istiʿāra bi-l-kināya) regarding regret, by likening it to what is seen with the eye.
[Translator's note: «وفيل» in the source is evidently «وقيل»; the translation follows the sense.]

dervis-irab:152-154.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ سَيَنالُهُمْ غَضَبٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَذِلَّةٌ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): Resumptive speech, brought to inform Moses of what will befall them after these successive grave sins. إن and its noun; the clause اتخذوا العجل has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; the clause سينالهم is the khabar of إن; غضب is the agent; من ربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of غضب; ذلة is conjoined to غضب; في الحياة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of ذلة; and الدنيا is an adjective of الحياة. (وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُفْتَرِينَ): That is, "We recompense them with the like of that recompense"; many parallels of it have preceded. (وَالَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا السَّيِّئاتِ ثُمَّ تابُوا مِنْ بَعْدِها وَآمَنُوا): conjoined to the preceding «الذين», or a mubtadaʾ; the clause عملوا السيئات is the ṣila; ثم تابوا is conjoined to عملوا; من بعدها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and آمنوا is conjoined to عملوا. (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِها لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): إن and its noun; من بعدها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); غفور is the first khabar of إنّ and رحيم the second khabar; and the whole clause is the khabar of «الذين». (وَلَمَّا سَكَتَ عَنْ مُوسَى الْغَضَبُ): The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to show the exaggeration; لما is a linking or temporal particle, and this has recurred many times; سكت الغضب is a verb and agent; عن موسى is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to سكت; the clause سكت has no position, or is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (أَخَذَ الْأَلْواحَ وَفِي نُسْخَتِها هُدىً وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ): The clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; the wāw is circumstantial; في نسختها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; هدى is a delayed mubtadaʾ; رحمة is conjoined to هدى; وللذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يرهبون is its khabar; لربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يرهبون. The lām entered to strengthen the direct object, because the delaying of the verb gives it weakness, like «للرؤيا تعبرون». Al-Kisāʾī said it is redundant. Al-Mubarrad said: it is attached to the verbal noun of the mentioned verb, the implied form being "for those whose fear is of their Lord they fear"; and the clause هم لربهم يرهبون is a ṣila.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ولما سكت عن موسى الغضب» there are two metaphors (istiʿāra):

1- An explicit derivative metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya):
By likening stillness (sukūn) to silence (sukūt). [Translator's note: the source writes it in this order; the translation follows what is written.]

2- An implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya):
In likening anger to a speaking person who incites Moses and says to him: "Say to your people such-and-such, and throw down the tablets, and take your brother by the head." Then the inciting stops and he leaves off speaking.

Other divisions of metaphor:
Metaphor has been discussed before, and we return here to say: this metaphor, which is the attributing of silence to anger, is a metaphor of an intelligible for an intelligible on the basis of sharing in an intelligible matter, and it is one of five kinds of metaphor. The borrowed term (mustaʿār) is silence, that for which it is borrowed (mustaʿār lahu) is anger, that from which it is borrowed (mustaʿār minhu) is the silent one, and the meaning is "when anger left Moses", because the reality of silence is the cessation of speech, and the reality of the cessation of anger is the absence of what indicates it, whether speech or otherwise, in that state. Moses' anger was known there only from his saying «بئسما خلفتموني من بعدي», for that speech was the prelude to throwing down the tablets; and when the speech indicating anger ceased, the metaphor of silence for anger was fine. It does not follow from the silence of anger that contentment had been attained, for Moses was not content with their disobedience nor with their remaining in disobedience until repentance took place; for this reason He, glorified is He, reported of him the silence of anger without the attainment of contentment. This metaphor is the most delicate of the five metaphors, because it is the metaphor of an intelligible for an intelligible on the basis of sharing in an intelligible matter.

The other four divisions:
As for the other four divisions, they are:
2- The metaphor of the sensible for the sensible on the basis of sharing in an intelligible matter, which is the metaphor composed of the dense and the subtle. An example is His saying, Exalted is He: «إذ أرسلنا عليهم الريح العقيم». That for which it is borrowed is the wind; that from which it is borrowed is the one that bears offspring; the borrowed term is "barren" (ʿaqīm), which is the absence of offspring; and the sharing between that for which it is borrowed and that from which it is borrowed is in the absence of offspring, which is something intelligible.
3- The metaphor of the sensible for the intelligible, which is more delicate than the composite one. An example is His saying, Exalted is He: «بل نقذف بالحقّ على الباطل فيدمغه فإذا هو زاهق». Hurling (qadhf) and pushing are borrowed terms, and they are sensible, while truth and falsehood are what they are borrowed for, and they are intelligible. Like it is His saying, Exalted is He: «ضربت عليهم الذلة أين ما ثقفوا إلا بحبل من الله وحبل من الناس». The borrowed term is the rope, which is sensible, and that for which it is borrowed is the covenant, which is intelligible; the sharing between them is in connection, because the covenant connects the covenanter and the one who submits, as the rope connects the two bound together, and that is something sensible. Of this division is His saying, Exalted is He: «فاصدع بما تؤمر». That from which it is borrowed is the glass vessel; the borrowed term is splitting (ṣadʿ), which is cleaving; and that for which it is borrowed is the undutifulness of the legally responsible. The meaning is: declare plainly everything that has been revealed to you, and make clear all that you were commanded to make clear, even if that is hard on some hearts so that they split. The resemblance between them lies in what the splitting does to hearts, so that its effect shows on the surface of the faces, in contraction and expansion, and the signs of denial and rejoicing appear on them, just as that appears on the surface of a cracked glass vessel from the hammering inside it. It is related that when a certain Bedouin heard these three words he prostrated, and it was said to him: Why did you prostrate? He said: I prostrated for the eloquence of this speech.
4- The metaphor of the intelligible for the sensible on the basis of sharing in an intelligible matter. An example is His saying, Exalted is He: «إنا لماطغى الماء حملناكم في الجارية». That for which it is borrowed is the abundance of water, which is sensory; that from which it is borrowed is arrogance (takabbur), which is rational; and the common ground is excessive elevation, which is also rational. Further discussions of metaphor will come in their place in this book.
[Translator's note: the source prints «لماطغى» joined; the verse reads «لَمَّا طَغَى». Also, the numbering in the source runs 1-2 then 2-3-4 as printed above, and the phrase «عقوق المكلفين» is translated as written.]

dervis-irab:174-177.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَخْلَدَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ): الإخلاد إلى الشيء is inclining toward a thing out of feeling secure in it.
In al-Miṣbāḥ: خلد بالمكان خلودا, of the pattern قعد, means "he stayed"; أخلد with an alif is the same; and خلد إلى كذا and أخلد إليه mean "he relied upon it".
(يَلْهَثْ): he lolls out his tongue. One says لهث يلهث, with fatḥa on the ʿayn in both the past and the imperfect, لهثا and لهاثا; it is the sticking out of his tongue in a state of rest and of exhaustion, and it is an inherent nature of the dog, whereas other animals do not pant except when they are exhausted or thirsty. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: لهث الكلب when it sticks out its tongue from fatigue or thirst. As for His saying, the Exalted: «إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث»: when you charge at a dog it barks and turns to flee, and if you leave it alone it rushes at you and barks, so it tires itself in both cases, and then there befalls it what befalls it in thirst, the sticking out of the tongue.

* I'rab:
(وَكَذلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ): the واو is a conjunction; the كاف and what it enters is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and many parallels of it have preceded; الآيات is a direct object; ولعلهم: the واو is conjoined to an omitted item, its implied form being "so that they may reflect on them"; لعل and its noun; the clause يرجعون is its khabar; and the clause of hope is a ḥāl.
(وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ الَّذِي آتَيْناهُ آياتِنا فَانْسَلَخَ مِنْها): the واو is conjoined to what «إذ» in His saying «وإذ أخذ» is attached to; اتل is an imperative verb, its agent latent, the implied form being "you"; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «اتل»; نبأ is a direct object; الذي is a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause آتيناه is the ṣila of the relative; آياتنا is the second direct object; فانسلخ is conjoined to آتيناه; and منها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to انسلخ.
(فَأَتْبَعَهُ الشَّيْطانُ فَكانَ مِنَ الْغاوِينَ): أتبع is a quadriliteral past verb that governs one object, in which case it means "he overtook him", and it governs two objects, in which case the هاء is the first direct object and the second direct object is omitted, its implied form being "Satan made him follow his footsteps", i.e. he made him a follower of them; الشيطان is the agent; فكان is conjoined to أتبعه, and its noun is latent; and من الغاوين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of it.
(وَلَوْ شِئْنا لَرَفَعْناهُ بِها): the واو is circumstantial; لو is a non-jussive conditional; شئنا is a verb and agent [the source has «وشيئا», which is a misprint for «وشئنا»]; the lām is the apodosis of لو; the clause رفعناه has no position; and بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to رفعناه.
(وَلكِنَّهُ أَخْلَدَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ): the واو is a conjunction; لكن and its noun; the clause أخلد is the khabar of لكن; and إلى الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخلد.
(وَاتَّبَعَ هَواهُ): conjoined to أخلد, and هواه is a direct object.
(فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ الْكَلْبِ إِنْ تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْهِ يَلْهَثْ أَوْ تَتْرُكْهُ يَلْهَثْ): the فاء is the fāṣiḥa; مثله is a mubtadaʾ and كمثل الكلب its khabar; إن is conditional; تحمل is the protasis; عليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تحمل; يلهث is the apodosis; أو is a conjunction; and تتركه is conjoined to the protasis and apodosis that preceded. More will be said about the position of the conditional clause, because of the length of the discussion, in the section on benefits.
(ذلِكَ مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and مثل القوم its khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl; الذين is an adjective of القوم; the clause كذبوا has no position because it is a ṣila; and بآياتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كذبوا.
(فَاقْصُصِ الْقَصَصَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ): the فاء is the fāṣiḥa, i.e. "if you have established that the mentioned parable is the parable of these deniers, then relate it to them"; اقصص is an imperative verb, its agent latent, the implied form being "you"; القصص, in the sense of "that which is related", is a direct object; and the clause of hope is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the addressed pronoun in «اقصص», the meaning being "hoping for their reflection".
(ساءَ مَثَلًا الْقَوْمُ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا): ساء is a past, non-inflecting verb for expressing blame; مثلا is a tamyīz; القوم is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause ساء; it is necessary to imply an omitted item so that the tamyīz, the agent and the one specified for blame are all identical in meaning, the implied form being "evil is the parable of the people" or "evil are the possessors of the parable of the people"; الذين is an adjective of القوم; and the clause كذبوا بآياتنا is a ṣila. More will be said on this verse in the section on rhetoric.
(وَأَنْفُسَهُمْ كانُوا يَظْلِمُونَ): the واو is a conjunction; أنفسهم is a fronted direct object of يظلمون; كان and its noun; and the clause يظلمون is its khabar. It is also possible that what follows the conjunctive واو enters into the ṣila, conjoined to كذبوا, meaning "those who combined denying the signs with wronging themselves", or that it is cut off from it, meaning "they wronged only themselves by the denial".

* Rhetoric:
In these verses are arts of rhetoric that we summarize as follows: and al-Jāḥiẓ named it:
[Translator's note: the clause «وقد سماه الجاحظ:» ("and al-Jāḥiẓ named it:") is left hanging in the source, with no name following; it is translated as it stands.]

1- The theological method (al-madhhab al-kalāmī):
This name is as Ibn al-Muʿtazz mentioned in his book, and al-Jāḥiẓ claimed that nothing of it is found in the Qur'an, whereas the Noble Book is full of it. The definition of this chapter is that it is the speaker's argument for what he wants to establish with a proof that cuts off the obstinate and blunts the weapon of the stubborn disputant, in the manner of the theologians. Among it is the logical kind, in which conclusions are drawn from true premises. The verse intended by this art is His saying, the Exalted: «ولو شئنا لرفعناه بها ولكنه أخلد إلى الأرض واتبع هواه». The arrangement of the two premises in these words and the conclusion is that we say: what Allah wills is, and what He does not will is not; and had Allah willed, He would have raised Balʿam ibn Bāʿūrāʾ, who is the one intended by this verse. Allah had sent him to the king of Madyan to call him to faith, but he gave him gifts and land grants, so he followed his religion and abandoned the religion of Moses; in him this verse and what follows were revealed.
Further, the one intended for praise or blame must be only of the same kind as the one raised by نعم and بئس. So if a speech is found whose apparent sense contradicts this rule, let it be known that there is an omitted item whose mention returns the speech to this established principle. An example is His saying, Glorified be He: «ساء مثلا القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا»: the people are not of the same kind as the parable, so the implied form is "evil is the parable of the people", and the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place; and on this one reasons by analogy.

2- The representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī):
In His saying «واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه» to the end of the verse, He likened the state of one who was given something and did not accept it to the dog that, if you charge at it, barks and turns away, and if you leave it, rushes at you and barks, since the dog gives earnestness and effort from itself in every state. He likened his rejecting the signs, casting them away and returning them after having been eager for them and extremely desirous of them, to the dog when it returns barking after you have driven it off; and it must be that rejecting precious and valuable things comes after seeking them and being eager for them. And the dog, when it tires itself with intense barking, approaching you and turning from you, pants, and there befalls it what befalls it at fatigue and thirst.
[Translator's note: the phrase «في خدن طلبها» appears in the source as printed and is rendered here by its sense ("after seeking them"); the wording seems corrupt.]

* Benefits:
The conditional clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "panting in both cases". Al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. One of them said: "As for the conditional, it does not occur in its entirety in the place of a ḥāl, so one does not say جاء زيد إن يسأل يعط as a ḥāl; rather, if that were wanted, the conditional would be made a khabar of a pronoun of that which the ḥāl is about, as in جاء زيد هو وإن يسأل يعط, so that what occurs in the place of the ḥāl is [the whole], but only after they have taken it out of the reality of the condition. That clause is either followed by a conjoined clause that contradicts it, or it is not. In the first case, omission of the واو is constant, as in أتيتك إن أتيتني وإن لم تأتني, since it is not hidden that two contradictory conditions in such a place do not remain with the meaning of condition but turn into the meaning of equalization, like the two contradictory interrogatives in His saying «أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم». As for the second case, the واو is necessary in it, as in أتيتك وإن لم تأتني, and if the واو were omitted it would be confused with a true condition. His saying «إن تحمل عليه يهلث أو تتركه يلهث» is of the first kind, because charging at it and leaving it are contradictory. This is among the most subtle of topics, so ponder it, for it is worthy of pondering."
[Translator's note: the source has «يهلث», a misprint for «يلهث».]

dervis-irab:178-179.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ذَرَأْنا): We created.

* I'rab:
(مَنْ يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِي): من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of accusative as a fronted direct object of يهد; الله is its agent; the فاء is the connective of the apodosis; هو is a mubtadaʾ and المهتدي its khabar. Here he took into account the form of «من», so he made المهتدي singular.
(وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ): conjoined to the preceding clause; here he took into account the meaning of «من», so he made الخاسرين plural.
(وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنا لِجَهَنَّمَ كَثِيراً مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ): the واو is a conjunction, so that the speech of Allah, the Exalted, runs in harmony in describing them and describing their destination. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; ذرأنا is a verb and agent; لجهنم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ذرأنا; كثيرا is a direct object; and من الجن والإنس is an adjective of «كثيرا».
(لَهُمْ قُلُوبٌ لا يَفْقَهُونَ بِها وَلَهُمْ أَعْيُنٌ لا يُبْصِرُونَ بِها وَلَهُمْ آذانٌ لا يَسْمَعُونَ بِها): لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; قلوب is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is a ḥāl from «كثيرا», even though it is indefinite, because it has been specified by the adjective; and the clause لا يفقهون is an adjective of قلوب. The same is said of the two following clauses.
(أُولئِكَ كَالْأَنْعامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ، أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْغافِلُونَ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; كالأنعام is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; بل is a particle of disregard and conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ and أضل its khabar; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation with no position; and الغافلون is the khabar of أولئك; or «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and الغافلون the khabar of «هم», and the clause هم الغافلون is the khabar of أولئك.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse is the representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī). He likened the Jews, in the enormity of what they set about of denying the Messenger of Allah ﷺ although they knew that he was the promised Prophet, to those who lack understanding hearts, seeing eyes and listening ears; and, because of their immersion in disbelief and their persistence in error, He made them as those created for the Fire, who never leave it. Then He likened them to cattle, indeed to something lower than cattle in reversal, foolishness and descent into the pits of vice and sin.
